wikis.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-5
wikis.summary: OpenAI's August 7, 2025 launch post for GPT-5, a unified system with a router and thinking model, plus benchmarks, safety changes and availability.
wikis.body:
- Dated August 7, 2025. GPT-5 is a unified system: a smart, efficient model, a deeper reasoning model (GPT-5 thinking), and a real-time router choosing between them. Once limits are reached a mini version handles queries.
- New default in ChatGPT, replacing GPT-4o, o3, o4-mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.5 for signed-in users. Rolling out to Plus, Pro, Team and Free users "today"; Enterprise and Edu "next week". Pro gets unlimited use and **GPT-5 pro** (replacing o3-pro); free users fall back to GPT-5 mini. Usable in Codex CLI for Pro, Plus, Team.
- Benchmarks: 94.6% AIME 2025 (no tools), 74.9% SWE-bench Verified, 88% Aider Polyglot, 84.2% MMMU, 46.2% HealthBench Hard; GPT-5 pro 88.4% GPQA.
- Efficiency: GPT-5 thinking beats o3 with 50-80% fewer output tokens.
- Reliability: ~45% fewer factual errors than GPT-4o (with web search); ~80% fewer than o3 when thinking; deception rate on production reasoning traffic 4.8% (o3) to 2.1%. o3 answered confidently about non-existent images 86.7% vs 9% for GPT-5.
- Sycophancy cut from 14.5% to under 6% on targeted evals. New "safe completions" safety training. "GPT-5 thinking" treated as High capability in biological and chemical domain with safeguards (5,000 hours of red-teaming).
- Four preset personalities (Cynic, Robot, Listener, Nerd) in research preview.
- GPT-5 pro: experts preferred it over GPT-5 thinking 67.8% of the time; 22% fewer major errors. Trained on Microsoft Azure AI supercomputers.

- Manga by Rumiko Takahashi, serialized in Shogakukan's Weekly Shonen Sunday since May 8, 2019 (announced December 2018); first volume September 18, 2019; 30 volumes as of August 18, 2026. English: Viz Media (licensed February 2021; vol. 1 September 14, 2021; simultaneous digital release on Viz Manga from May 9, 2023). Genres adventure, dark fantasy, supernatural.
- Plot: eight years after surviving a fatal accident at Gogyo Shopping Center, Nanoka Kiba is transported from an abandoned shop passage to the Taisho era, where she meets Mao, and they investigate strange events.
- Main characters: Mao (onmyoji, cursed by the byoki, wields Hagunsei; English voice Howard Wang); Nanoka Kiba (Natsumi Kawaida; English Anjali Kunapaneni), 15, cursed by byoki, wields Akanemaru; Otoya (shikigami assistant); Byoki (cat demon, Takashi Matsuyama; Patrick Seitz).
- Heian-era Goko clan: Master, Hyakka (fire), Kamon (wood), Masago (water), Shiranui (water, runs the new Goko clan), Hakubi (metal), Daigo (earth), Natsuno (earth), Sana, Yurako (Sana's twin sister). Taisho-era members include Soma Kagami, Kagari Hosho, Renji, Mei Mitazono, Sasuga.
- Anime: announced July 2025; Sunrise; director Teruo Sato, series composition Yuko Kakihara, character design Yoshihito Hishinuma, music Shu Kanematsu. Premiered April 4, 2026 on NHK General TV; infobox 24 episodes. Ep 1 "Nanoka and Mao" (April 4, 2026), ep 11 "Blood Bond" (June 13, 2026).
- Themes: OP1 "Heartloud" Kis-My-Ft2; ED1 "Juai" True; OP2 "Bokura ga Uwagaki suru Sekai" 20th Century; ED2 "Tayutau" Reina Ueda.
- Licensing: Viz Media (Hulu in the US; Disney+ in Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Latin America); Medialink for South/Southeast Asia. English dub by Bang Zoom! Studios premiered with the first cours on August 24, 2026; second cours "set to premiere in November of the same year".
- Reception: 1 million copies in circulation by July 2021; Brutus "Most Dangerous Manga" list (December 2019); School Library Journal top 10 manga of 2021 (vol. 1); ANN's Rebecca Silverman gave vol. 1 a B-, noting reused elements; ICv2 said "closest to Inuyasha in style"; anime nominated at the 6th Astra TV Awards, Best Anime Series (2026).

wikis.title: OpenAI debuts GPT-4o 'omni' model
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, May 13 2024: OpenAI announces GPT-4o, a multimodal flagship model powering ChatGPT, with a new desktop app and free-tier features.
wikis.body:
- Published May 13, 2024. GPT-4o ("omni") handles text, speech and video; rolling out "iteratively" over the next few weeks. CTO Mira Murati: "GPT-4o reasons across voice, text and vision."
- ChatGPT voice becomes real-time, can be interrupted, picks up on vocal nuance; improved vision (photos, desktop screen). Better in around 50 languages.
- API/Azure: twice as fast, half the price and higher rate limits than GPT-4 Turbo. Audio in the API first to "a small group of trusted partners" in coming weeks.
- Free tier gets GPT-4o today; Plus and Team get "5x higher" message limits. New ChatGPT voice in alpha for Plus in about a month.
- Also: refreshed web UI, macOS desktop app (Plus first, Windows later in the year), GPT Store opened to free users, and memory, file/photo upload and web search for free users.

wikis.title: OpenAI explains why ChatGPT became too sycophantic
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, April 29 2025, on OpenAI's postmortem of the GPT-4o update that made ChatGPT overly agreeable and was rolled back.
wikis.body:
- Published April 29, 2025. OpenAI published a postmortem on sycophancy in GPT-4o after rolling back an update released the previous week.
- Users noticed the over-validating behavior over the weekend; Sam Altman acknowledged it Sunday and two days later announced the rollback.
- OpenAI said the update, meant to make the default personality "feel more intuitive and effective", was informed too much by "short-term feedback" and "did not fully account for how users' interactions with ChatGPT evolve over time."
- Fixes: refine training and system prompts, add guardrails for "honesty and transparency", expand evaluations, let users give "real-time feedback" and choose multiple personalities, and explore "broader, democratic feedback".

wikis.title: GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 Pro release announcement
wikis.summary: OpenAI developer community announcement of GPT-5.4 (Thinking) and GPT-5.4 Pro across ChatGPT, the API and Codex, with benchmark figures.
wikis.body:
- Announced in the OpenAI Developer Community; thread activity dated Mar 5 (year not shown).
- GPT-5.4 releases in ChatGPT (as GPT-5.4 Thinking), the API and Codex; GPT-5.4 Pro in ChatGPT and the API. Rolling out gradually in ChatGPT and Codex; API names gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-pro.
- Up to 1M tokens context in Codex and the API (opt-in via model_context_window and model_auto_compact_token_limit; default window 272K per a companion post).
- Native computer use: OSWorld-Verified 75.0%. GDPval: matches or exceeds professionals in 83.0% of comparisons (GPT-5.2: 70.9%). Internal spreadsheet benchmark 87.3% vs 68.4%. Tool search cut token usage 47% across 250 MCP Atlas tasks at the same accuracy. Codex /fast mode up to 1.5x faster.

wikis.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 series: Sol, Terra and Luna
wikis.summary: OpenAI developer community announcement of the GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna models, generally available July 9, 2026.
wikis.body:
- Update (Jul 7): GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna generally available starting Thursday, July 9 2026, 10am PT. The thread was first posted as a preview (Jun 26).
- Sol: newest flagship for frontier reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Terra: balanced everyday model with GPT-5.5-competitive performance at 2x lower cost. Luna: fastest, most affordable.
- Sol sets a new SOTA on Terminal-Bench 2.1; on ExploitBench uses roughly one-third of the output tokens of another leading system; SecureBio scores 53.5% Virology Capabilities Test, 60.0% Molecular Biology, 68.4% Human Pathogen Capabilities, 68.3% World-Class Bio (about 9 points above GPT-5.5).
- New "max" reasoning effort and "ultra mode" using subagents. During the preview, access was for select trusted partners via API and Codex.

wikis.title: OpenAI launches Canvas interface in ChatGPT
wikis.summary: TechCrunch on OpenAI's October 2024 canvas, a side workspace in ChatGPT for writing and coding projects.
wikis.body:
- Published around Oct 3, 2024 (Thursday launch). Canvas opens a separate window beside chat for writing and coding; users highlight sections for the model to edit.
- Beta for ChatGPT Plus and Teams on Thursday, Enterprise and Edu next week; free users planned once out of beta.
- Select "GPT-4o with canvas" or write "use canvas"; it may open automatically for longer outputs.
- Writing: length slider, tone edits, translate. Coding: "add comments", "review code" button with approve/decline. Compared with Anthropic's Artifacts and Cursor. PM Daniel Levine: "a more natural interface for collaborating with ChatGPT".

wikis.title: ChatGPT Tasks: scheduled tasks and reminders (beta)
wikis.summary: SiliconANGLE, January 2025, on ChatGPT's new Tasks beta for reminders and recurring requests.
wikis.body:
- Published around Jan 14, 2025. Tasks launching in beta for ChatGPT Plus, Team and Pro users; no official OpenAI announcement at the time, reports per VentureBeat and TechCrunch.
- Set reminders (e.g. passport expiry in six months) with push notifications, and recurring requests (weekend plan each Friday, daily 7 a.m. news briefing).
- Accessed via "4o with scheduled tasks" in the model menu; manageable via chat or a tasks manager tab. ChatGPT may suggest tasks. It will not run continuous searches nor make purchases.
- Described as an early foray into AI agents; OpenAI reportedly preparing "Operator" (Bloomberg said possibly within weeks).

wikis.title: Doraemon (2005 TV series)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2005 Doraemon anime by Shin-Ei Animation and TV Asahi: production, voice recast, English dubs, episode counts, themes and films.
wikis.body:
- Japanese sci-fi comedy anime based on Fujiko F. Fujio's manga; third adaptation after the 1973 and 1979 anime. Produced by Shin-Ei Animation, TV Asahi and ADK Emotions; premiered April 15, 2005 (one-hour special) on TV Asahi/ANN and airs in over fifty countries. Called the "Mizuta Edition" in Asia after Wasabi Mizuta, Doraemon's voice.
- Scale: infobox says 22 seasons, 915 episodes (1,750+ segments), 20-26 min; text says 892 episodes, 45 feature films and a 46th set for spring 2027.
- Premise: Doraemon, a cat-like robot from the 22nd century, is sent to Tokyo to help 10-year-old Nobita Nobi. Others: Shizuka Minamoto, Suneo Honekawa, Takeshi "Gian" Goda.
- Japanese cast: Wasabi Mizuta (Doraemon), Megumi Ohara (Nobita), Yumi Kakazu (Shizuka), Tomokazu Seki (Suneo), Subaru Kimura (Gian). Directors: Soichiro Zen 2005-2017, Shinnosuke Yakuwa 2017-2018, Hirofumi Ogura 2020-present. Music Kan Sawada.
- Production: revival development began 2004 for the 1979 anime's 25th anniversary; trailer first shown March 25, 2005. The five-actor recast (announced March 13, 2005) was chosen from 590 applicants after Nobuyo Oyama, 1979 Doraemon voice, wished to step down. Kimura was 14 when cast. Look overhauled with more vivid colours from July 28, 2017. Aired Fridays 7:00 pm until September 29, 2017; since October 5, 2019 Saturdays 5:00 pm. Recorded at APU Meguro Studio.
- Changes from manga: episodes extended for better conclusions; medicine-like gadgets changed; Nobita's dad rarely smokes.
- English dubs: Bang Zoom!/Viz Media "Doraemon: Gadget Cat from the Future" on Disney XD, July 7, 2014 to September 1, 2015 (2 seasons, 52 episodes), heavily localized; Red Angel Media (Hong Kong, LUK International) on Boomerang UK from August 2015 to January 2016 (about 26 episodes); EarCandy (South Africa, Spacetoon India) on Disney Channel India from February 4, 2020, Disney Channel HD August 14, 2023 to May 10, 2025, three actors; fourth dub by Cake Entertainment announced June 2026, no release date given.
- Episodes per year (examples): 2005 32; 2020 52; 2023 48; 2024 47; 2025 49; 2026 TBA (from January 10, 2026).
- Openings: eight in Japanese; "Doraemon no Uta" (12 Girls Band) from April 15, 2005, "Hagushichao" (Rimi Natsukawa) from October 28, 2005, "Yume wo Kanaete Doraemon" (Mao) from May 11, 2007; as of November 2024 the current opening is "Yume wo Kanaete Doraemon" again.
- Mini corners: Doraemon Mini Theater (April-July 2005), Dora Dora Mini Theater (October-December 2022). Tribute: after Nobuyo Oyama died on September 29, 2024, a rerun episode was replaced by a montage of 1979 clips.
- Films listed include Nobita's Art World Tales (2025), New Nobita and the Castle of the Undersea Devil (2026), Nobita's Steam-Powered Time Machine (2027).

wikis.title: Kaiju No. 8: synopsis, production, media, anime and reception
wikis.summary: Article body on Naoya Matsumoto's manga Kaiju No. 8, its spin-offs, Production I.G anime seasons and sales.
wikis.body:
- Web manga by Naoya Matsumoto (English also "Monster #8"), Shueisha Shonen Jump+, July 3, 2020 to July 18, 2025 (129th chapter); 16 volumes, first December 4, 2020, last September 4, 2025. Viz Media English digital from August 2, 2020, print from December 7, 2021 (licensed February 19, 2021); Manga Plus from July 22, 2020. Over 20 million copies in circulation by September 2026.
- Story: kaiju attack Japan; Kafka Hibino swallows a parasitic creature and can become a kaiju ("Kaiju No. 8") while joining the Japanese Anti-Kaiju Defense Force to keep a promise to childhood friend Mina Ashiro (Third Division captain). Allies: Reno Ichikawa, Kikoru Shinomiya; First Division captain Gen Narumi; vice-captain Soshiro Hoshina. Antagonist Kaiju No. 9, later the Meireki entity; Kafka helps defeat it and is later allowed to use his kaiju form when necessary.
- Production: outline pitched near end of 2018; influenced by Ultraman (esp. Ultraseven), Shin Godzilla, Pacific Rim; Kaiju No. 8's design modelled on oni.
- Spin-offs: light novel "Exclusive on the Third Division" (Keiji Ando, November 4, 2022); "B-Side" manga (January 5 to July 12, 2024, 2 volumes); "Kaiju No. 8 Relax" (from June 4, 2024, Saikyo Jump); Jump Toon vertical edition from September 1, 2025; a video game.
- Anime: announced August 4, 2022; Production I.G, Studio Khara supervised kaiju designs; directors Shigeyuki Miya and Tomomi Kamiya; scripts Ichiro Okouchi; music Yuta Bandoh. Season 1 April 13 to June 29, 2024 on TV Tokyo; season 2 July 19 to September 27, 2025; compilation film plus "Hoshina's Day Off" from March 28, 2025 (released abroad as "Kaiju No. 8: Mission Recon"); Crunchyroll streams; Medialink for Southeast Asia. Shorts "Minute! Kaiju No. 8" from December 6, 2024.
- December 2025: a "conclusion arc" and short "Narumi's Week at Work" announced; the short premiered on September 5, 2026 and "will run for four episodes".
- Reception: 100 million views by April 2021, 400 million by February 2023; won the 2021 Next Manga Award (web) and was nominated for a 2022 Eisner Award; School Library Journal top 10 manga of 2021; Kono Manga ga Sugoi! 2022 third place. Vol. 1 first week 90,831 copies in Japan.

wikis.summary: Article body on Kureha's light novel series The Ogre's Bride (Oni no Hanayome) and its manga, live-action film and Colored Pencil Animation Japan anime.
wikis.body:
- Light novel series by Kureha, illustrated by Yu Shiroya; web novel on Novema from 2019; Starts Publishing (Starts Shuppan Bunko) from October 28, 2020; 9 volumes (vol. 9 May 24, 2024). Genre romantic fantasy.
- Manga: illustrated by Jun Togashi, noicomi, from December 24, 2021; 10 volumes as of July 2026 (vol. 10 July 10, 2026); English on NTT Solmare's MangaPlaza. Won the grand prize at NTT Solmare's Digital Comic Awards in 2023 and ranked third for the Tsutaya Comic Award in 2023.
- Reading play at Hamagin Hall Viamare, November 18-19, 2023. A source cited says the novel and comic series passed 1.5 million copies in total.
- Live-action film: announced December 3, 2025; Shochiku; director Chihiro Ikeda; screenplay Manato Hamada; premiered March 27, 2026 in Japan; 122 minutes; Ren Nagase as Reiya, Ai Yoshikawa as Yuzu.
- Synopsis: in a world where ayakashi (Japanese demons) and humans coexist, Yuzu Shinonome is neglected by her parents, who dote on her sister Karin, chosen bride of fox spirit Yota Kogetsu. After a quarrel Yota burns Yuzu's hands; she meets Reiya Kiryuuin, next head of the highest-ranking ayakashi clan, who says "I've missed you, my bride."

wikis.title: Beyblade X (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Beyblade X, the fourth-generation Beyblade toyline with a CoroCoro Comic manga, OLM anime, video games, characters and season schedule.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese manga, anime and toyline based on Takara Tomy and ADK Emotions' Beyblade franchise; the fourth generation of the franchise.
- Toyline launched July 15, 2023; manga serialized in Shogakukan's CoroCoro Comic since May 15, 2023 (9 volumes); anime by OLM premiered on TV Tokyo and affiliates October 6, 2023.
- ADK Emotions NY, Inc. and T-Licensing released the anime in English in 2024.

## Plot
Amateur Blader Robin Kazami (Bird Kazami in Japanese) is ditched by his friends after a crushing defeat. A chance encounter with former champion Jaxon Cross leads to a team-up; Jaxon intends to climb back to the top of The X as "Blader X" and challenge champion Khrome Ryugu. With influencer Multi Nana-iro, they form Team Persona and aim to go pro.

## Manga
- Written by Homura Kawamoto and Hikaru Muno, illustrated by Posuka Demizu; Viz Media announced an English licence in May 2024 (vol. 1 January 14, 2025); Shogakukan Asia publishes an English version in Singapore.

## Anime
- Announced May 14, 2023; OLM Team Masuda; directed by Moto Terada, Dai Fukuyama from episode 101, Katsuhito Akiyama supervising to episode 100; 134 episodes as of September 18, 2026.
- Season 1 OP "Prove" by One Ok Rock, ED "Zoom Zoom" by Aespa. Season 2 announced September 13, 2024, began October 18, 2024 (OP "You Gotta Run" by L'Arc-en-Ciel; ED "Cosmic Treat" by Perfume; later OP "Rise" by Tomorrow X Together, ED "Stay Gold" by Ado and Jax Jones). Season 3 announced September 12, 2025, began October 24, 2025 (OP "Invincible" by i-dle, ED "Vortex" by imase).
- After episode 122 the series left TV Tokyo and moved to the Beyblade YouTube channel on April 17, 2026 with a two-episode premiere, then a biweekly schedule. "A fourth season will premiere on October 9, 2026."
- English dub of season 1 premiered at Anime Expo on July 6, 2024, on Disney XD, DisneyNow and Hulu in the US July 13, 2024; season 2 dub premiered July 26, 2025.

## Video games
- BEYBLADE X XONE (GrooveBoxJapan/FuRyu; Switch, Windows), November 14, 2024; BEYBLADE X EVOBATTLE, November 13, 2025.

## Main characters (Japanese / English voice)
Jaxon Cross (Soma Saito / AJ Beckles), Robin Kazami (Shuichiro Umeda / Caleb Yen), Multi Nana-iro (Ruriko Noguchi / Anairis Quinones), Tenka Shiroboshi (Yuko Natsuyoshi / Justine Lee), Nine Cross; many teams (Pendragon, Phalanx, Zooganic, Yggdrasil, Gordius, Zodiac, Misleaders) are listed.

Utena Hiiragi, an introverted girl who admires the magical-girl trio Tres Magia, is given powers by the mascot Venalita but becomes an evil general of the Enormita organization (as Magia Baiser). She discovers a sadistic side and revels in torturing her idols.

wikis.title: Age of Empires 4 announced at Gamescom (HEXUS)
wikis.summary: HEXUS reports Microsoft announced Age of Empires 4 (PC only, Relic and Microsoft Studios) at Gamescom 2017, plus Age of Empires: Definitive Edition on 19 October.
wikis.body:
- By David Ross, 22 August 2017.
- Microsoft announced Age of Empires 4 at Gamescom 2017 in Cologne; PC exclusive, led by Relic Entertainment with Microsoft Studios. The trailer had been watched over two million times in 14 hours. Little information given; Relic's blog says it wants to "fuse historical context with deep strategic gameplay" and will share details "in the months to come". Release is "still quite a long way away".
- Age of Empires: Definitive Edition, a remake marking the game's 20th anniversary, is set for 19 October (2017). Features: all-new 4K graphics, re-orchestrated soundtrack, new zoom levels, Attack Move, unit queuing, 250-300 population cap, rally points, grid default key layout, select idle military/villagers, right-click mouse scroll.
- Definitive Editions of Age of Empires II and III were confirmed in the works; Forgotten Empires is the developer of all three. Microsoft produced a 'History of the Age of Empires' mini-documentary.

wikis.title: Age of Empires IV announced at Gamescom 2017
wikis.summary: Gamesplanet news post on Microsoft announcing Age of Empires IV (by Relic Entertainment) and Definitive Editions of earlier games at Gamescom 2017.
wikis.body:
- Dated 22 August, 2017 (Gamesplanet news, by CraigB).
- During Gamescom, Microsoft announced a brand new Age of Empires on PC: Age of Empires IV, being created by Relic Entertainment, the RTS team behind Dawn of War.
- No release date and few concrete details yet. A short trailer teased Native Americans, British Redcoats, Roman legionnaires, Japanese samurai and other factions, which "may or may not be present in the final game".
- Relic blog quote: "We can't wait to tap into our strengths as a studio to fuse historical context with deep strategic gameplay, and to bring this franchise back to the forefront of gaming".
- A new trailer for Age of Empires Remastered Definitive Edition was shown; 2017 marks the franchise's 20th anniversary.
- Definitive Edition features listed: Attack Move, 250-300 population cap, Rally Points (basic and contextual/intelligent villagers), grid default key layout, Select Idle Military, Select Idle Villagers, unit queueing, right-click mouse scroll.
- Age of Empires Remastered is coming to PC on October 19th; an insider Beta signup opened that day via the Age of Empires site.
- Definitive Editions of Age of Empires 2 and Age of Empires 3 are also reported to follow in the future.

wikis.title: Rumored 2017 Google Pixel XL with squeezable frame
wikis.summary: MacRumors report on an Android Police leak of the second-generation Pixel XL with a squeezable frame, 6-inch display and thin bezels.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Tuesday July 11, 2017 (Juli Clover), citing information and rendered images leaked by Android Police.
- Google's second-generation Pixel XL could have a squeezable body, a 6-inch AMOLED display and thinner bezels. LG is said to be manufacturing it.
- Design curved like the original Pixel; rear fingerprint sensor now in the aluminum portion; a large single-lens rear camera (no dual lens).
- Only the XL is covered by the leak: 6-inch LG-made display, 2:1 aspect ratio, rounded corners, "minimal bezel".
- The "squeezable" frame, like the HTC U11's "Edge Sense", would let users squeeze the phone to activate Google Assistant "in various ways". On the U11 squeeze can turn on the flashlight, launch the camera, take a photo or launch Assistant.
- Release date unclear; the original was unveiled in October 2016, so a fall release is plausible, alongside the iPhone 8 and against the Galaxy S8 and rumored Galaxy Note 8.

wikis.title: Google Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL announced
wikis.summary: Android Authority's Oct 4, 2017 rundown of the officially announced Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL: specs, IP67, no headphone jack, Active Edge, pricing and Oct 19 shipping.
wikis.body:
- Android Authority, Oct 4, 2017 (Jimmy Westenberg).
- Design: mostly-aluminum chassis with a shorter glass panel that no longer covers the fingerprint sensor; larger rear camera sensor. Google says the fingerprint sensor "unlocks faster than any other smartphone".
- Pixel 2: 5.0-inch OLED 1,920 x 1,080, 16:9, 2,700 mAh battery. Pixel 2 XL: 6.0-inch 2,880 x 1,440 P-OLED, 18:9, slim bezels, 3,520 mAh battery.
- Both: octa-core 2.35 GHz Snapdragon 835, Adreno 430 GPU, 4 GB RAM, 64 or 128 GB storage, no microSD.
- Always-On Display listens to nearby audio (if enabled) to show song info. Pixel Launcher redesigned: search bar moved under docked icons and an "at a glance" section added.
- Camera: DxOMark score of 98 for the Pixel 2 (vs 94 for the Galaxy Note 8 and the iPhone 8 comparison); 1/2.6-inch 12.2 MP sensor, f/1.8.
- IP67 water and dust resistance (up to 1 meter of fresh water for 30 minutes).
- No 3.5 mm headphone jack; USB Type-C or wireless needed.
- Active Edge (similar to HTC's Edge Sense): squeeze the sides to launch Google Assistant. HTC made the smaller Pixel 2; Google recently bought a big chunk of HTC's workforce for $1.1 billion.
- Colors: Pixel 2 in Just Black, Clearly White, Kinda Blue; Pixel 2 XL in Just Black and Black & White.
- Pre-orders open Oct 4, shipping date October 19. Prices: Pixel 2 $649 (64 GB) / $749 (128 GB); Pixel 2 XL $849 / $949. Free Google Home Mini for a limited time. Verizon exclusive carrier again.

wikis.title: Google Pixel 2 launch date teased for October 4
wikis.summary: TechRadar, 14 September 2017: a cryptic Google video and a Boston billboard appear to confirm an October 4 Pixel 2 launch.
wikis.body:
- TechRadar, published 14 September 2017 (Cameron Faulkner).
- A cryptic Google video "appears to confirm" an October 4 launch for the Google Pixel 2. It frames the phone as the search result to common phone complaints.
- Google did not name the Pixel 2 or state any specs.
- The teaser themes: battery performance, waterproofing, image quality and Google Assistant smarts.
- Hours earlier, Boston residents noticed a billboard confirming October 4, reading "Ask more from your phone".
- Whether the Pixel 2 would be waterproof or lack a headphone jack was not answered.
- Update: TechRadar received invitations to Google's October 4th event and planned coverage from London and San Francisco.

wikis.title: Xbox One X announced at E3 2017: November 7, $499
wikis.summary: The Verge on Microsoft unveiling Project Scorpio as the Xbox One X at E3 2017, with specs, launch games and pricing.
wikis.body:
- The Verge, Jun 11, 2017 (Tom Warren). Project Scorpio officially named Xbox One X, days after Microsoft trademarked an "S" logo.
- Launch: November 7 worldwide, $499, 449 pounds, 499 euro, 599 Canadian dollars, 649 Australian dollars.
- Compatible with all existing Xbox One accessories, Xbox 360 backwards-compatible titles and Xbox One games. "Super sampling" makes new games look better on 1080p TVs.
- 6 teraflops of GPU power vs PS4 Pro's 4.2; custom GPU at 1172MHz (Xbox One 853MHz, PS4 Pro 911MHz). Ultra HD Blu-ray drive, 1TB storage, liquid-cooled vapor-chamber cooling.
- "Smallest Xbox ever", black design similar to Xbox One S, HDMI-in, no dedicated Kinect port.
- Forza Motorsport 7 at native 4K and 60fps debuts October 3rd. 22 "console launch exclusives" incl. Crackdown 3, Forza Motorsport 7, Sea of Thieves. Gears of War 4, Forza Horizon 3, Killer Instinct, Halo Wars 2 and Minecraft updated free to 4K. More than 30 third-party titles in the Xbox One X Enhanced program. Original Xbox games (starting with Crimson Skies) coming to Xbox One.

wikis.title: Xbox One X launches worldwide
wikis.summary: Microsoft press release on the November 7, 2017 worldwide launch of Xbox One X in 35 markets, with launch lineup, Enhanced program and pricing.
wikis.body:
- Microsoft Source, November 7, 2017 (dateline REDMOND, Wash., Nov. 6, 2017). "World's most powerful console"; record preorder sales indicate high demand this holiday season.
- "40 percent more power than any other console"; true 4K gaming, HDR, Wide Color Gamut, 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray, 4K streaming, Dolby Atmos support.
- Launch lineup: more than 70 Xbox One X Enhanced titles in the first week, more than 50 on launch day (Forza Motorsport 7, Super Lucky's Tale, Assassin's Creed Origins, Middle-earth: Shadow of War, FIFA 18). More than 160 new and existing games to be enhanced, incl. Halo Wars 2, Gears of War 4, Halo 5: Guardians, Minecraft, Final Fantasy XV, Star Wars Battlefront II.
- PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds arrives as an Xbox One console launch exclusive Dec. 12, 2017 via Xbox Game Preview.
- Xbox One library: more than 1,300 games, more than 220 exclusives. Xbox One X coexists with Xbox One S; all accessories compatible. Xbox Game Pass: more than 100 games monthly.
- Available now in 35 markets; retails at US$499, 449 pounds, 499 euro, C$599, A$649.
- Launch events: New Zealand supercar delivery, Sydney "Xbox Stay N' Play", Munich "World's Largest Unboxing", London 14-hour livestream, Paris 8-hour Mixer stream, Mexico City midnight event, Toronto-inspired custom consoles by Brian Espiritu, and a New York Microsoft Store launch with Shaquille O'Neal, Liam Payne, Ronda Rousey, Odell Beckham Jr. and Caleb McLaughlin. Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson surprised three Make-A-Wish kids with custom consoles.
- Quote, Phil Spencer: "We built Xbox One X to give game creators the most powerful platform to bring their visions to life."

wikis.title: Xbox One X FAQ: price, release, specs, games
wikis.summary: PCWorld's updated guide (Nov 7, 2017) to the Xbox One X covering price, launch, specs versus rivals, software features and FAQs.
wikis.body:
- PCWorld, updated Nov 7, 2017. Xbox One X (formerly Project Scorpio) launched worldwide November 7 at $500.
- Early buyers could preorder a limited $500 "Project Scorpio" Edition with branding and dotted paint; most US retailers sold out by launch day (Amazon and Target still had it). Standard version at Amazon, GameStop, Best Buy, Microsoft Store.
- Specs: 40 Radeon cores at 1,172MHz (original Xbox One 12 cores at 853MHz); 6 teraflops vs PS4 Pro ($400) 4.2, Xbox One S 1.4, PS4 1.84, Radeon RX 580 6.17, RX 570 5.1, RX 560 2.6. RAM up from 8GB DDR3 to 12GB GDDR5, 326GB/s bandwidth. Vapor chamber cooling. 1TB storage.
- Forza Motorsport 7 and other Microsoft franchises run at 4K and 60fps; not all games will.
- Software (announced at Gamescom): transfer settings, games and apps from an existing Xbox One via external drive or local network; Dashboard revamp with horizontal Guide tabs, "content blocks" home screen, and a Light mode.
- FAQ: does not replace Xbox One S, which stays as the base option from $250 (500GB); On a 1080p TV, supersampling still helps detail, clarity and anti-aliasing.

wikis.title: Ecocapsule off-grid pod home
wikis.summary: Mashable, May 26, 2015, on Nice Architects' wind and solar-powered Ecocapsule microhome.
wikis.body:
- Mashable, May 26, 2015 (Karissa Bell). Ecocapsule by Slovakia-based Nice Architects, designed to offer the "convenience of household facilities in off-grid conditions".
- About 120 square feet; "comfortably" houses two adults. Bed, kitchenette, bathroom (running water, hot shower, flushing toilet), small workspace with table and chairs.
- Wind turbine and solar cells fuel a 9,744 watt-hour battery; collects and reuses rainwater and dew. The company says it can support a person for as much as a year at a time off-grid.
- Uses named by the company: independent research station, tourist lodge, emergency housing, humanitarian-action unit.
- No price revealed; pre-orders planned later in 2015 and first units shipping in the first half of 2016. Shipping estimates: about $1,632 to Melbourne, $2,394 to New York.
- To be shown at the Pioneers Festival in Vienna, Austria that week and later in the year in the Slovak National Pavilion.

wikis.title: First Ecocapsule microhomes shipping to customers
wikis.summary: Inhabitat slideshow saying the Ecocapsule off-grid pods are due to reach their first customers this year, with 50 first-edition units.
wikis.body:
- Inhabitat slideshow (dated 06/06/2017, by Lacy Cooke).
- The Ecocapsule is eight feet high, seven feet long and 14.5 feet wide; powered by sun and wind, designed to gather rainwater; moves on a trailer or in a shipping container.
- Late night host James Corden tested the pods in a garden, a horse ranch and a restaurant rooftop; he said he could stay in the Ecocapsule for years.
- Financial backing from international investors lets the company move forward; first units to be delivered to clients "later this year". Only 50 first-edition pods will be made, with mass production at a lower price planned for 2018.

wikis.title: Ecocapsule pre-orders open, first unit complete
wikis.summary: New Atlas, Feb 9, 2018: the Slovak egg-shaped Ecocapsule tiny house is finished, with 50 units pre-ordered at EUR 79,900 for 2018 delivery.
wikis.body:
- New Atlas, February 09, 2018 (Adam Williams). Ecocapsule's first unit is complete; an initial run of 50 is being sold this year, more planned for 2019. Photos show the first finished unit delivered by helicopter to the roof of the UNIQ building in Bratislava.
- Size: 4.67 x 2.2 m (15 x 7.2 ft), max height 2.5 m (8.2 ft), floorspace 8.2 sq m (88 sq ft), weight 1,650 kg (3,637 lb) with full water tanks. Steel frame, fiberglass shell, polyurethane foam insulation, no foundations needed. Sliding door (prototype had a lifting door).
- Interior: bed, camper-van-style bathroom with shower and composting toilet, kitchenette with sink and electric cooktop (mini-fridge optional), seating area, closet, desk, storage.
- Power: grid hookup or off-grid with 880 W solar array and 750 W telescopic wind turbine, both feeding batteries. Rainwater collection tanks or external water. HVAC unit; iOS/Android app shows power use and water levels and controls lighting and ventilation.
- Price: the initial 50 units are pre-orders at EUR 79,900 (US$97,800) with delivery promised for 2018; a cheaper second run planned for early 2019, price TBA. Delivery was previously expected in 2017; the article notes delays and uncertainty.

wikis.title: UK's ST40 fusion reactor generates first plasma
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering, May 3, 2017: Tokamak Energy's privately built ST40 tokamak switched on and made first plasma, aiming for 100 million degrees C by 2018.
wikis.body:
- Interesting Engineering, May 03, 2017 (Shelby Rogers). The UK switched on its newest fusion reactor the previous week; the ST40, by Tokamak Energy, already generated plasma in its core.
- The reactor "should heat plasma to 100 million degrees Celsius (or 180 million degrees Fahrenheit) by 2018", described as seven times hotter than the Sun's core.
- CEO David Kingham: "We are unveiling the first world-class controlled fusion device to have been designed, built and operated by a private venture... This will allow fusion power to be achieved in years, not decades."
- Context cited: MIT plasma-pressure record last October; a South Korean team's 300 million degrees C plasma held 70 seconds last December; Germany's Wendelstein 7-X controlled plasma.
- Challenges: costs; Kingham says significant investment, collaborations and supply chain are needed; "We are already half-way to the goal of fusion energy... commercial scale by 2030."
- ST40 is stage three of a five-stage plan; Tokamak Energy is based in Oxfordshire, England.

wikis.title: Tokamak Energy turns on ST40 fusion reactor
wikis.summary: World Nuclear News, 28 April 2017: ST40 achieved first plasma; full magnetic coils to follow, aiming at 100 million degrees.
wikis.body:
- World Nuclear News, Friday, 28 April 2017. The UK's newest fusion reactor was turned on for the first time and achieved first plasma. It aims for a record 100 million degrees plasma temperature for a privately-funded venture, "seven times hotter than the centre of the Sun".
- Oxford, England-based Tokamak Energy: next steps are completing commissioning and installing the full set of magnetic coils. That should allow 15 million degrees plasma (as hot as the Sun's centre) in the autumn of this year.
- CEO David Kingham quoted: "the first world-class controlled fusion device to have been designed, built and operated by a private venture"; needs significant investment; "deliver fusion power at commercial scale by 2030."
- Background: company grew out of Culham Laboratory (home to JET); uses high temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets. Its ST25 HTS demonstrated 29 hours of continuous plasma at the Royal Society Summer Science Exhibition in London in 2015, a world record.

wikis.title: First plasma for upgraded ST40 (December 2022)
wikis.summary: Nuclear Engineering International, Dec 15, 2022: Tokamak Energy's upgraded ST40 achieved first plasma after returning to operation; this is a later upgrade, not the 2017 switch-on.
wikis.body:
- Nuclear Engineering International, December 15, 2022. The upgraded ST40 achieved first plasma after returning to operation, part of a mission to demonstrate grid-ready power by the early 2030s.
- Earlier in 2022 the ST40 reached a plasma temperature of 100 million degrees Celsius, "the highest temperature ever achieved in a privately funded spherical tokamak".
- Upgrade included a new high-powered Thomson scattering laser system measuring temperature and density; new experiments can reach temperatures more than six times hotter than the sun's core, relating to the planned ST80-HTS prototype and ST-E1 pilot plant.
- CEO Chris Kelsall quoted on clean, low-cost commercial fusion.
- In October, Tokamak Energy and UKAEA signed a five-year framework agreement on spherical tokamaks (materials, power generation, fuel cycle, diagnostics, remote handling). UKAEA's STEP programme aims for a prototype at West Burton, Nottinghamshire.
- The page does not describe the original 2017 first plasma.

wikis.title: Fitbit says smartwatch will be ready for the holidays
wikis.summary: The Verge, Aug 2, 2017: Fitbit's Q2 2017 earnings call said its delayed smartwatch will arrive by the holiday season, with GPS and 50m water resistance.
wikis.body:
- The Verge, Aug 2, 2017 (Lauren Goode). In its Q2 earnings report Fitbit said its long-awaited smartwatch, reported delayed by production issues, will be available "by this holiday season".
- CEO James Park: health and fitness tracking, GPS, water resistant up to 50 meters, cross-platform compatibility, "multi-day battery life". No exact ship date; CFO Bill Zerella said "vast majority of revenue in Q3 will be related to legacy products", implying not before Q4.
- Fitbit is looking into tracking conditions like sleep apnea.
- Q2 revenue beat expectations: $353.3 million vs $341.6 million expected. US revenue down 55 percent to $199 million; Americas excluding US down 11 percent to $24 million; Asia-Pacific up 21 percent to $21 million. Units 3.4 million vs 5.7 million a year earlier; operating costs down seven percent. 67 million Fitbits sold to date; Charge 2 is the most popular.

wikis.title: Fitbit Q2 2017 results beat expectations
wikis.summary: CNBC, Aug 2, 2017: Fitbit reported a smaller-than-expected loss and higher revenue, and said its smartwatch is on track before the holidays.
wikis.body:
- CNBC, published Wed, Aug 2 2017 (Abigail Summerville).
- Loss per share 8 cents vs 15 cents expected (Thomson Reuters); revenue $353.3 million vs $341.6 million expected. Year-ago: earnings of 12 cents a share on revenue of $586.5 million.
- 3.4 million devices sold in the quarter, about in line with the 3.47 million expected (StreetAccount).
- Stock gained more than 8 percent after hours, later more than 4 percent higher; it had fallen 62 percent in the past year, hitting a 52-week low of $4.90 on June 22.
- CEO James Park: "Our smartwatch, which we believe will deliver the best health and fitness experience in the category, is on track for delivery ahead of the holiday season and will drive a strong second half of the year."
- R&D is exploring the medical sector, with tools to diagnose and monitor sleep apnea.

wikis.title: Highlights from Fitbit's Q2 2017 earnings call
wikis.summary: Motley Fool piece on Nasdaq (Aug 11, 2017) summarizing Fitbit's Q2 2017 results, inventory recovery, upcoming smartwatch and health ambitions.
wikis.body:
- Motley Fool via Nasdaq, August 11, 2017. Shares rallied 15% the day after the Aug. 3 report; still down about 60% over 12 months.
- Q2 revenue $353 million vs guided $340 million midpoint; adjusted net loss $0.08 per share vs guidance of $0.14 to $0.17.
- Units: 3.4 million vs 5.7 million a year earlier (40% fewer), an improvement on the first quarter. Sell-in vs sell-through mismatch; excess retailer inventory said to be worked down. Direct-to-consumer sales up 34% year over year to $48 million.
- Smartwatch: Park confirmed availability for the holiday season with GPS, water resistance to 50 meters and third-party software development; "health and fitness-first focus". Exact price and release date still missing. Q3 revenue guidance $380 million to $400 million.
- Park: devices are a "means to an end"; sleep apnea affects 22 million Americans, 80% of whom don't realize they have it.

wikis.title: SolarGaps smart window blinds that generate solar power
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering, May 17, 2017, on the SolarGaps Kickstarter: photovoltaic window blinds for renters that track the sun.
wikis.body:
- Interesting Engineering, May 17, 2017 (Shelby Rogers). SolarGaps Kickstarter idea: photovoltaic solar panel window blinds needing no roof, aimed at renters and small businesses.
- Claims: could save users up to 70 percent on the energy bill; blinds track the sun and adjust angle; also cool a home and save up to 40 percent on air conditioning.
- Wall brackets aren't permanent; plug-in dock to charge devices directly; store energy in a battery for peak hours; or sell surplus to the grid via a two-way meter. Connects with Google Home, Amazon Echo and Nest; companion app (WiFi or Bluetooth) shows forecast and basic controls, plus schedules (wake-up / bedtime).
- Founder Yevgen Erik was inspired by sunflowers following the sun (phototropism). Recommended install on the exterior; withstands -40 to 176 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Shipping: earliest September 2017; all Kickstarter backers by December of this year. Extra small set $390, "50 percent off the market retail price". Custom fittings offered.

wikis.title: TechCrunch hands-on with SolarGaps solar blinds
wikis.summary: TechCrunch, May 31, 2017: a skeptical look at SolarGaps' Kickstarter solar window blinds, its performance claims, payback and a review sample.
wikis.body:
- TechCrunch, May 31, 2017 (Haje Jan Kamps). SolarGaps runs a Kickstarter for solar panel window blinds; integrates with a smartphone app, Google Home, Amazon Echo and Nest Thermostat; can feed the grid or a battery like the Tesla Powerwall; claimed custom-made for the same cost as non-solar motorized blinds.
- The math: south-facing wall about 10 hours of direct sun per day; a 10-square-foot panel (quoted $385) yields around 1.5 kWh per day, about 500 kWh per year, roughly $88 per year, so about 4-6 years payback in perfect sunshine.
- Author's concerns: vertical walls are at a disadvantage to roof panels. A roughly 3.2-foot review sample was well built, but measured output fell well short; the sample had a 220V to 110V converter and a less efficient DC-DC test box than planned for shipping.
- CEO Yevgen Erik: face the sun, no shade, rotate blinds via the app; active shading may cut AC energy by up to 40%, payback "3 years or less"; software updates improved efficiency by 20 percent. Recommends outside mounting (harder to install).
- Verdict: good for hot, sunny, high-AC-bill areas but a small market. Kickstarter status: 14 days to go, 231 backers, about $60,000 vs $50,000 goal.

wikis.title: Tesla sets July 29 Gigafactory grand opening
wikis.summary: Electrek, May 27, 2016: invitations show Tesla's Nevada Gigafactory grand opening is July 29, with the factory still partly built.
wikis.body:
- Electrek, May 27 2016 (Fred Lambert). Tesla sent invitations to top Model S referrers (5+ sales, October to December): grand opening "on the evening of Friday, July 29th at our facility outside Reno, Nevada".
- Only phase one is built: 800,000-square-foot footprint and 1.9 million square feet of space, called the "pilot plant". Expected total: about 13 million square feet. Tesla calls it "Gigafactory 1".
- Tesla Energy production moved from Fremont to the plant in October 2015; volume production ramp in early 2016; battery cell production expected to start later in 2016.
- Musk called the cells "moderate" battery improvements; Tesla aims to cut cell cost 30 to 50% through scale.

wikis.title: Tesla sets July 29 grand opening for Nevada gigafactory
wikis.summary: Utility Dive, May 31, 2016: Tesla will hold the $5 billion Gigafactory grand opening July 29 though it was only 14% complete.
wikis.body:
- Utility Dive, published May 31, 2016 (Gavin Bade), citing Fortune. Grand opening of the $5 billion Reno, Nevada gigafactory on July 29, though it was only 14% complete earlier that month. Tesla habitually hosts opening events for each completed section.
- Already producing Powerwall and Powerpack stationary batteries; car batteries not yet at large scale. Model 3 has more than 400,000 reservations; Tesla raised $1.7 billion.
- May 2015 Powerwall/Powerpack launch is called the day "energy storage went mainstream". Examples: Green Mountain Power offering Powerwalls with no upfront cost; SolarCity using Tesla batteries in Hawaii.
- Prep work began May 2014. When complete: 5.8 million square feet; net-zero energy building with rooftop and hillside solar; Tesla acts as its own contractor.

wikis.title: SolPad Mobile pricing and pre-order date
wikis.summary: pv magazine USA press release (Jan 13, 2017): SolPad Mobile integrated solar panel with storage, $1395, pre-orders from May 3, 2017.
wikis.body:
- pv magazine USA press release, Jan 13 2017 (Frank Andorka). SolPad Mobile: "world's first integrated solar panel with built-in energy storage and an Internet of Energy (IoE) smart home platform".
- Pre-order from May 3, 2017 at www.solpad.com for an introductory $1395.00; limited offer includes the free SolControl Solar Smart Plug (valued $59.95); extra SolControls $39.95. Ships second half of 2017.
- Specs: 70 watts solar, 600 Wh battery, two fast-charging USB outlets, LED lighting, Wi-Fi, two AC outlets with 2000 W peak and 1000 W continuous; 25 pounds; units link into a micro-grid and mesh networks can act as a hot spot. Controlled from an iPhone; SolControl directs stored power to specific appliances.
- Quoted as "the coolest energy tech to debut this year" by David Roberts of Vox.
- SolPad Home (rooftop panel) pricing and pre-order date TBA.

wikis.title: GLOBALFOUNDRIES to jump from 14nm straight to 7nm
wikis.summary: HEXUS, 16 September 2016: GLOBALFOUNDRIES plans to skip 10nm and start 7nm FinFET production by early 2018.
wikis.body:
- HEXUS.net, 16 September 2016 (Mark Tyson). GLOBALFOUNDRIES announced it plans to go straight to 7nm FinFET production by early 2018, skipping "the marginal performance and power benefits for the high cost of the 10nm process node".
- 7nm expected to deliver "more than twice the logic density and a 30 percent performance boost" over 16/14nm FinFET. Reuses significant portions of 14nm tools and processes; multi-billion dollar investment in its Fab 8 campus.
- CEO Sanjay Jha touts experience, former IBM Microelectronics staff and the research alliance; AMD CEO Lisa Su cheers it on; IBM Research's Arvind Krishna says IBM continues to collaborate on 7nm and beyond. A WSJ analyst: "It's a bit risky to make that big of a jump".
- Press release: test chips already made in Fab 8; ready for customer product design starts in the second half of 2017, "with ramp to risk production in early 2018".

wikis.title: GlobalFoundries offers 7nm after skipping 10nm
wikis.summary: Electronic Design, June 14, 2017: GlobalFoundries opened 7nm design to customers, with volume production planned in the second half of 2018 at Fab 8.
wikis.body:
- Electronic Design, June 14, 2017 (James Morra). Last year GlobalFoundries said it skipped 10nm; on Tuesday it began letting customers design chips for its 7nm line (smartphones, servers).
- 7LP claims around 40% more processing power and twice the area scaling vs 14nm. First products in the first half of 2018; volume production in the second half at Fab 8 in Saratoga County, N.Y.; "multiple product tapeouts planned in 2018" (Greg Bartlett). Uses optical lithography first, later EUV; plans to install two EUV tools this year.
- Rivals: Samsung shipped 70,000 wafers of 10nm by March and plans 8nm this year, 7nm next year, 4nm in 2020; TSMC plans several 7nm tapeouts this year (contracts $29.5 billion last year, up from $24.1 billion); Intel said its 10nm chips will contain 100.8 million transistors, with 34nm fin spacing vs 42nm in 14nm chips, and is building a 7nm pilot plant.
- GlobalFoundries began 14nm last year at Fab 8, capacity to expand 20% by early next year; more than 20 customers including AMD (Polaris graphics). With IBM and Samsung it demonstrated 5nm silicon nanosheets.
- VLSI Research's Dan Hutcheson: "By biting the bullet and skipping 10nm, GlobalFoundries opened up the technical bandwidth to attack 7nm head-on."

wikis.title: GlobalFoundries confirms skipping 10nm for 7nm
wikis.summary: Custom PC Review, Aug 17, 2016: CEO Gary Patton told SemiWiki GlobalFoundries will skip 10nm and go directly to 7nm.
wikis.body:
- Custom PC Review, Aug 17, 2016 (Sam Chen), from a SemiWiki interview with GlobalFoundries CEO Gary Patton.
- GlobalFoundries will skip 10nm, which, like 20nm, it believes will be a very short-lived node.
- It offers 14nm FinFET via a licensing agreement with Samsung and is developing 7nm thanks to its acquisition of IBM's Microelectronics business in July of the previous year.
- First 7nm process will use optical lithography but will support EUV when ready. No production timing given; TSMC expected to begin 7nm trial production as early as 2017.

wikis.title: Micron updates GDDR5X and GDDR6 development
wikis.summary: HEXUS, 5 June 2017: Micron sells GDDR5X at up to 12Gbps, tested 16Gbps, and expects GDDR6 mass production early in 2018.
wikis.body:
- HEXUS.net, 5 June 2017 (Mark Tyson). Micron: GDDR5X launched at 10Gbps, now supplied at 10, 11 and 12Gbps; 16Gbps GDDR5X tested "on a meaningful sampling size of our mass production G5X silicon".
- GDDR6 (dual-channel architecture) will hit mass production early in 2018; estimated 12-14Gbps at launch. Key advantages: FBGA180 ball package with increased pitch, and dual channel.
- Nvidia Titan Xp uses Micron's G5X at 11.4Gbps, in mass production.
- Strong demand segments: PC gaming, console gaming, professional visualisation, HPC / data centre, autonomous vehicles; expected to continue to 2020 and beyond.

wikis.title: Micron completes GDDR6 design and qualification
wikis.summary: Wccftech, Dec 25, 2017: Micron says GDDR6 design and device qualification are complete, with mass production in the first half of 2018.
wikis.body:
- Wccftech, Dec 25, 2017 (Hassan Mujtaba). Micron confirmed in a blog post (Kristopher Kido, Director of its global Graphics Memory Business) that GDDR6 design and device qualification are complete; mass production expected early or first half of 2018. Graphics teams in Munich and Boise did the work.
- Micron says it is the only manufacturer to design, test and mass produce GDDR5X, giving it a position with GDDR6, which "shares a very similar specification".
- Initial GDDR6 production speeds 12 and 14 Gb/s, with 16 Gb/s expected over time. Specs: 16Gb dies, FBGA180 ball package with increased pitch, dual channel architecture.
- Micron also began mass production shipments of 8Gb GDDR5 on its 1Xnm DRAM node; budget cards are expected to keep using GDDR5 as GDDR6 costs a slight premium.

wikis.title: Micron pushes GDDR5X to 16Gbps, GDDR6 early 2018
wikis.summary: PC Perspective, Jun 7, 2017: Micron reached 16Gbps on GDDR5X silicon and expects GDDR6 mass production in early 2018.
wikis.body:
- PC Perspective, Jun 7, 2017 (Tim Verry). JEDEC made GDDR5X official almost a year and a half earlier, launching at 10 Gbps and quickly hitting 12 Gbps.
- Micron's Graphics Design Team in Munich achieved 16 Gbps on a "meaningful sampling" of mass-production GDDR5X silicon, measured with a PRBS11 pattern read.
- Micron expects to begin mass production of GDDR6 in early 2018. GDDR6: larger FBGA180 package, starts at 12Gbps vs G5X's 10Gbps, dual channel with x8/x16 per channel (GDDR5X is x16/x32).
- SK Hynix showed its first GDDR6 chip at GTC with a similar two-channel design.

wikis.title: Intel and AMD team up on 8th-gen H-series with AMD graphics
wikis.summary: MacRumors, Nov 6, 2017: Intel announced 8th-generation H-series mobile chips with custom AMD Radeon graphics and HBM2 in one package via EMIB.
wikis.body:
- MacRumors, Monday November 6, 2017 (Juli Clover). Intel and AMD are joining forces on new 8th-Generation H-Series Intel mobile processors paired with stacked second-generation High Bandwidth Memory and custom-built discrete AMD graphics in a single package.
- Uses Intel's Embedded Multi-Die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB), which cuts the silicon footprint to less than half that of standard discrete components; first consumer product using EMIB. Intel developed drivers to coordinate temperature and power sharing across the package.
- Goal: thin, light, powerful laptops that can game; helps compete with Nvidia. Many unknowns; first machines in the first quarter of 2018.

wikis.title: 15-inch HP Spectre x360 with new graphics and number pad
wikis.summary: Laptop Mag, 8 January 2018: HP's CES 2018 15-inch Spectre x360 adds Kaby Lake-G Radeon RX Vega M or MX150 options and a number pad; from $1,369.99 on March 18.
wikis.body:
- Laptop Mag, published 8 January 2018 (Andrew E. Freedman), at CES 2018 in Las Vegas.
- Launch March 18 starting at $1,369.99. Choice of Intel Core i7-8550U with Nvidia MX150, or the newly announced Intel Kaby Lake-G chip with built-in Radeon RX Vega M graphics.
- Specs: 15.6-inch 4K display, 16GB RAM, up to 512GB PCIe NVMe SSD, 14.1 x 9.84 x 0.76 inches, 4.6 pounds, up to 13.5 hours battery, Thunderbolt 3, USB Type-C, USB 3.1, HDMI. IR camera for Windows Hello, fingerprint reader, stylus in the box.
- New expanded keyboard with a number pad; silver/ash and copper configurations.

wikis.title: AMD delivers semi-custom GPU for new Intel processor
wikis.summary: AMD press release, November 06, 2017: AMD designed a semi-custom Radeon GPU for an Intel multi-chip package, launching Q1 2018.
wikis.body:
- AMD press release, November 06, 2017 (Sunnyvale). AMD designed a semi-custom GPU integrated into a new Intel multi-chip processor package; the product, designed by Intel, combines an Intel Core processor, a semi-custom Radeon graphics chip and second-generation HBM2.
- Scott Herkelman (AMD Radeon Technologies Group): the collaboration "expands the installed base for AMD Radeon GPUs" and offers thinner-and-lighter PCs with discrete-tier graphics for AAA games and content creation.
- Intel expects the product to launch in the first quarter of 2018.

wikis.title: Intel's first 10nm Cannon Lake chip ships (Core i3-8121U)
wikis.summary: AppleInsider, May 17, 2018: Core i3-8121U in the Lenovo IdeaPad 330 confirms Cannon Lake 10nm with 32GB LPDDR4 support.
wikis.body:
- AppleInsider, Thu May 17 2018 (Malcolm Owen), citing Ars Technica. Chinese retailer listings for the Lenovo IdeaPad 330 show the new Core i3-8121U; Intel's Ark confirms it is 10-nanometer, launched in Q2 2018.
- Dual-core, four threads, 2.2GHz base, 3.2GHz Turbo, 4MB cache, 15W TDP. Supports DDR4-2400 and LPDDR4/x-2400 with a max of 32 gigabytes; Cannon Lake could let Apple offer 32GB in MacBook lines (current MacBook Pro capped at 16GB partly due to no native LPDDR4 support).
- Ark doesn't appear to list an integrated GPU, suggesting it needs a discrete GPU.
- In April Intel said it would concentrate on shipping 14nm processors this year, with some 10nm chips shipping but high-volume 10nm manufacturing shifted into 2019 to improve yield.

wikis.title: Daimler starts building a $562 million lithium-ion battery factory in Kamenz, Germany
wikis.summary: Ars Technica reports Daimler's groundbreaking for a roughly EUR 500 million battery factory in Kamenz attended by Chancellor Merkel.
wikis.body:
- On Monday (article dated May 22, 2017), German Chancellor Angela Merkel visited the site of a future lithium-ion battery factory in Kamenz, eastern Germany.
- Daimler (maker of Mercedes-Benz) will devote about EUR 500 million ($562 million) to batteries for electric vehicles and stationary storage.
- The investment would quadruple the size of an existing battery factory on the site, run by Accumotive, a wholly-owned Daimler subsidiary.
- Daimler gave no capacity projections. It pledged another EUR 500 million to expand battery production worldwide. It says the site will "go into operation in mid-2018."
- Compared with Tesla's Nevada Gigafactory (Tesla and Panasonic, $5 billion, hoped 35 GWh by 2018).
- Mercedes-Benz Energy recently partnered with Vivint Solar to sell stationary storage with solar panels in California; Daimler has also experimented with reusing old EV batteries for grid storage.
- Merkel: "We need long-term horizons and companies that invest in the future." German government invested EUR 35 million in battery research; she said she was briefed on lithium cells that could allow up to 1,000 km (621 miles) per charge (per Reuters).
- Bloomberg New Energy Finance: Kamenz will be the biggest battery factory yet in Europe, with large factories planned for Sweden, Hungary and Poland; battery costs expected to fall 41% by 2021, from $271 per kWh to $156 per kWh.
- Daimler wants to bring 10 new electric models to market by 2020 (subtitle).

wikis.title: Daimler unveils its Kamenz battery Gigafactory for electric vehicles
wikis.summary: Electrek covers the May 22, 2017 foundation-stone ceremony for Daimler's EUR 500 million Kamenz battery plant.
wikis.body:
- Daimler produces battery packs via its ACCUmotive subsidiary; last year it announced a EUR 500 million investment in a new battery factory in Kamenz, Germany.
- Inauguration attended by Chancellor Angela Merkel and Saxony Minister President Stanislaw Tillich, with Dieter Zetsche (Daimler chairman), Markus Schaefer, Frank Deiss and Frank Blome; they laid a vehicle battery casing as the foundation stone.
- Capacity not confirmed, but expected to be in the gigawatt-hour range; it will employ over 1,000 workers.
- Goes into operation "in mid-2018", in time for Mercedes' first ground-up all-electric vehicle, the 'EQ' SUV.
- Zetsche: "By 2022, we will have more than ten purely electric passenger cars in series." Daimler earlier announced accelerating EV plans by 3 years and $11 billion on 10 models by 2022.
- Other programmes: all-electric Urban eTruck; 1,500 electric Mercedes-Benz vans for Germany's largest independent logistics firm.
- Partner SK Innovation (Korea) recently announced doubling battery production for EVs to 4 GWh/year.

wikis.title: Apple reportedly planning three OLED iPhones for 2018
wikis.summary: MacRumors relays a Nikkei report that Apple tentatively plans three new OLED iPhone models in the second half of 2018.
wikis.body:
- Nikkei (via MacRumors, July 6, 2017), citing two industry sources: Apple plans OLED displays "in all new iPhone models launched from the second half of 2018."
- One source said Apple is "tentatively" looking at three new models next year, all OLED; 2017's trio has two LCD models and the OLED "iPhone 8".
- Earlier report: OLED for 60 million iPhone 8 units in 2017, doubling in 2018, OLED-only by 2019. A May report predicted 2018 OLED sizes of 5.28-inch and 6.46-inch.
- LG Innotek to start flexible printed circuit boards for the 2018 iPhone in 2018.
- Plans are "subject to change". Apple has begun designing the 2018 phones. Apple did not comment; Samsung Display declined to comment.
- Concern: only Samsung is a reliable OLED source; Samsung is sole supplier for iPhone 8. Apple may invest in an LG Display OLED plant with production estimated to begin in early 2019.
- JDI and Sharp keep supplying LCDs for the "iPhone 7s" and "7s Plus", expected to sell into 2019. A Sharp executive said it is "not likely" every new 2018 iPhone will go OLED.
- iPhone 8 rumored 5.8-inch OLED, edge-to-edge; Ming-Chi Kuo predicts no Touch ID; Bloomberg says improved facial recognition is being worked on.

wikis.title: Supply chain rumors: OLED and LCD iPhone models in 2018
wikis.summary: AppleInsider reports China Times claims about display suppliers for a rumored 2018 iPhone lineup of two OLED and one LCD model.
wikis.body:
- Report (AppleInsider, Jan 23, 2018): Apple's next iPhone lineup rumored to include two OLED versions (5.8 and 6.5 inches) and a 6.1-inch LCD variant.
- China Times, without citing sources: Apple will rely on Samsung for OLED panels in 2018, as with iPhone X. Apple currently orders OLED from Samsung and LG (LG supplies Apple Watch).
- Earlier this month: LG, Sharp and Japan Display reportedly want to join OLED iPhone production; LG, likeliest second supplier, aims for full capacity in 2019; Foxconn-owned Sharp began investing last March.
- Japan Display to supply 18:9 LCD panels for the 6.1-inch model, with LG also; General Interface Solution and TPK Holding reportedly supply touch modules. All would feature edge-to-edge display and Face ID.
- Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo believes Apple will discontinue iPhone X in 2018.
- Source of rumor: Japanese blog Mac Otakara.

wikis.title: iPhone 2018 rumors roundup (Macworld)
wikis.summary: Macworld's running collection of rumors about Apple's 2018 iPhones, updated Sep 5, 2018, with plausibility notes.
wikis.body:
- Updated Sep 5, 2018: 9to5Mac claims leaked official Apple images of the OLED models (5.8 and 6.5-inch), which it says will be called iPhone Xs (5.8) and iPhone Xs Max (6.5); reportedly a glossy gold band/new gold color. 9to5Mac separately claims "Plus" is dropped for "Max".
- Aug 27, 2018 (Ming-Chi Kuo): no Apple Pencil support on OLED models (contradicting Trendforce); preorders Sept 14, availability Sept 21; the 6.1-inch LCD model comes "slightly later due to its production schedule". OLED models 4GB RAM (iPhone X 3GB), LCD 3GB. Batteries: 6.5-inch 3,300-3,400 mAh; 5.8-inch 2,700-2,800 mAh; LCD 2,600-2,700 mAh (iPhone X 2716 mAh).
- Bloomberg: three models (5.8 and 6.5 OLED, 6.1 LCD); LCD model aluminum frame in an array of colors; all with TrueDepth camera and Face ID; some international dual-SIM; likely "iPhone Xs"; biggest gains in processing speed and camera; 6.5-inch may view content side-by-side in apps like Mail and Calendar.
- Aug 20, 2018: Macerkopf, from German carriers, says preorders begin September 14. China Times: at least one model gets a copper wireless-charging coil (current iPhone 8/8 Plus/X use ferrite polymer composite coils, Qi up to 7.5 W).
- Aug 14, 2018: Trendforce predicts 512GB tier for the OLED models (RAM stays 4GB) and Apple Pencil support.
- Dual SIM: 9to5Mac found code in the iOS 12 beta 5 (July 30) referencing "secondSimStatus", "secondSimTrayStatus", "isDualSimDevice".
- July 25, 2018: Morgan Stanley's Katy Huberty (via Barron's) expects a small delay of the 6.1-inch LCD model, blamed on "suspected issues with LED backlight leakage".
- Each rumor has Macworld's "Plausible?" commentary.

wikis.title: Key takeaways: 2018 MacBook Pro vs 2017 MacBook Pro
wikis.summary: MacRumors compares the 2018 Touch Bar MacBook Pro models, introduced July 12, 2018, with the 2017 models.
wikis.body:
- July 12, 2018: Apple introduced new 13-inch and 15-inch MacBook Pro with Touch Bar, available to order.
- Eighth-generation Intel Core; Apple says 15-inch up to 70 percent faster, 13-inch up to two times faster than 2017 (7th-gen).
- 15-inch: up to 2.9GHz six-core Core i9 (2017 topped at 3.1GHz quad-core i7). 13-inch Touch Bar: quad-core up to 2.7GHz (2017 dual-core up to 3.5GHz).
- 15-inch: up to 32GB DDR4 (2017: 16GB LPDDR3); battery watt-hour rating up 10 percent; battery life up to 10 hours. Radeon Pro with 4GB GDDR5 standard on 15-inch; 13-inch has 128MB eDRAM (64MB in 2017).
- Apple T2 chip (with "Hey Siri") replaces T1. SSD up to 2TB (13-inch) and 4TB (15-inch), doubled.
- True Tone displays incl. Touch Bar. "Improved third-generation keyboard for quieter typing" still butterfly; unclear whether it fixes sticky/repeating keys that prompted Apple's service program. Bluetooth 5.0 (was 4.2).
- Same design and I/O (four Thunderbolt 3, headphone jack); resolutions unchanged 2880x1800 / 2560x1600.
- Prices unchanged: 13-inch from $1,799, 15-inch from $2,399 (US), though configure-to-order tops out higher. 13-inch models without Touch Bar were not refreshed.

wikis.title: Apple updates MacBook Pro with faster performance (press release, July 12, 2018)
wikis.summary: Apple's Singapore newsroom copy of the July 12, 2018 announcement of 6-core 15-inch and quad-core 13-inch MacBook Pro with True Tone and T2.
wikis.body:
- Cupertino, July 12, 2018: new 13-inch and 15-inch MacBook Pro with Touch Bar, 8th-generation Intel Core: 6-core on 15-inch (up to 70 percent faster) and quad-core on 13-inch (up to twice as fast).
- Up to 32GB memory (15-inch); SSD up to 2TB (13-inch) and 4TB (15-inch); True Tone Retina display (500 nits, P3 wide colour); improved third-generation keyboard for quieter typing; Apple T2 chip (first in iMac Pro) bringing secure boot, on-the-fly encrypted storage and "Hey Siri" to Mac for the first time.
- 15-inch: 6-core i7/i9 up to 2.9 GHz, Turbo Boost up to 4.8 GHz, DDR4, Radeon Pro with 4GB. 13-inch: quad-core i5/i7 up to 2.7 GHz, Turbo up to 4.5 GHz, Iris Plus 655 with 128MB eDRAM.
- Philip Schiller: "the fastest and most powerful notebook we've ever made".
- Back to School promotion starts that day (Beats headphones with eligible Mac or iPad Pro). New leather sleeves in Saddle Brown, Midnight Blue and, first time, Black. macOS Mojave update coming "this fall".

wikis.title: MacBook Pro (Wikipedia): overview and Intel-based history to the unibody era
wikis.summary: Part 1 of the Wikipedia article on Apple's MacBook Pro line: overview of generations from 2006 and the aluminum and unibody Intel models.
wikis.body:
- Line of notebook computers by Apple, introduced Feb 14, 2006 (released); manufacturers Foxconn, Pegatron, Quanta. Successor to PowerBook; first Apple laptop to use the "MacBook" name. As of June 2026 sold with 14- and 16-inch screens, all Apple M-series chips; Intel Core used 2006-2021.
- Overview: first model used PowerBook G4 design with Intel Core Duo, iSight webcam, MagSafe; 15-inch announced January 2006, 17-inch April. Unibody 15-inch Oct 2008, 17-inch Jan 2009, 13-inch June 2009. Retina MacBook Pro 2012 (15-inch June, 13-inch October). Touch Bar model Oct 2016 (USB-C only, butterfly keyboard, OLED Touch Bar). Nov 2019 revision brought Magic Keyboard (scissor switch), 16-inch; physical Esc key restored. Nov 2020 first with Apple M1; 2022 M2. 14/16-inch M1 Pro/Max Oct 2021 (return of MagSafe, function keys, HDMI, SD card); M2 Pro/Max Jan 2023; M3 family Nov 2023 with base 14-inch M3.
- Aluminum (2006-2008): ExpressCard/34 slot, Core 2 Duo and LED backlight in 2007-2008; GeForce 8600M GT GPU failures, Apple replaced logic boards free for up to four years. Original design discontinued Oct 14, 2008 (15-inch) and Jan 6, 2009 (17-inch).
- Unibody (2008-2012): announced Oct 14, 2008; Mini DisplayPort, Nvidia 9600M GT/9400M, whole-trackpad button; 17-inch unibody announced Jan 6, 2009 with non-removable battery, quoted 8 hours and 80% after 1,000 cycles; 13-inch rebranded MacBook Pro at WWDC June 8, 2009.

wikis.title: NASA renames Solar Probe Plus the Parker Solar Probe, launch planned 2018
wikis.summary: Interesting Engineering reports NASA's May 31, 2017 renaming of Solar Probe Plus after Eugene Parker and the mission's planned 2018 launch.
wikis.body:
- May 31, 2017: NASA announced Solar Probe Plus is renamed Parker Solar Probe, honoring solar astrophysicist Dr. Eugene Parker (S. Chandrasekhar Distinguished Service Professor Emeritus, University of Chicago, where the announcement was made). His 1958 Astrophysical Journal article "Dynamics of the interplanetary gas and magnetic fields" underpinned the concept of solar wind.
- Mission: NASA's first mission to fly directly into the Sun's corona; goal includes why the corona is much hotter than the surface. It will plunge within 4 million miles of the Sun.
- Launch: "in the summer of next year", with a 20-day window opening July 31, 2018.
- Spacecraft: 4.5-inch-thick (11.43 cm) carbon-composite shield; 24 orbits, with many hot and cold cycles. Studying the corona should help understand and potentially forecast space weather (satellite communications, aircraft radiation exposure, astronaut safety, pipeline erosion).
- Nicola Fox (project scientist, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory): the probe "is going to answer questions about solar physics that we've puzzled over for more than six decades."
- Team is placing photos of Parker and his paper inside the spacecraft. It was undergoing tests; the key upcoming test is thermal environment simulation.
- Parker: "The solar probe is going to a region of space that has never been explored before."

wikis.title: Tesla delivers first Model 3 sedans to 30 customers
wikis.summary: Business Insider reports the July 28, 2017 handover event where Tesla delivered its first mass-market vehicle, the Model 3.
wikis.body:
- Friday (July 28, 2017): Elon Musk delivered the first 30 Model 3 sedans at a party at the Fremont factory, kicking off production. Production to ramp to 1,500 a month in September and 20,000 in December.
- Price $35,000; base range 220 miles, 0-60 mph in 5.6 s, top speed 130 mph. Premium (extra $9,000): 310 miles, 5.1 s, 140 mph. Colors: black, midnight silver, deep blue metallic, silver metallic, pearl white multi-coat, red multi-coat.
- Revealed March 2016 with an estimated 500,000 pre-orders ($1,000 deposit); sold out until at least mid-2018. Base model ships to pre-order customers "this fall"; new customers currently only get Premium rear-wheel drive.
- Hardware supports second-generation Enhanced Autopilot ($5,000; software update planned before year-end); collision avoidance and automatic emergency braking are free. Supercharger network doubling in size by end of 2017, restoring 170 miles in 30 minutes.
- Risks cited: production challenges (delays and a Model X recall earlier), skipping the production prototyping stage (per Matthew DeBord), lower margins of sedans; competitors plan battery SUVs by 2019. Tesla stock up more than 50% in the last year; market value rivaled GM and Ford.

wikis.title: Tesla Model 3 delivery date for new orders moves to mid-2018 or later
wikis.summary: TechCrunch reports Tesla's Oct 18, 2016 website change pushing shipping for new Model 3 pre-orders to mid-2018 or beyond.
wikis.body:
- Tesla updated its Model 3 website: orders placed from now on will ship by mid-2018 or beyond (noted by Kyle Russell on Twitter). The page previously listed late 2017.
- TechCrunch confirmed the timeline applies to new orders only, not earlier ones. The site still says production begins in late 2017.
- Pre-orders "well above 400,000", a threshold Tesla confirmed passing in June; the car is an all-electric, $35,000 sedan.

wikis.title: Tesla pushes back delivery of new Model 3 orders to mid-2018
wikis.summary: CNBC via NBC News reports Tesla changing its website to say new Model 3 reservations ship 'mid-2018 or later'.
wikis.body:
- Oct. 18, 2016 (CNBC, Robert Ferris): Tesla tells prospective buyers new orders for the Model 3 will begin shipping in "mid-2018 or later."
- As of Sunday, Tesla's site said deliveries "begin late 2017"; the wording now says production begins late 2017 and the delivery estimate for "new reservations is mid-2018 or later."
- CNBC had asked Tesla for comment.

wikis.title: What a new design could mean for Apple Watch Series 4 (rumors)
wikis.summary: MacRumors summarizes July 2018 rumors, chiefly from Ming-Chi Kuo, of a redesigned Apple Watch Series 4 with a 15 percent larger display.
wikis.body:
- July 12, 2018: Series 4 expected in the fall with a new design and a display 15 percent larger (Ming-Chi Kuo); possibly the first design change since debut three years earlier.
- Kuo expects two sizes with 1.57 inch (39.9mm) and 1.78 inch (45.2mm) displays versus current 38mm and 42mm watches. Unclear whether casings grow or bezels shrink. Mockups by Venya Geskin; developer Ryan Jones calculates 35 and 38 percent larger display area for the 38mm and 42mm models.
- Outside chance of micro-LED screens (thinner, lighter, better gamut/brightness).
- Kuo: improved health monitoring including heart rate features (unclear whether hardware or software), higher-capacity battery. Solid-state Taptic Engine buttons could free space. Apple reportedly testing an EKG feature using two fingers.
- Apple expected to announce at its September event.

wikis.title: Everything we know so far about the Apple Watch Series 4 (9to5Mac)
wikis.summary: 9to5Mac's July 27, 2018 roundup of Series 4 rumors on design, buttons, health, performance, price and release.
wikis.body:
- Design: first major shift since 2015; reduced bezels, display roughly 15 percent bigger than Series 3 (Kuo, March). Later Kuo: 1.57-inch and 1.78-inch displays for 38mm and 42mm models, with no overall body size increase; Series 3 has 1.5-inch and 1.65-inch. Curved display edges like iPhone X.
- Buttons: Fast Company reported Apple would replace the physical Digital Crown and Side button with solid-state ones using the Taptic Engine (like iPhone 7 Home button), aiding waterproofing and freeing space for a bigger battery.
- Health: Kuo indicates improved heart rate detection; details unclear. Fitbit noted as supporting sleep tracking and sleep apnea detection.
- Performance: Series 3 has dual-core S3; processor for Series 4 unclear, likely called S4.
- Price: expected unchanged; Series 3 starts $329 (GPS) and $399 (cellular).
- Release: likely announced in September alongside new iPhones; first three models were all announced at September events.

wikis.title: Microsoft's next-gen HoloLens codenamed Sydney, arriving Q1 2019
wikis.summary: Thurrott reports, from documents viewed by Brad Sams, that Microsoft targets a Q1 2019 release for a cheaper, lighter HoloLens codenamed Sydney.
wikis.body:
- Jun 12, 2018 (Brad Sams): a little over a year earlier he reported Microsoft stopped development of HoloLens V2 and pushed to V3.
- Based on documents he viewed, Microsoft still targets a Q1 release ("early next year", i.e. 2019) and calls the project Sydney internally.
- Per the documents: lighter, more comfortable, significantly improved holographic displays, and significantly cheaper than the current HoloLens.
- Unknown whether Q1 is general availability or a developer preview (speculation).
- Microsoft approaches MR/VR as a "must-win market"; competitors include Apple, Google, Magic Leap.

wikis.title: Microsoft HoloLens 2, codenamed Sydney, reportedly tipped for Q1 2019
wikis.summary: HotHardware relays Thurrott's report of a cheaper, lighter second-generation HoloLens codenamed Sydney due Q1 2019.
wikis.body:
- June 13, 2018 (Shane McGlaun): rumor that a second-generation HoloLens codenamed Sydney arrives Q1 2019. Microsoft reportedly had stopped developing HoloLens V2 and moved toward a more groundbreaking "V3" device.
- Thurrott says documents claim the headset is lighter, more comfortable, with improved holographic displays, and tipped to cost significantly less.
- Unclear whether Q1 is developer preview only or general availability. Microsoft views mixed/virtual reality as must-win.
- Google reportedly planning its own HoloLens competitor.
- Other reports: Microsoft to unveil details in the second half of 2018; reportedly testing an ARM-based processor to improve battery life; OS would be a version of Windows 10.

wikis.title: HoloLens 2 codename is Sydney (techAU)
wikis.summary: techAU's June 13, 2018 note, via Thurrott, that Microsoft's HoloLens 2 is due Q1 2019 under the codename Sydney.
wikis.body:
- June 13, 2018 (Jason Cartwright): HoloLens was developed in secrecy for 5 years; moderate business success, usually as a training device; high price and limited field of view held it back.
- News from Thurrott.com: version 2 due in the first quarter of 2019, codename 'Sydney'. Paul Thurrott says he saw documents showing Microsoft sees the Mixed Reality / Virtual Reality market as a must-win after missing on phones.
- Competitors named: Google, Magic Leap, HTC, Sony, Facebook-owned Oculus.
- Author's hopes: fix field of view and price.

wikis.title: Eli Zero neighborhood electric vehicle (Ars Technica)
wikis.summary: Ars Technica's May 1, 2018 look at the Eli Zero, a small enclosed two-seat NEV pitched as a city second car.
wikis.body:
- May 1, 2018 (Jonathan M. Gitlin). Argues autonomous cars won't solve congestion; NEVs like the Eli Zero may help city dwellers.
- NEV: low-speed vehicle certified for roads with limits of 45mph (72km/h) or less. Zero is a two-seater, side-by-side, fully enclosed (unlike Renault Twizy, GEM, golf carts).
- 4kW (5.3hp) motor, 6kWh lithium-ion battery: 55 miles (89km) range, 4.5 hours charge at 110V. Zero+ with 8.3kWh pack: 85 miles (137km), six hours. Weight 877lbs (398kg) or 904lbs (410kg).
- Founder Marcus Li: "85 clean miles at only $1, assuming 12c/kWh"; about 350MPGe; aluminum chassis; 40 percent smaller than a Smart Car. No self-driving; Li believes autonomy will worsen traffic.
- Not eligible for IRS credit; California Air Resources Board in contact about a $1,000 rebate.
- Eli tooling up; hopes to deliver first vehicles in early 2019. MSRP $10,900, with discounts for preorders.

wikis.title: First Eli Zero Neighborhood Electric Vehicles go into production
wikis.summary: New Atlas reports the Sept 24, 2021 start of the first production run of the Eli Zero NEV with European partners.
wikis.body:
- Sept 24, 2021 (Paul Ridden): Los Angeles-based Eli Electric Vehicles announced the Zero in 2018; an initial production run has now started with manufacturing partners in Europe.
- NEV: top speed 25 mph (40 km/h); Eli says legal on most roads with a 35-mph limit.
- Changes from the 2018 prototype: 72-V architecture (was 48 V), power steering and braking, reversing camera, dual-beam LED headlight, redesigned chassis.
- 4-kW rear-drive motor; 5.8-kWh or 8-kWh battery for 50 or 70 miles (80/112 km). Size 88.6 x 54.3 x 62.5 in; 23.6-ft turning circle; aluminum chassis; 160 liters trunk; 7-inch digital dash; tilting sunroof; two of three configurations have hot/cold AC.
- Homologated late 2020; production-ready earlier in 2021. Shipments to first European distributors expected in the coming weeks; US launch planned "in the near future".
- Second equity crowdfunding on StartEngine launched; first closed July 30 with nearly US$1.4 million from over 1,500 investors.

wikis.title: NASA pays the price of a massive, expensive rocket (SLS delay)
wikis.summary: Ars Technica's May 12, 2017 analysis of why NASA's Space Launch System is likely at least three years late and over budget.
wikis.body:
- May 12, 2017 (Eric Berger). NASA's acting administrator Robert Lightfoot and human spaceflight chief William Gerstenmaier announced completion of a study on adding crew to the first SLS launch (after Trump advisers asked NASA to consider a splashy first-term achievement).
- Result: technically feasible but would cost $600 million to $900 million above the existing budget and would not appreciably advance long-term deep-space goals. Lightfoot: "We're in this for the long haul."
- SLS was born in the 2010 authorization bill signed Oct 11, 2010, mandating launch of the rocket and Orion by December 31, 2016; that slipped to 2017, then to a September-November 2018 target. NASA now says not before 2019 and needs one or two months to finalize; Ars heard from two sources November 2019 for the uncrewed launch.
- Cost: about $10 billion through next year. A 2011 Booz Allen Hamilton analysis warned of "unjustified cost reductions"; the President's budget typically offered about $1.3 billion a year while Congress appropriated $2 billion for SLS.
