wikis.title: KONE reopens its mine elevator test laboratory in Tytyri, Finland
wikis.summary: Elevator Today report of 29 March 2017 on KONE's renewed high-rise elevator test lab in a working limestone mine in Tytyri, 350 m deep.
wikis.body:
- KONE unveiled its renewed high-rise elevator test facility in Tytyri, Finland, after extensive renovations. It reaches 350 meters depth, is part of a working limestone mine and hosts the world's deepest elevator test shaft.
- 11 elevator shafts with combined length of 1.6 km: seven for super-tall and mega-tall testing, four for mid- and low-rise.
- Tests: speeds up to 70 km/hour (about 19 m/s) at conventional acceleration; free-fall tests up to 90 km/hour (26 m/s). Free-fall test drops a 10,000 kg elevator frame into a 200 meter shaft to test safety gear.
- Used to test the carbon fiber hoisting technology KONE UltraRope, ride comfort, aerodynamics and robot-aided installation.
- The Tytyri lab first opened in 1997; part of a global test network at seven R&D sites in Finland, Italy, China, USA, Mexico and India.
- Quote, CTO Tomio Pihkala: "At Tytyri we can push the limits of elevator physics like at no other place in the world."

wikis.title: Antwerp Port House by Zaha Hadid Architects (ArchDaily)
wikis.summary: ArchDaily project page for the Antwerp Port House, published 22 September 2016, with specs and a short architect description.
wikis.body:
- Antwerp Port House, Antwerp, Belgium; architects Zaha Hadid Architects; area 12,800 m2; year 2016. Category: port, institutional buildings, refurbishment.
- Design: Zaha Hadid and Patrik Schumacher; ZHA project director Joris Pauwels, project architect Jinmi Lee. Executive architect Bureau Bouwtechniek; structural engineers Studieburo Mouton; acoustic engineers Daidalos Peutz; services engineers Ingenium nv.
- Photographs by Hufton+Crow and Tim Fischer.
- Architects' text: it "repurposes, renovates and extends a derelict fire station into a new headquarters for the port", bringing together the port's 500 staff who previously worked in separate buildings around the city.

wikis.title: Port Authority Building (Antwerp) (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Encyclopedia entry on Zaha Hadid's Port House (Havenhuis) in Antwerp, headquarters of the Antwerp Port Authority.
wikis.body:
- Government building at Zaha Hadidplein 1, Eilandje, Port of Antwerp; built 2009 to 2016; construction of the expansion began October 2012; officially opened September 2016, the year of Hadid's death. Sole government building she designed. Floor area 12,800 m2; height 46 m; owner Port of Antwerp.
- Houses about 500 staff. In 2007 port authorities determined a new location would house technical and administrative services together.
- The lower part is a disused fire station, a protected replica of a Hanseatic house, which had to be preserved ("the original building had to be preserved", Marc Van Peel). Five shortlisted candidates all added a modern structure on top; ZHA's design was chosen.
- Design: glass-covered diamond-shaped extension over 100 m long, resembling a ship's hull with protruding bow, transparent and opaque triangular facets; references water and the diamond industry. Concrete pillars and 900 tonnes of steel carry it; a bridge level joins the two structures.
- Energy: BREEAM 'Very Good'; borehole system to 80 metres depth at over 100 locations for heating and cooling. Quay named Zaha Hadidplein by the city council.
- Port of Antwerp described as Europe's second largest by traffic, 26% of Europe's container shipping.

wikis.title: Engineering the Antwerp Port House (The B1M)
wikis.summary: The B1M video page (5 October 2016) on how Zaha Hadid Architects extended a heritage fire station into the Antwerp Port Authority headquarters.
wikis.body:
- Video hosted by Tom Payne, 5 October 2016; 56,006 views listed.
- Port Authority grouped technical and administrative services into one HQ on the docklands: a protected replica of a Hanseatic House and former fire station plus a new extension, for about 500 staff.
- Historical studies by ZHA showed a central spire planned but never built; to keep all four original facades, they extended vertically with a four-storey beam-shaped form. Multi-faceted glass echoes waterways and Antwerp's diamond industry.
- Construction: new foundations in the courtyard and beside the southern facade; two concrete towers built and bridged; steel superstructure assembled in two phases; concrete floors poured; clad; below-ground garage for vehicles and cycles.
- Building named after Zaha Hadid, one of several projects begun but not completed in her lifetime. Staff work flexibly.

wikis.title: Contractor Pizzarotti sues Fortis over alignment issues at 161 Maiden Lane
wikis.summary: The Real Deal report of 3 April 2019 on a lawsuit claiming Fortis's 58-story Seaport tower at 161 Maiden Lane is leaning three inches north.
wikis.body:
- Pizzarotti, general contractor for Fortis Property Group's 58-story condo at 161 Maiden Lane, sued in New York County Supreme Court (March 2019), alleging foundation work by a previous contractor using a cheaper "soil improvement" method causes issues with structure, facade, waterproofing and elevators. Building said to lean three inches north.
- Fortis denies it: the lawsuit is "patently false from start to finish"; says Arup and WSP certified no safety issues and only a slight curtain wall redesign is needed; new general contractor is Ray Builders.
- Dispute over who terminated: Pizzarotti says it gave notice on 1 March; Fortis says it sent termination notice last week.
- Project long delayed, largely by concrete slab pours; Pizzarotti replaced SCC Concrete last year after a worker fell to his death from the 29th floor; RC Structures took over and reported the structural issues per the complaint.
- Pizzarotti (Italy-based) is also partnering with Madison Equities on 45 Broad Street.

wikis.title: The Leaning Tower of the Seaport: contractor sues Fortis (Bisnow)
wikis.summary: Bisnow report of 4 April 2019 on Pizzarotti's lawsuit claiming Fortis's 161 Maiden Lane condo tower is leaning three inches.
wikis.body:
- Pizzarotti, contractor since 2015 on Fortis Property Group's Lower Manhattan apartment building at 161 Maiden Lane, sued Fortis in New York State Supreme Court, claiming the tower is leaning 3 inches north. Suit: "there are structural issues, unusual settlement up to three inches".
- Determination made by a concrete company recently hired. Previous concrete contractor SSC High Rise Construction pleaded guilty to manslaughter after a worker fell to his death on the site.
- Pizzarotti alleges Fortis avoided driving piles, using a cheaper remediation method; says the building will keep moving unless changes are made and fears parts of the facade could fall. It terminated its contract 1 March.
- Fortis spokesman: the lawsuit is "patently false from start to finish" and a "desperate attempt by a failing general contractor"; says the building is still safe.

wikis.title: Mont d'Ambin Base Tunnel (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Encyclopedia entry on the 57.5 km Mont d'Ambin (Mont Cenis) Base Tunnel of the Lyon-Turin rail link, under construction with opening scheduled for 2033.
wikis.body:
- Twin-tube, double-track rail tunnel through the Alps between Maurienne (France) and the Susa Valley (Italy); part of the Turin-Lyon high-speed railway. Length 57.5 km, which would make it the world's longest rail tunnel, ahead of Gotthard (57.1 km). Status: under construction; work began 2002, constructed 2019-present; "As of July 2024" expected completion 2033.
- Estimated cost EUR 8 billion (January 2018 value), roughly one third of the whole project. EU agreed to finance 40% and is willing to go to 55%. A 2012 French Court of Audit report questioned cost and traffic estimates.
- Design speeds: passenger 220 km/h, freight 100 km/h; 25 kV 50 Hz AC; max elevation 580 m.
- History: reconnaissance work from 2002 on the French side; September 2016 France-Italy agreement; January 2017 treaty ratified; July 2020 a Vinci Construction Grands Projets-led consortium awarded major elements incl. four Avrieux shafts up to 500 m deep. Eight TBMs are to be used; a 9 km reconnaissance gallery was completed 2016 to 2017. Length increased from 52 to 57.5 km after protests over the original Susa Valley alignment.
- July 2021 contracts: Lot 1 EUR 1.47 billion (22 km, 72 months); Lot 2 EUR 1.43 billion (23 km, 65 months); Lot 3 EUR 228 million (3 km, all blasting, 70 months).
- Opposition mainly the No TAV movement.

wikis.title: Japan's tallest skyscraper completed in Tokyo (CNN)
wikis.summary: CNN Style article of 4 July 2023 on the completion of the 330 m Azabudai Hills Mori JP Tower, Japan's new tallest building.
wikis.body:
- Tower reaches 330 meters (1,083 feet) with 64 floors above ground, surpassing Osaka's Abeno Harukas (300 m). Completion announced Monday; Azabudai Hills complex scheduled to open in the fall; under construction since 2019 with "final touches" left, per developer Mori Building Co.
- Multi-purpose: branded hotel residences, offices, a university medical center, shops, restaurants and the largest international school in central Tokyo. Site over 8 hectares; also spa, fitness clubs, art gallery and museum; "city within a city". Expected to house about 20,000 employees and 3,500 residents, with 25-35 million visitors per year projected.
- Towers designed by Pelli Clarke & Partners; Heatherwick Studio designed one low-rise structure.
- A nearby 390 m Torch Tower is due to complete in 2027.

wikis.title: Mori JP Tower on The Skyscraper Center
wikis.summary: Skyscraper Center database entry for Mori JP Tower (Azabudai Hills Main Tower), Tokyo, with only public facts visible because most data requires CVU membership.
wikis.body:
- Official name Mori JP Tower; other names: Tora Asa, Azabudai Hills Main Tower, Toranomon-Azabudai District Main Tower, Aman Residences. Complex: Azabudai Hills. Address Azabudai 1-chome, Minato Ward, Tokyo, Japan.
- Height 327.2 m / 1,073 ft; 65 floors; function residential / office; status completed, completion 2023. Developer Mori Building.
- Rankings: #145 tallest in the world, #95 in Asia, #1 in Japan, #1 in Tokyo.
- Schedule: 2017 proposed; 2019 construction start; 2023 completed.
- Images by Jason O'Rear, Pelli Clarke & Partners, Bezier Studios and D-BOX. Much data (rankings by location, function, material, companies involved) is member-only.

wikis.title: Second tunnel boring machine begins excavating for the Western Harbour Tunnel
wikis.summary: NSW Government release of 11 August 2026 that TBM Barangaroo has launched to join Patyegarang on the final stretch of the Western Harbour Tunnel under Sydney Harbour.
wikis.body:
- Second TBM, Barangaroo, launched 44.7 metres below Birchgrove Oval, excavating the final section of twin tunnels between Birchgrove and Waverton. Sister TBM Patyegarang started "last month".
- Together they excavate the final 1.5 km beneath the harbour, completing tunnelling for the 6.5 km Western Harbour Tunnel.
- Each is 15.7 m in diameter and 4,350 tonnes, described as the largest ever assembled underground and largest in the Southern Hemisphere. They install about 13,000 pre-cast concrete segments and 1,300 20-tonne culverts made at Emu Plains; operate around the clock to depths up to 50 metres below sea level.
- Berry St on-ramp in North Sydney is nearing completion; mechanical and electrical fit-out in progress.
- Tunnel "remains on track to open in 2028"; expected to reduce traffic 35% on the Western Distributor, 20% in the Sydney Harbour Tunnel and 17% on the Sydney Harbour Bridge; remains in public hands. Minister for Roads Jenny Aitchison quoted.

wikis.title: Sydney's under-harbour Western Harbour Tunnel set to open in 2028 (Time Out)
wikis.summary: Time Out Sydney article of 9 June 2026 on construction progress of the 6.5 km Western Harbour Tunnel, with the first giant TBM about to start.
wikis.body:
- 6.5 km Western Harbour Tunnel due to open in 2028.
- First TBM Patyegarang preparing to tunnel 44.7 metres below Birchgrove Oval towards Waverton after final testing; 15.7 m diameter, 4,350 tonnes, biggest ever assembled underground in the Southern Hemisphere; will install around 13,000 pre-cast concrete segments.
- Second TBM Barangaroo (also named for a notable Aboriginal woman): assembly 94 per cent complete, tunnelling expected to begin within the month.
- They tackle the final 1.5 km beneath the harbour, to depths of up to 50 metres below sea level, around the clock with 40 workers on shift.
- Expected traffic reductions per NSW Government: Western Distributor 35 per cent, Sydney Harbour Tunnel 20 per cent, Harbour Bridge 17 per cent. Connects Warringah Freeway/North Sydney with WestConnex at Rozelle Interchange.

wikis.title: Mamdani will rebuild the BQE to last until 2080 (Streetsblog)
wikis.summary: Streetsblog NYC report of 24 August 2026 on Mayor Mamdani's plan to rebuild the BQE triple cantilever over 10 years using a temporary bypass rather than tearing it down.
wikis.body:
- Mayor Mamdani will not tear down the deteriorating triple-cantilevered BQE stretch and will rebuild it over 10 years with a temporary bypass structure; plan to be unveiled Monday (24 August 2026). Construction starts in 2030, wraps up in 2040, extending lifespan to 2080. Cost $4 billion.
- The city spends $160 million a year maintaining the structure; DOT says a shutdown would divert a "significant portion" of 130,000 daily car and truck trips onto local streets.
- Bypass: temporary two-tiered highway along Furman Street beside the 0.4-mile cantilever, between Atlantic Avenue and Columbia Heights, continuing over the Brooklyn Bridge approach at Vine Street (exact route still under consideration). It does not expand the footprint; two lanes each direction, built about at the height of the northbound upper roadway, lower than the Promenade. Parts of the Promenade will close but stay partially open; Columbia Heights overpass rebuilt; parks affected include Squibb Park, Anchorage Plaza and Adam Yauch Park; DOT will ask the state to alienate parkland and vows to restore it.
- History: earlier plans fizzled under de Blasio (2018 six-lane plan) and Adams. City owns only the 1.5-mile portion between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Streets; the state owns the rest. A 2024 coalition of Brooklyn Heights residents and groups urged reimagining the corridor away from a highway.
- Quote, Mamdani: "we can no longer afford to wait for the perfect solution".

wikis.title: BQE Central Project (NYC DOT)
wikis.summary: NYC DOT project page describing the proposed rehabilitation of the 1.5-mile city-owned BQE Central, including the Triple Cantilever, with temporary bypasses.
wikis.body:
- BQE Central: about 1.5-mile City-owned section of the BQE (I-278) between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Street, Brooklyn; 12% of the BQE in Brooklyn; 21 bridges and structures, including the 0.4-mile "Triple Cantilever" (two highway levels, the Brooklyn Heights Promenade above, Furman Street below). Over 70 years old.
- Proposal: rehabilitation (repair and strengthen), not replacement: fix deck, walls, joints; improve drainage, lighting and railings. Extends life about 40 years (replacement would give 75+). Highway stays two lanes; interchanges not altered.
- Temporary bypasses: a two-level bypass over Furman Street from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights, no higher than the existing Queens-bound level; a Queens-bound-only bypass from Columbia Heights to just before the Manhattan Bridge over the BQE and Brooklyn Bridge approach. Alignments illustrative; removed after construction.
- Schedule: "Construction is expected to begin in 2029 and finish by 2040", including bypass building and dismantling. The project is preparing to enter CEQR environmental review.
- Need: inspections found cracked concrete, exposed steel, rust, water damage; highway kept safe by interim repairs, automated enforcement on overweight trucks and two lanes on the cantilever. 130,000 vehicles daily, including 13,000 trucks.
- Goals include protecting the Promenade and keeping the option to re-envision the full BQE corridor.

wikis.title: Miral announces SeaWorld Yas Island, Abu Dhabi opening on 23 May 2023
wikis.summary: Press release of 21 March 2023 announcing the opening date and eight realms of SeaWorld Yas Island, Abu Dhabi.
wikis.body:
- Miral announced (21 March 2023) that SeaWorld Yas Island, Abu Dhabi opens to the public on 23 May 2023; a collaboration between Miral and SeaWorld Parks & Entertainment; described as a next-generation marine life theme park with a "One Ocean" story.
- Eight realms: Abu Dhabi Ocean, One Ocean, MicroOcean, Endless Ocean, Tropical Ocean, Rocky Point, and Polar Ocean (Arctic and Antarctica). Explored across five indoor levels spanning approximately 183,000 m2; Endless Ocean is set to hold the world's largest and most expansive multi-species aquarium.
- Habitats designed to AZA and American Humane standards; systems include Advanced Animal Lighting System and Animal Life Support System.
- One Ocean realm has a 360-degree screen show, One Epic Ocean, and a view into the Animal Care Center. Abu Dhabi Ocean covers pearl diving heritage, dining (Matbakh Ummi) and a Souk, and starts the S.E.A Guardian park-wide game.
- Quotes: Miral chairman Mohamed Khalifa Al Mubarak; SeaWorld Parks chairman Scott Ross called it the "first SeaWorld outside of the United States".

wikis.title: SeaWorld Abu Dhabi (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Encyclopedia entry on the marine life theme park and rescue center that opened on 23 May 2023 on Yas Island, Abu Dhabi.
wikis.body:
- Opened 23 May 2023 on Yas Island; first SeaWorld park outside the US and first without orcas. Owned and operated by Miral under license from United Parks & Resorts.
- History: a 2007 proposed Dubai park was cancelled after the 2008 financial crisis; on 13 December 2016 a partnership with Miral was announced. In February 2023 the park received three captive walruses from parks in Canada.
- Eight realms (One Ocean hub with 360-degree screen; Abu Dhabi Ocean; Rocky Point; MicroOcean; Tropical Ocean; Arctic; Antarctica; Endless Ocean with 6.6 million saltwater gallons and 1,800 species). More than 15 rides, 13 retail options, 17 dining options and 150 species in text; infobox says 6 rides (as of November 2025), including Manta (Intamin launched coaster), Eel Racer and Hypersphere (Intamin dome theatre ride).
- Yas SeaWorld Research and Rescue opened February 2023, 8,602 m2, to rescue and rehabilitate marine animals in the Persian Gulf.
- 2024 attendance 1,750,000, ranked 18th in EMEA.

wikis.title: Iconic Tower, Egypt (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Encyclopedia entry on the 394 m Iconic Tower in Egypt's New Capital, completed 2024 as the tallest building in Africa.
wikis.body:
- Mixed-use supertall skyscraper in The New Capital of Egypt; architectural height 394 m (1,293 ft); 77 floors; floor area 265,000 m2. Tallest in Africa since 2024, overtaking Great Mosque of Algiers tower.
- Architect: Dar al-Handasah Shair & Partners (architect of record); developer/contractor CSCE (China State Construction Engineering), employing over 5,000 workers. Egyptian and modern style, inspired by a pharaonic obelisk, glass exterior representing Amun's Shuti crown.
- Timeline: excavation began May 2018 (construction start 2 May 2018); foundation concrete pour ceremony 25 February 2019 attended by PM Mostafa Madbouly; structural concrete complete July 2021; topped out 24 August 2021 at full height; completed 2024.
- Part of a plan led by the Egyptian Ministry of Housing that includes 20 high-rises in the complex around it.

wikis.title: Iconic Tower on The Skyscraper Center
wikis.summary: Skyscraper Center database entry for Iconic Tower, Cairo, with only public facts visible because most data requires CVU membership.
wikis.body:
- Height 393.8 m / 1,292 ft; 77 floors; official name Iconic Tower; complex: New Administrative Capital Central Business District; city Cairo, Egypt. Status completed; completion 2024.
- Rankings: #44 tallest in the world, #1 in Africa, #1 in Egypt, #1 in Cairo.
- Schedule: 2018 construction start; 2024 completed.
- Developer: Ministry of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities of Egypt. Images credited to China State Construction Engineering Corporation Ltd. and the New Urban Communities Authority.
- Many details are member-only.

wikis.title: Gothenburg City Gate (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Encyclopedia entry on the 144 m Gothenburg City Gate (Citygate) office skyscraper in the Garda district, built 2019 to 2022.
wikis.body:
- Office skyscraper at Fabriksgatan 2, Garda District, Gothenburg, Sweden; built 2019 to 2022; roof height 144 m (472 ft), 36 floors, floor area 42,000 m2. Third tallest building in Sweden and tallest office building in Scandinavia (Nordic region).
- Architect Henning Larsen Architects (with Kanozi Arkitekter); structural engineer VBK Konsulterande Ingenjorer; main contractor Skanska.
- Contains offices, a restaurant, cafe, co-working spaces, gym, bicycle hotel and garage. Built on the plot of a former gas station; named a city gate because it guides E6 and E20 highway traffic entering the town. WELL certified and LEED certified.

wikis.title: Citygate, Gothenburg (Skanska project page)
wikis.summary: Short Skanska project page for the completed Citygate office tower in Gothenburg, billed as the tallest office building in the Nordic region.
wikis.body:
- Project status: completed. Billed as "Tallest Office Building in the Nordic Region" and "a new landmark in Gothenburg", with views over the city from the top.
- Focus on well-being and healthier living and working; environmentally certified by LEED and WELL certified.
- Client: Egenutvecklat (self-developed); service: commercial development; segment: commercial offices; Gothenburg, Vastra Gotaland County, Sweden.

wikis.title: Vogtle Unit 4 enters commercial operation (Georgia Power)
wikis.summary: Georgia Power press release of 29 April 2024 that Plant Vogtle Unit 4 entered commercial operation, completing the Vogtle 3 and 4 expansion.
wikis.body:
- On 29 April 2024 Georgia Power declared Plant Vogtle Unit 4 in commercial operation; it can power an estimated 500,000 homes and businesses and provide emissions-free energy for at least 60 to 80 years. Unit 3 entered commercial operation on 31 July 2023.
- With all four units operating, Vogtle is described as the largest generator of clean energy in the nation, expected to produce more than 30 million megawatt hours a year. Operated by Southern Nuclear for co-owners Georgia Power, Oglethorpe Power, MEAG Power and Dalton Utilities.
- Described as the first newly constructed nuclear units in the U.S. in more than 30 years; more than 9,000 onsite jobs at the peak of construction. Nuclear provided more than 25% of Georgia Power's 2023 generation (Vogtle and Plant Hatch).
- Quotes: Kim Greene (Georgia Power CEO) and Chris Womack (Southern Company CEO, net zero by 2050 goal).

wikis.title: Plant Vogtle Unit 4 begins commercial operation
wikis.summary: EIA in-brief note that Vogtle Unit 4 in Georgia entered commercial operation, completing the 11-year expansion of the largest US nuclear plant.
wikis.body:
- EIA "In-brief analysis", May 1, 2024.
- Georgia Power announced that the 1,114-MW Unit 4 reactor at Plant Vogtle near Waynesboro, Georgia entered commercial operation after connecting to the grid in March 2024. This completes the 11-year expansion; no nuclear reactors are under construction in the US now.
- Unit 3 began commercial operation in July 2023. Units 1 and 2 (combined 2,430 MW nameplate) began operations in 1987 and 1989.
- Total capacity is nearly 5 GW, surpassing the 4,210-MW Palo Verde plant in Arizona, making Vogtle the largest US nuclear plant.
- Construction at the new units began in 2009. Originally expected to cost $14 billion and start in 2016 (Unit 3) and 2017 (Unit 4); delays and overruns mean Georgia Power now estimates more than $30 billion.
- Both use the Westinghouse AP1000 Generation III+ design with passive safety systems; they are the first and only US AP1000 deployments. Two other AP1000s planned in South Carolina were halted in 2017.
- US nuclear fleet: about 97 GW, nearly 19% of 2023 US electricity, second after natural gas (43%).

wikis.title: London Gatwick completes its main runway resurfacing
wikis.summary: VINCI Airports news release saying Gatwick resurfaced its main runway in Sept 2022 in half the time and cost using 70% less asphalt.
wikis.body:
- Dated 05 October 2022. London Gatwick, part of VINCI Airports, completed (Sept 2022) a plan to resurface its main runway in half the time and for half the cost, using 70% less asphalt than traditional methods.
- The original 2020 plan was halted by the pandemic; the airport then redesigned it.
- Only the most "trafficked" parts (landing and exit areas) were resurfaced, as other sections had seven to ten years of expected life.
- Both asphalt layers were laid in a single night rather than two nights.
- 40,000 tonnes of asphalt laid, 100,000 tonnes less than normal; project took six months (half the normal time) at 50% less cost.
- Old asphalt was recycled as aggregate in road construction; a temporary on-site batching plant cut lorry travel.
- Alasdair Scobie, Capital Delivery Director: "The pandemic gave us the time and reason to rethink our original design." Savings can be reinvested elsewhere in the airport.
- VINCI Airports operates more than 50 airports in 11 countries; committed to net zero across its network by 2050.

wikis.title: Groundbreaking ceremony held for new 2 World Trade Center
wikis.summary: NY1 report on the July 2026 groundbreaking of 2 WTC, the future American Express global headquarters.
wikis.body:
- NY1 (Olivia Quinones), published Jul. 09, 2026: a groundbreaking ceremony was held Thursday for the new 2 World Trade Center.
- Per officials it will be the final commercial office tower on the World Trade Center Campus and the new global headquarters for American Express, which will be the only owner and occupant (per governor's office release).
- Expected to create more than 3,200 construction jobs and invest almost $6 billion in NYC's economy, per Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Expected completion in 2031.
- Once finished, expected to support more than 20,000 jobs; Mamdani: "this headquarters will contribute roughly $11.4 billion towards our economy, including nearly $250 million in tax revenue".
- Gov. Kathy Hochul called it "a shining symbol of the resilience, excellence and opportunity that defines Lower Manhattan".

wikis.title: Four (Frankfurt) mixed-use skyscraper complex
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Four Frankfurt, a four-tower mixed-use development on the former Deutsche Bank site, designed by UNStudio.
wikis.body:
- Mixed-use complex of four towers in Frankfurt's Deutsche Bank triangle (Innenstadt). Infobox status: Completed; opened 2025 (article text still says "under construction" and estimated completion 2024/2025). Construction started 2018 (complex), 2021 (tallest tower).
- Heights: Tower 1 233 m (59 floors), Tower 2 179 m (50), Tower 3 128 m (33), Tower 4 105 m (25; text says 104 m). 53 elevators. Tower 1 has the highest usable floor in Frankfurt.
- Architect Ben van Berkel / UNStudio with HPP Architects; developer Groß & Partner. Projected cost around one billion euros.
- Site: 16,159 m2, formerly the Deutsche Bank IBCF tower (completed 1971, demolished 2018). Sold to Groß & Partner, announced November 2015, price undisclosed. Design competition March 2016 won by UNStudio.
- Earlier history: 1999 competition; Murphy/Jahn's 228 m "MAX" tower chosen in 2000 but doubted after 9/11.
- Uses: office space for ~4,000 people, 600 residential units, subsidized housing, retail, restaurants, two hotels (Kimpton, Radisson Collection). Towers 1 and 4 mainly offices (tenants DekaBank, Boston Consulting Group, Baker McKenzie); towers 2 and 3 mainly residential. Penthouses up to 1000 sqm selling for up to 20 million euros.
- Towers connected by a multi-storey plinth; planned roof garden and city square.

wikis.title: The Exchange TRX opens to the public in Kuala Lumpur
wikis.summary: Lendlease release (29 Nov 2023) announcing the opening of The Exchange TRX mall and TRX City Park in Kuala Lumpur.
wikis.body:
- Kuala Lumpur, 29 November 2023: The Exchange TRX opened, part of the 17-acre TRX lifestyle quarter in Malaysia's first dedicated international financial district.
- More than 400 stores across 1.3 million sq ft nett lettable area; first Malaysian retail asset with LEED Gold Certification.
- 10-acre rooftop TRX City Park, free and open year round, "the first major green space in the city in over two decades", over 150,000 plantings, 95% native or naturalised.
- Jointly developed by Lendlease and TRX City Sdn Bhd. Quotes from Mitch Wilson (Lendlease Malaysia) and TRX City CEO Dato' Azmar Talib.
- Five dining precincts: Food Exchange, Concourse Dining, Park Dining, Premium Dining, Dining Terrace. Shake Shack's first Malaysian store; also Bacha Coffee, Venchi, Kanbe Ramen, Paolo Paolo Gelato.
- National debuts include Gentle Monster, Alo Yoga, Molton Brown; also Louis Vuitton, Chanel, Gucci, and the largest HOKA store in Kuala Lumpur.
- Partnered with Podium Property Insights for retail data; adjoins Tun Razak Exchange MRT Station.

wikis.title: The Exchange TRX (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on The Exchange TRX shopping mall in Kuala Lumpur: development, tenants, rooftop park, access and opening problems.
wikis.body:
- Shopping mall in Tun Razak Exchange, Kuala Lumpur; opened 29 November 2023; 400+ stores; 1,300,000 sq ft; 5 floors, 3 parking levels. Anchors: Apple, Seibu, Aurum Theatre (Golden Screen Cinemas), Mercato.
- Developer Lendlease (60%) with TRX City Sdn Bhd (formerly 1MDB Real Estate). Construction began 2017; expected completion Q3 2021 but delayed by COVID-19 Movement Control Order.
- Includes Kimpton hotel block, office block, six residential towers nearby. June 2022 partnership integrated the mall with The Exchange 106 retail podium (70 units) via the "106 Connection".
- Malaysia's first Apple Store opened 22 June 2024, Apple's sixth in Southeast Asia.
- 10-acre TRX City Park on Level 3, owned by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and managed by TRX; Shake Shack and % Arabica have first Malaysian outlets there.
- Directly linked to Tun Razak Exchange MRT station; district loop tunnel has 3 levels.
- Incidents: tower crane jib fell during a storm 13 April 2021 (no injuries); first-week defects (cracked tiles, escalator/elevator faults), power outage on the second day, water play area closed for repair.

wikis.title: Xi'an International Football Center
wikis.summary: Wikipedia stub on the 60,235-seat stadium in Xi'an, China, opened September 2025.
wikis.body:
- Also called Fengdong Stadium, in Xi'an, Shaanxi. Capacity 60,235; record attendance 43,937. Cost ¥2.5 billion. Architect Zaha Hadid Architects; contractor Shaanxi Construction Engineering Group.
- Groundbreaking 2020, built 2020-2023 (text: completed 2025), opened September 3, 2025. Initially planned for the 2023 AFC Asian Cup, which China pulled out of hosting.
- Home of China League One club Shaanxi Union (2026-present).
- First official match 3 September 2025: China beat Timor-Leste 2-1 in 2026 AFC U-23 Asian Cup Qualifiers. Hosted the 2026 Team China Xi'an International Youth Football Tournament, 25-31 March 2026.

wikis.title: Xi'an International Football Center by Zaha Hadid Architects + iDEA + AISA (ArchDaily)
wikis.summary: ArchDaily project page for the 60,000-seat Xi'an International Football Center, giving credits, area (251,000 m2), year (2025) and its first matches.
wikis.body:
- Published on ArchDaily November 24, 2025. Football stadium in Xi'an, China; year 2025; area 251,000 m2; photographs Hufton+Crow.
- Architects: Arcplus Institute of Shanghai Architectural Design & Research (executive architect), Zaha Hadid Architects (ZHA principal Patrik Schumacher), iDEA (local architect and landscape). Structural engineers AISA, Schlaich Bergermann Partner, Qiang Chang; lighting Lichtvision; general contractor Shaanxi Construction Engineering Group; facade by FORCITIS and Zhejiang Yasha.
- Architects' text: the centre "has hosted its inaugural international matches" with China's U-23 team facing Australia, Timor-Leste and Northern Mariana Islands in Group D qualifiers for the 2026 Asian Cup finals to be held in Saudi Arabia.
- The 60,000-seat stadium and training grounds are described as integral to football development in China, initiated by the Chinese Football Association and national sports bodies, from international competition to grassroots and youth academies.

wikis.title: Century-old Loop skyscrapers to be preserved, federal agency decides
wikis.summary: Chicago Sun-Times report that the GSA chose to reuse rather than demolish the Century and Consumers buildings on State Street.
wikis.body:
- Chicago Sun-Times, by Kade Heather, URL dated 2024/08/02: the US General Services Administration released its final environmental impact report on Friday, choosing adaptive reuse of the Century (202 S. State St.) and Consumers (220 S. State St.) buildings and the smaller 214 S. State St. building, scrapping demolition plans.
- In 2022 Congress earmarked $52 million for demolition; the federal government argued the buildings posed a security risk to the Dirksen Federal Building behind them (security buffer zone acquired after a 2005 bombing attempt).
- Both are on the National Register of Historic Places and in the Loop Retail Historic District; last year the Commission on Chicago Landmarks unanimously recommended landmark designation.
- Century: 16 stories, opened 1915, Holabird & Roche. Consumers: 22 stories, opened 1913, Jenney, Mundie & Jensen. 214 S. State: four stories, believed built 1883 (architect C.M. Palmer, for Gunther's Confectionary).
- Preservation Chicago had lined up 20 religious orders interested in a proposed Chicago Collaborative Archive Center.
- A record of the decision will be issued in September, followed by a GSA request for lease proposals.

wikis.title: What commuters can expect from Hong Kong's cross-harbour rail section opening May 15
wikis.summary: SCMP explainer (5 May 2022) on the Hung Hom-Admiralty cross-harbour section of the Sha Tin to Central link (teaser only).
wikis.body:
- SCMP, Cannix Yau, published 5 May 2022. The Hung Hom-Admiralty section of the Sha Tin to Central link, "Hong Kong's most expensive rail project yet", will fully open on May 15, ending a saga "plagued by shoddy work, repeated delays and cost overruns".
- Journeys between Tai Wai and Admiralty on the East Rail line are expected to take only 17 minutes without changing lines; smart facilities help passengers pick faster routes or train cars with more space.
- The extension runs East Rail from Hung Hom to Admiralty via the new Exhibition Centre stop at Wan Chai North, making the line 46 km with 16 stations and the fourth cross-harbour route directly linking the northeastern New Territories, central Kowloon and Hong Kong Island.
- Text is cut off (paywall) after the first question.

wikis.title: Sha Tin to Central Link (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Hong Kong's Sha Tin to Central Link heavy rail project, its two phases, history, costs and delays.
wikis.body:
- MTR heavy rail project owned by KCR Corporation, operated by MTR Corporation; 17 km line (infobox); depots Tai Wai, Hung Hom, Pat Heung.
- Phase 1 became the Tuen Ma line: opened 14 February 2020 (Tai Wai-Kai Tak) and 27 June 2021 (Kai Tak-Hung Hom, delayed); West Rail line closed 27 June 2021 (absorbed). Phase 2 extended East Rail line from Hung Hom to Admiralty via new Exhibition Centre station, opened 15 May 2022.
- Kwun Tong line extension to Whampoa (opened 23 October 2016) was done in conjunction but is not a direct component.
- History: route roughly follows the East Kowloon line proposed in the late 1960s; in Railway Development Strategy 2000. 25 June 2002 KCRC won the bid over MTRC. Modified proposals 2005 and 2007 (after MTR-KCR merger on 2 December 2007).
- Cost: government funds required HK$37.4 billion (as first stated); Executive Council approved a construction cost of HK$79.8 billion in March 2012; construction began 22 June 2012.
- Delays: Nov 2014, at least 11 more months due to archaeological work at To Kwa Wan (now Sung Wong Toi) and extra enabling works at Exhibition Centre; then further delayed by construction quality problems at Hung Hom station (whistleblowing 2018; a Commission of Inquiry appointed).

wikis.title: Bakauheni-Terbanggi Besar Toll Road
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 140.98 km Trans-Sumatra toll road section in Lampung, Indonesia.
wikis.body:
- Controlled-access toll road linking Port of Bakauheni to Terbanggi Besar in Lampung, Indonesia; length 140.98 km (text: 140.9 km); part of the Trans-Sumatra Toll Road and AH25; maintained by PT Hutama Karya. Two lanes each direction, nine interchanges.
- Construction inaugurated 30 April 2015 by President Joko Widodo. Existed 2018-present; also named Drs. H. M. Adeham M.Pd. Memorial Lampung Toll Road.
- Sections: 1 Bakauheni-Sidomulyo (39 km), 2 Sidomulyo-Kotabaru (40 km), 3 Kotabaru-Metro (30 km), 4 Metro-Terbanggi Besar.
- Progress: on 21 January 2018 nine km from the port to Bakauheni Interchange and five km from Lematang to Kota Baru Interchange were operating; the rest of section 2 and sections 3 and 4 operated on March 8, 2019. Predicted daily traffic (5 Jan 2018): 16,097 vehicles/day.
- Toll gates include Bakauheni Selatan (5 booths), Lematang (6), Natar (6), Terbanggi Besar (4).

wikis.title: President inaugurates Bakauheni-Terbanggi Besar toll road (Setneg)
wikis.summary: Indonesian State Secretariat report (8 March 2019, in Indonesian) on Jokowi inaugurating the 140.9 km Trans-Sumatra toll section in Lampung.
wikis.body:
- Sekretariat Negara, Friday 8 March 2019: President Joko Widodo inaugurated the 140.9 km Bakauheni-Terbanggi Besar section of the Trans-Sumatra Toll Road in Lampung at the Natar toll gate, South Lampung.
- Attended by First Lady Iriana, SOE Minister Rini Soemarno, Public Works Minister Basuki Hadimuljono, Cabinet Secretary Pramono Anung, Transport Minister Budi Karya Sumadi.
- The toll road is to continue to Palembang, expected done "next June", making it about 350 km. President: "2024 Lampung to Aceh will be connected." The Banda Aceh-Sigli groundbreaking was on 14 December 2018.
- He expects the road to trigger investment and tourism; praised Lampung's fast land acquisition and permits (SIUP free and one day; building permits (IMB) in 3 days to a week).

wikis.title: Denver International Airport unveils final phase of Great Hall renovation
wikis.summary: CBS Colorado report (18 Feb 2025) on DEN's Great Hall renovation final phase, cost, timeline and future projects.
wikis.body:
- CBS Colorado, Austen Erblat, updated February 18, 2025. CEO Phil Washington unveiled plans/renderings for the final phase of the Great Hall Project in Jeppesen Terminal; airport says work will finish on time and on budget in 2027, though cost and timeline "have changed several times" in recent years.
- Total cost now expected to be below $1.3 billion. Renovations began in 2018, phase three in 2021; a 2023 city auditor report warned of overspending; a new contractor was hired in 2020 after terminating the previous one.
- Completion budget is "mostly local funding" with some federal dollars for baggage modernization.
- Future projects: seventh runway, Concourse C West extension with 11 gates, Peña Boulevard improvements (11-mile road, traffic up 80% since 1995, environmental study pending), 17,500-vehicle rental car facility, more baggage carousels, expanded international arrivals, 14 new train cars.
- 2023 passengers just under 78 million; projected 120 million by 2045.

wikis.title: How the Palace Theatre ended up 30 feet above Manhattan
wikis.summary: Commercial Observer (9 May 2022) on raising the landmarked Palace Theatre 30 feet as part of the TSX Broadway tower.
wikis.body:
- Commercial Observer, Rebecca Baird-Remba, May 9, 2022. Between January and May 2022 engineers and contractors working with L&L Holding raised the Palace Theatre 30 feet, at six inches an hour over roughly 17 days, in fits and starts.
- The theatre weighs 14 million pounds; 34 hydraulic lifting posts with jacks pushed up a ring beam; system designed by Urban Foundation Engineering.
- Part of L&L's $2.5 billion TSX Broadway hotel and retail tower at 47th Street and Broadway, Times Square: 46 stories, 550,000 sq ft, 600-key hotel, 100,000 sq ft retail/entertainment, 51,000 sq ft LED signage; "complete in early 2023".
- The 1,650-seat theatre gets a $50 million renovation: 1,657 new seats, expanded lobby, new marquee and entrance, restored plaster and chandelier; grows from 40,000 to 80,000 sq ft.
- Next: column extensions from first to third floor, then load transferred from lift posts to permanent structure (L&L's Domenick DeNizo).

wikis.title: Palace Theatre completes lifting as part of TSX Broadway project
wikis.summary: BroadwayWorld (5 May 2022) note that the Palace Theatre's lift is complete, with background on the theatre's history.
wikis.body:
- BroadwayWorld, May 05, 2022, citing New York YIMBY: the lifting of the Palace Theatre is complete, its new position 30 feet above street level within the podium of the 47-story Times Square hotel tower (TSX Broadway).
- Lift designed to free the ground level for retail; the tower will also have hotel rooms, restaurants and a stage facing Times Square. Next phase: restoration by PBDW Architects.
- TSX Broadway designed by Perkins Eastman and Mancini Duffy; developed by L&L Holding Company and Fortress Investment Group.
- Theatre history: last home of The SpongeBob Musical (2018); designed by Kirchoff & Rose, funded by Martin Beck, opened 1913; flagship vaudeville house to about 1929; RKO movie palace in the 1930s; Nederlander Organization bought it in 1965; renovation 1987-1991 replaced the original building with the DoubleTree Suites Times Square Hotel, itself demolished in 2019 for TSX Broadway.

wikis.title: NGV receives $74m for Australia's largest contemporary art museum
wikis.summary: The Art Newspaper (22 April 2022) on the A$100m Fox donation for The Fox: NGV Contemporary in Melbourne.
wikis.body:
- The Art Newspaper, Gabriella Angeleti, 22 April 2022. The National Gallery of Victoria received an A$100m ($74m) donation from Lindsay and Paula Fox for a new building expected to be Australia's largest contemporary art museum, to be called The Fox: NGV Contemporary; the largest gift by a living private donor to an Australian museum.
- About 30,000 sq m on Melbourne's southbank, designed by Sydney-based Angelo Candalepas and Associates, with about 13,000 sq m of exhibition space, rooftop terrace, conservation labs and education centre. Slated to open in 2028.
- Supplemented in part by a A$1.7bn ($1.3bn) grant made in 2020 by the Victorian government for the arts precinct.
- NGV director Tony Ellwood called the gift "awe-inspiring".

wikis.title: Victoria unveils winning NGV Contemporary design
wikis.summary: The Urban Developer (15 Mar 2022) on Angelo Candalepas and Associates winning the NGV Contemporary design competition.
wikis.body:
- The Urban Developer, Ted Tabet, Tue 15 Mar 22. Victorian government announced the winning design for a new contemporary art museum at 77 Southbank Boulevard, centrepiece of a $1.7 billion revamp of the Southbank arts precinct.
- Winner Angelo Candalepas and Associates with 20 Victorian and Australian firms, chosen from four shortlisted teams (others led by Open Weave, John Wardle Architects, Field). Jury headed by Corbett Lyon, Jill Garner and Tony Ellwood.
- Design: 13,000 sq m gallery, rooftop sculpture terrace and restaurant, central spherical hall rising more than 40 metres, arched entries, conservation laboratories.
- Expected to generate more than 11,000 jobs; state committed $1.4 billion in the 2020-21 budget; early works within the next year, completion expected by 2028.
- Wider precinct: new 18,000 sq m public space by Hassell and So-il, Arts Centre Melbourne Theatres upgrade by NH Architecture and Snohetta, later a Centre for Creativity.

wikis.title: The Spiral (New York City)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on The Spiral (66 Hudson Boulevard), a 66-floor, 1,031-foot BIG-designed skyscraper in Hudson Yards, opened 2023.
wikis.body:
- Also 66 Hudson Boulevard; former names Hudson Spire, 509 West 34th Street. 66 floors, 1,031 ft (314 m), 2.85 million sq ft. Architect Bjarke Ingels Group (AAI Architects as architect of record); developer Tishman Speyer; contractor Turner Construction. Construction started 2018, topped out January 2021, opened 2023.
- Named for outdoor gardens spiralling up the facade. Interiors by Space Copenhagen; Bosch irrigation system designed to save 4.5 million gallons of water per year.
- History: conceptualized 2014 as Hudson Spire (1,800 ft roof, marketed as tallest in the Western Hemisphere). Tishman Speyer spent $438 million on the site and paid $25 million to two residents to relocate (late 2015). Plans filed September 2016; April 2018 Blackstone-managed REIT provided a $1.8 billion loan.
- March 2023 CoStar Impact Award; January 2025 a $2.85 billion five-year fixed-rate refinancing (after seeking $3 billion).
- Tenants: HSBC (floors 3-5), Pfizer (7-21), AllianceBernstein (25-28), Marshall Wace (32-33), Turner Construction (35-36), Debevoise & Plimpton (40-52), NewYork-Presbyterian Och Spine Center (floor 2), among others.

wikis.title: China reaffirms ban on skyscrapers taller than 500m
wikis.summary: Global Times (2 Nov 2021) on China's rules banning buildings over 500 m and limiting 150 m and 250 m towers by city size.
wikis.body:
- Global Times, Nov 02, 2021. China reaffirmed a ban on skyscrapers taller than 500 m, citing pragmatic and security risk factors.
- Per MOHURD and the Ministry of Emergency Management (statement of October 26): no buildings over 150 m in cities with fewer than 3 million people; none over 250 m in larger cities.
- CTBUH statistics quoted: China has 2,581 buildings over 150 m, 861 over 200 m and 99 over 300 m, all first in the world.
- Deputy minister Huang Yan said problems have emerged in construction cost, energy consumption, security risks and environmental protection.
- In May the 356 m Saige building in downtown Shenzhen repeatedly shook and suspended operation for nearly four months.
- April 2020 MOHURD/NDRC document on urban architecture; NDRC regulation in April 2021 restricting 500 m+ towers and "ugly buildings"; "not until the beginning of July that NDRC officially banned" super high-rises over 500 m.

wikis.title: China's NDRC issues guidelines to ban construction of skyscrapers over 500m
wikis.summary: World Construction Network (13 July 2022) on NDRC guidelines banning 500 m+ skyscrapers and restricting those over 250 m.
wikis.body:
- WCN Editorial Team, July 13, 2022, reporting Global Times: China's NDRC released guidelines banning skyscrapers over 500 m and strictly restricting buildings over 250 m, in the new urbanisation outline under the 14th Five-Year Plan 2021-25, to enhance city landscape and restrict extreme architectural scale.
- CTBUH figures cited: 2,928 buildings over 150 m, 953 over 200 m, 102 over 300 m.
- In May 2021, the 356 m SEG Plaza in Shenzhen swayed and was suspended from use for four months.
- Last October, cities under 3 million people were restricted from building above 150 m (special exemption needed); larger cities above 250 m; exemptions possible for 250-500 m. Ministries said "lifelong accountability" would apply to officials approving non-compliant projects.

wikis.title: Russia's costly success: Nord Stream 2 construction is complete
wikis.summary: OSW Centre for Eastern Studies analysis (9 Sept 2021) of Nord Stream 2 pipe-laying completion, delays, costs and remaining hurdles.
wikis.body:
- OSW analysis by Szymon Kardaś, 2021-09-09. On 6 September Nord Stream 2 AG (100% Gazprom) announced completion of pipe laying for the second branch; the first line was finalised in June and was being tested.
- Project inaugurated June 2015; planned laying April 2018-December 2019, actual September 2018-September 2021, more than two years late. Official budget not to exceed EUR 10 billion; Sberbank analysts in 2018 said costs could reach around EUR 14.5 billion, likely higher.
- Causes of delay: Polish antimonopoly proceedings forcing consortium termination; slow permits (Denmark decided only end of October 2019, after a third application); US sanctions of December 2019 suspended work for nearly 12 months (Allseas halted).
- Still to do: German regulator certification (application in June 2021, may last until January 2022), Danish-waters certification, EU gas directive (April 2019) unbundling and third-party access; BNetzA refused a derogation in May 2020 and a Düsseldorf court upheld it on 25 August 2021.
- Analysis says the launch date is unclear despite talk of 2021.

wikis.title: Second Ave Subway opens, but future work remains
wikis.summary: Eno Center (5 Jan 2017) on the January 1, 2017 opening of the first phase of the Second Avenue Subway and its cost and funding questions.
wikis.body:
- Eno Center for Transportation, Emily Han, January 5, 2017. The Second Avenue Subway opened to passengers at noon on January 1st, extending the Q line with three stations at 72nd, 86th and 96th Streets, Upper East Side.
- Construction began 2002; total cost $4.45 billion (excluding future phases); initial proposal in the 1920s. First phase is about 2 miles, i.e. $2.2 billion per mile. It is one of four phases; the full line runs from 125th Street to Hanover Square.
- Funding not secured for phase two to 125th Street, projected $6 billion. Article raises equity concerns and notes the WTC PATH station cost $4 billion, double the original.
- New stations have wheelchair-accessible elevators, but the elevators are slow. MTA chief Tom Prendergast announced he would retire.

wikis.title: High-speed rail in Egypt (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Egypt's planned 2,000 km high-speed rail network led by Siemens, with three lines and 2027 targets.
wikis.body:
- Egypt has no operational high-speed rail; a project launched in 2018 for three lines totalling about 2,000 km. Dates of operation 2027; standard gauge; design speed 250 km/h, normal service 230 km/h.
- Green line (Ain Sokhna to Marsa Matrouh, 660 km): Ain Sokhna-Sixth of October segment expected around Q1 2027, whole line mid-to-late 2027. Blue line: Sixth of October to Fayoum, Minya, Aswan, Abu Simbel (over 1,100 km); first segment around Q1 2027; extended May 2022 toward Toshka and Wadi Halfa (Sudan). Red line: Safaga/Hurghada/Qena. Proposed 4th line Port Said-Alexandria. All three lines expected around 2029.
- Contractors: Siemens consortium with Arab Contractors and Orascom Construction; Deutsche Bahn and Elsewedy Electric to operate and maintain (contract November 2022).
- Money: January 2021 declaration of intent; first contract EUR 4.5 billion for 660 km in September 2021; May 2022 extension to full 2,000 km, budget 8.1 billion Euros (US$8.7 billion).
- Green line to carry up to 30 million passengers annually, cut travel times in half and carbon emissions by 70%.

wikis.title: Siemens introduces new Velaro high-speed train for Egypt
wikis.summary: Railway Technology (11 Nov 2025) on Siemens showing the Velaro at TransMEA 2025 and a Desiro HC test run in Egypt.
wikis.body:
- November 11, 2025. Siemens Mobility unveiled its Velaro to the Egyptian public at TransMEA 2025 in Cairo: up to 250 km/h, 489 passengers, desert-adapted filtration and cooling; design optimised with Altair tools.
- Desiro HC regional train completed a maiden run near the 6th of October Depot; slated for the Green Line, a 660 km network linking Cairo with Ain Sokhna, Alexandria and Marsa Matrouh. 94 Desiro HC trains expected (up to 849 passengers each, 160 km/h, ETCS Level 2).
- Project: three lines totalling over 2,000 km, reaching nearly 90% of the population, expected to be the sixth-largest high-speed network globally. Rolling stock: 41 Velaro, 94 Desiro HC, 41 Vectron locomotives; Siemens has a 15-year maintenance agreement.
- Minister Kamel El-Wazir called it "a defining moment in Egypt's transport modernisation strategy".

wikis.title: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 2021 US Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act: legislative history, provisions and funding (first part).
wikis.body:
- IIJA / Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (H.R. 3684, Pub. L. 117-58), signed by President Biden on November 15, 2021. Introduced June 4, 2021 as the INVEST in America Act by Peter DeFazio ($547 billion); House passed July 1, 2021 (221-201, $715 billion); Senate passed amended version August 10, 2021 (69-30); House agreed November 5, 2021 (228-206).
- Amended bill: approximately $1.2 trillion, $550 billion "new" plus $650 billion for existing infrastructure; adds broadband, clean water, electric grid.
- Background: Biden's $2.3 trillion American Jobs Plan (March 31, 2021). Negotiations: Republican $568 billion counter (April), $928 billion Capito plan, a bipartisan $974 billion five-year / $1.2 trillion eight-year deal (June 2021); Senate voted 67-32 to advance on July 28 and 66-28 to proceed on July 30. House vote delayed by progressives linking it to Build Back Better; on November 5, 13 Republicans joined most Democrats; six Democrats voted no.
- Original House bill: $343 billion roads/highways/bridges/safety, $109 billion transit, $95 billion rail.
- NPR summary of Senate version: $110 billion roads and bridges, $11 billion safety, $39 billion transit, $66 billion rail, $7.5 billion EV chargers, $73 billion power, $65 billion broadband.
- Also makes the Minority Business Development Agency permanent; authorizes ARPA-I; broadens the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council. Climate: REPEAT Project says the Act alone makes only a small reduction in emissions.

wikis.title: Biden signs the $1 trillion bipartisan infrastructure bill into law
wikis.summary: NPR report on President Biden signing the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act on 15 November 2021 and the backlash faced by Republicans who supported it.
wikis.body:
- Biden signed a $1 trillion infrastructure bill into law on Monday (article dated November 15, 2021), a ceremony on the White House South Lawn before some 800 guests including members of Congress, governors, state and local officials, and labor and business leaders.
- The law will "funnel billions to states and local governments to upgrade outdated roads, bridges, transit systems and more."
- Biden: "today, we are finally getting this done ... America is moving again, and your life is going to change for the better."
- Sen. Rob Portman (R-Ohio), one of the authors, stressed bipartisanship and said Trump had "furthered the discussion" on infrastructure; Trump declared "Infrastructure Week" several times but never got a bill through Congress.
- The bill drew support from 19 Senate Republicans and 13 House Republicans despite opposition from Trump and some GOP leaders who linked it to a larger partisan spending package.
- Portman and Sen. Kyrsten Sinema (D-Ariz.) led the negotiations; Sens. Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Bill Cassidy attended.
## Backlash
- Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene called the 13 House Republicans "traitors" and tweeted their office phone numbers.
- Rep. Fred Upton told the Detroit News he received over 1,000 calls, including "nasty death threats"; Rep. Tom Reed also reported threats. A 64-year-old man was arrested in Nassau County, New York, for threatening to kill Rep. Andrew Garbarino.

wikis.title: Gateway Program construction begins on the Hudson River Tunnel
wikis.summary: Construction Dive article (Nov. 21, 2023) on construction starting Nov. 3 on the Hudson River Tunnel part of the $16.1 billion Gateway Program.
wikis.body:
- Construction began Nov. 3 (2023) on the Hudson River Tunnel portion of the Gateway Program, a $16.1 billion group of projects to double capacity of the Northeast Corridor rail segment between New Jersey and New York City.
- The federal government pledged to cover 70% of the cost and gave $3.8 billion from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.
- The project will create nine miles (4.5 miles each direction) of new two-track tunnel and rehabilitate the North River Tunnel, which opened in 1910 and carries more than 450 Amtrak and N.J. Transit trains a day. Superstorm Sandy heavily damaged it in 2012.
- History: the similar Access to the Region's Core began in 2010 and was canceled by then-N.J. Gov. Chris Christie that year; it would have cost $8.7 billion. Trump killed another attempt while in office.
- Tunnel digging expected to begin in 2025; overall project slated for completion in 2035.
- Hudson Yards Concrete Casing work ($649 million) should finish by summer 2026.
- Tonnelle Avenue Bridge and Utility Relocation got notice to proceed; in September the GDC awarded $47.3 million in contracts to Naik Consulting Group and Conti Civil.
- Five of nine Hudson Tunnel packages will be under construction or procurement by end of 2023; Sawtooth Bridges Replacement procurement began Nov. 20.

wikis.title: Hudson Tunnel Project (Gateway Program)
wikis.summary: Gateway Program page describing the Hudson Tunnel Project, its urgency, timeline, and the history of the North River Tunnel.
wikis.body:
- Builds nine miles of new passenger rail track between New York and New Jersey, including nearly five miles of tunnel boring for a new two-tube Hudson River tunnel, and rehabilitates the North River Tunnel (in service since 1910).
- New tunnel to open for service in 2035; North River Tunnel rehabilitation completed in 2038. Result: four tracks where there are currently two.
- Ten construction packages; seven in progress or completed.
- Urgency: the ten-mile Newark to New York Penn stretch is the busiest on the Northeast Corridor; two tubes mean any disruption affects both directions; Hurricane Sandy flooded the tunnels in 2012 and chlorides continue to damage the tunnel.
- Benefits claimed: over 95,000 direct, indirect and induced jobs and $19.6 billion in economic activity; Buy America requirement.
- History: built by the Pennsylvania Railroad with the shield method; original plans called for two tunnels but only one was completed.

wikis.title: Deposits refunded as Beulah's STH BNK collapse plays out
wikis.summary: The Urban Developer (14 Aug 2026) on buyers' deposits being returned after the failure of Beulah's STH BNK towers in Melbourne and the sale of the Hanover House site.
wikis.body:
- Buyers in the failed STH BNK learn their deposits will be returned, confirmed by receivers KordaMentha and Alvarez & Marsal.
- More than 80 per cent of the 705 apartments were sold, totalling close to $1 billion; earlier this year deposits for 540 contracts worth around $650 million were held in an interest-earning trust account. Buyers have 10-year sunset clauses.
- Beulah statement: "ambitious vision" for Melbourne; "challenging market conditions made delivery increasingly difficult."
- Timeline: 118 City Road bought 2018 for $101 million; plans for two twisting towers (102-storey and 68-storey) unveiled the following year; approved 2020; launched 2022 as a $2.7-billion project with $400 million sold on day one; sub-penthouse sold for $38 million (previous record $35 million).
- Costs escalated in 2024; by February 2025 BSSPV was in administration after wind-up orders by Cox Architecture and UN Studio, with debts of more than $100 million. Creditors voted in March 2025 to sell the land; a Deed of Company Arrangement was submitted December 2025; first dividend paid January 2026.
- The 158 City Road site (Hanover House) reportedly sold for $26 million, below the $30 million Beulah paid in 2021, reportedly to a developer planning build-to-rent.

wikis.title: STH BNK by Beulah (Green Spine) skyscraper development, Melbourne
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the never-built STH BNK by Beulah twin-tower project in Southbank, Melbourne, its design, approval and 2025-2026 collapse.
wikis.body:
- Status: "Never built". Location 60 Southbank Boulevard, Southbank, Victoria. Construction started 2024 (infobox), completion ~2029, cost ~AUD $2 billion. Previously and still commonly called Green Spine.
- Developer Beulah International; architects UNStudio and Cox Architecture. Tower 1: 102 storeys, 366 m (would have been Australia's tallest); Tower 2: 59 storeys, 251 m. Mixed-use: residential, retail, commercial, hotel rooms, offices; twisting glass facade with terracing, pocket parks and a publicly accessible botanic garden in the tallest tower.
- Site: amalgam of 102-156 City Road (former BMW flagship showroom, 6,191 m2, bought December 2017 for $101 million) and 158 City Road (Hanover House, bought April 2021, 1,515 m2); total 7,706 m2.
- Six-bid architect contest; UNStudio and Cox won, announced August 2018.
- Approved by the City of Melbourne in March 2020; Planning Minister Richard Wynne approved on 23 April 2020 as a fast-tracked COVID-era project.
- February 2025: BSSPV Pty Ltd placed into administration, owing more than $5 million in fees; Cox Architecture and UNStudio filed a wind-up notice.
- April 2026: project formally shelved due to inability to obtain financing amid surging construction costs; site due on the market later in 2026 with expectation another developer will submit an amended or new design.

wikis.title: Seestadt Aspern, Vienna
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Seestadt Aspern, a large urban development on the former Aspern airfield in Vienna's Donaustadt district.
wikis.body:
- One of the largest ongoing urban development projects in Europe; on completion expected 25,000 residents and 20,000 jobs. About 2.4 km2, roughly 10 km northeast of central Vienna; 2023 population 12,000. Named for the man-made Aspern Lake.
- Built on the former Wien-Aspern Airport (military use in the two World Wars, decommissioned in the 1980s).
- History: 2005 masterplan competition won by Tovatt Architects & Planners with N+ Objektmanagement; May 2007 municipal council unanimously agreed. Stage 1 (2009-2017), Stage 2 (2017-2022), Stage 3 (2022-2028). First road works 2012; U2 line with Aspern Nord and Seestadt stations completed 2013; district management from 2014; Seepark opened July 2015; population exceeded 6000 a year after settlement began.
- Seeparkquartier (230,000 m2) largely completed 2020, work began 2016 (first project HoHo Wien wooden hybrid high-rise); pedestrian zone redesigned spring 2022 after media controversy; to be completed 2024 with the Aspern NOA22 medical centre. A training centre for the Austrian Football Association was under construction as of 2025.
- Transit: 30 km/h limit, 80 parking spaces per 100 apartments, seven bus lines, U2, S80; tram 27 opened October 2025, first tram link.
- Many streets and parks named after women (Vienna had 519 streets named after women vs 4022 after men as of July 2020).

wikis.title: Seestadt Aspern Housing (D12) by Berger + Parkkinen and Querkraft
wikis.summary: Dezeen case study (5 March 2024) of the 213-apartment D12 housing block in Vienna's Seestadt Aspern, as part of its Social Housing Revival series.
wikis.body:
- Completed in 2015 by Berger + Parkkinen and Querkraft Architekten for housing cooperative EGB. Block D12: 213 apartments, eight shops and community facilities.
- Seestadt Aspern is described as one of Europe's largest urban development projects: due for completion in 2030, homes for 20,000 people and 20,000 workplaces across 240 hectares around an artificial lake on a former airfield.
- Design: seven parallel timber-clad blocks with projecting concrete balconies around a semi-public central courtyard nicknamed the "canyon"; concrete frame with prefabricated wood walls finished in larch planks; basement car park and ground-floor commercial/community level with full-height windows and metal mesh for growing plants; access via stairs, internal "streets" and raised walkways.
- Conceived as a continuation of Vienna's social housing legacy ("Red Vienna" 1918-1934, Karl Marx-Hof). A quarter of Vienna's residents are social tenants. Alfred Berger: "The fascination of huge housing units ... as built in the 1920s and 30s, is enormous."
- Photography by Herta Hurnhaus.

wikis.title: Deep Dive Dubai, the world's deepest swimming pool
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Deep Dive Dubai, a 60-metre deep diving pool in Dubai that opened on 28 July 2021.
wikis.body:
- 60 m (200 ft) deep diving pool in Dubai, UAE, holding 14,000,000 liters of fresh water; the deepest swimming pool in the world. Opened 28 July 2021.
- Includes an area designed to resemble a ruined, sunken city with walls, furnished rooms, a sunken car, motorbikes, snooker table and foosball table; can also be used as an underwater film studio.
- Before it opened, the deepest pool was the Deepspot in Mszczonow (45 m).
- The tank is shaped like an oyster, reflecting Dubai's pearl-diving heritage; corners are covered by 56 cameras plus audio and lighting equipment.
- Other deep pools listed: Nemo 33 (34.5 m), Blue Abyss, Y-40 (42.15 m).

wikis.title: Dubai opens world's deepest pool (Deep Dive Dubai)
wikis.summary: Rappler report (10 July 2021) on the opening of Deep Dive Dubai, a 60-metre underwater city dive pool certified by Guinness World Records.
wikis.body:
- Deep Dive Dubai, a 60-meter (196 feet) pool, certified as deepest by the Guinness Book of World Records in June (2021); opened to invitation-only guests on Friday, July 9; public opening expected by the end of July.
- Holds 14 million liters, almost six Olympic-sized pools; 15 meters deeper than the previous record holder Deepspot in Poland.
- Themed rooms, an underwater arcade (retro games like Pac-Man, foosball), a media editing room, and usable as an underwater film studio.
- Offers introductory free-diving and scuba courses and guided tours; safety includes up to 56 cameras and a hyperbaric chamber.
- Actor Will Smith posted a video: "This gives new meaning to deep end of the pool."

wikis.title: Turkey inaugurates the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge
wikis.summary: Daily Sabah report (18 March 2022) on the opening of the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge, described as the world's longest midspan suspension bridge.
wikis.body:
- Opened for traffic Friday March 18, 2022 in a ceremony attended by President Erdoğan; foundation laid March 18, 2017; date coincides with the 107th anniversary of the Çanakkale naval victory. South Korea's PM Kim Boo-kyum attended.
- Erdoğan: world's longest midspan suspension bridge, surpassing Japan. Investment of 2.5 billion euros ($2.76 billion); annual gains in time, fuel and emissions of 415 million euros; expected 5.3 billion euros in production, employment for 118,000 people, 2.4 billion euros national income. Built via public-private partnership by a consortium of South Korean and Turkish companies; some 5,000 workers.
- Main span 2,023 m between towers (symbolizing 2023, the Republic's 100th anniversary); towers 318 m high shaped like artillery shells; total length 4,608 m (side spans 770 m each, approach viaducts 365 m and 680 m); three lanes each direction; deck 45.06 m wide, 3.5 m high.
- Crosses the Dardanelles, first bridge linking the two continents there; part of the 101-km Malkara-Çanakkale Highway route, and of the Kınalı-Tekirdağ-Çanakkale-Savaştepe project. Ferry crossing normally takes about 30 minutes.

wikis.title: 1915 Çanakkale Bridge inauguration (IRF)
wikis.summary: International Road Federation member news (27 April 2022) describing the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge put into operation on 18 March 2022 and its dimensions and symbolism.
wikis.body:
- Put into operation 18 March 2022; foundations date to 2017. Located in Çanakkale province, spanning the Dardanelles about 10 km south of the Sea of Marmara, just south of Lapseki and Gelibolu.
- Connects to highways around the Marmara Sea, home to nearly one-third of Turkey's population.
- Main span 2,023 m (100th anniversary of the Republic), side spans 770 m each, approach viaducts 365 m and 680 m, crossing length 4,608 m; 2x3 traffic lanes; dual deck 45.06 m wide, 3.5 m high. (Source also gives total length as 3,563 m.)
- Steel towers 318 m (334 m above sea level with a 16 m cannonball figure), described as the world's highest; tower foundations at -45 m on the Asian side and -37 m on the European side.
- Symbolism: 1915 and the 318 m height (18th day of 3rd month) refer to the Çanakkale Naval Victory of March 18, 1915; shape symbolizes artillery shells.

wikis.title: Red Sea International Airport becomes operational
wikis.summary: Arab News report (21 September 2023) on the first Saudia flight landing at Red Sea International Airport, serving The Red Sea destination.
wikis.body:
- Red Sea International Airport (RSIA) became operational on Thursday (September 21, 2023) with the first Saudia flight, per Red Sea Global (developer of The Red Sea and AMAALA).
- Flights from King Khalid International Airport, Riyadh, every Thursday (departing 10:50 a.m.) and Saturday (12:50 p.m., return 15:35), connecting in under two hours.
- Group CEO John Pagano: "with the first flight touching down at RSIA, and our first resorts receiving bookings, Saudi Arabia's position on the global tourism map is all but secured."
- Within an eight-hour flight of 85 percent of the world's population; international flights to begin from next year as more phase one resorts open.
- Operated by daa International (supporting design validation and commissioning since 2020); new RSIA brand unveiled, its icon inspired by the bird's-eye view of the airport exterior.

wikis.title: Bond Street Elizabeth line station officially opens
wikis.summary: Rail Advent report (24 October 2022) on the opening of the Elizabeth line's Bond Street station in London.
wikis.body:
- First Elizabeth line services arrived at Bond Street at 05.47 on Monday 24 October 2022, welcomed by Transport Commissioner Andy Byford, Mayor Sadiq Khan and Transport Minister Katherine Fletcher.
- Services every five minutes; from Sunday 6 November peak services every three to four minutes; no service Sunday 30 October, then seven days a week.
- Station: two lifts for step-free access, two new ticket halls; Davies Street entrance has an angular bronze ceiling; Hanover Square entrance has a 60-metre escalator (longest at an Underground station on the Elizabeth line, second longest on the TfL network). Artworks by Darren Almond.
- The line opened on 24 May (2022); over 27 million journeys on the central section and more than 54 million in total in five months. Travel times from Bond Street: Liverpool Street 8 minutes, Canary Wharf 15 minutes.
- Khan: line delivers "a £42 billion boost to the UK economy". Fletcher: station will serve over 140,000 people a day; £9 billion government investment; 55,000 jobs created.
- Byford: the opening completes the central section, now with 10 new stations; through journeys from east and west are "less than two weeks away".

wikis.title: Almost four years late, Elizabeth line's Bond Street station set to open
wikis.summary: ITV News London (18 October 2022) on the delayed opening of Bond Street station on the Elizabeth line the following Monday.
wikis.body:
- Final preparations (trial evacuations, fire control testing, security checks) ahead of opening "next Monday".
- Under initial plans Bond Street was due to open with all other stations in December 2018; Crossrail problems meant the line opened only in May (2022). Construction issues meant it was announced in 2018 that Bond Street would open after the others.
- Two main entrances, near Oxford Street and Regent Street. Liverpool Street in eight minutes, Canary Wharf in 15.
- Sadiq Khan: "arguably the most beautiful, stylish, spacious station in Europe". Andy Byford (outgoing TfL commissioner): "massively important", the "missing piece in the heart of the West End".
- New West End Company's Dee Corsi: a key driver in returning to "£10 billion annual turnover".
- Line runs Reading and Heathrow to Abbey Wood and Shenfield; operates in three sections and is closed Sundays until 6 November when it becomes seven days a week. Final timetable, up to 24 trains per hour, expected by May.

wikis.title: Melbourne's Sapphire by the Gardens tops out
wikis.summary: The Property Tribune (3 August 2022) on the topping out of both towers of SP Setia's Sapphire by the Gardens in Melbourne, built by Multiplex.
wikis.body:
- Both towers topped out at 232 m and 220 m above street level. Includes a 62-level 5-star Shangri-La Hotel (500 rooms, champagne gold fins, largest ballroom in Melbourne's CBD with six-metre-high ceilings) and a 60-level tower with 325 luxury apartments.
- Location: corner of Exhibition and La Trobe Streets; designed by Fender Katsalidis with Cox Architecture; ground broken in late 2018. Towers joined by a Sky Lounge/sky bridge 46 storeys up; Multiplex used a temporary cantilevered deck to work beneath it.
- Builder Multiplex; over 400 workers daily at peak; over 2 million hours worked to date. Forecast over 1,000 jobs.
- Timeline: first residents expected October 2022; final precinct completion "on track for early in 2023"; hotel to welcome first guests in 2024.
- SP Setia CEO Datuk Choong Kai Wai: it will mark "our fifth significant development within Melbourne."

wikis.title: Major NYC airport upgrades and record passenger numbers
wikis.summary: City & State New York (29 April 2024) snapshot of the Port Authority's multibillion-dollar overhaul of JFK, LaGuardia and Newark airports.
wikis.body:
- Air travel in the NYC region is above pre-pandemic levels; passenger survey responses and independent ratings are improving.
- **JFK**: $19 billion ($15 billion private, $4 billion Port Authority); projected completion 2028 (Terminal 8 expansion completed November 2022; Terminal 4 expansion 2024; Terminal 6 phases 2026 and 2028; New Terminal One phases 2026 and 2030; roadway and ground transit center 2026); 19,000 projected construction jobs; passengers 2019 62,571,463, 2023 62,516,750.
- **LaGuardia**: $8 billion (two-thirds private); substantially completed 2022 (Terminal B January 2022; Terminal C substantially June 2022, final gates 2024); 7,000 construction jobs; passengers 2019 31,084,894, 2023 32,400,000.
- **Newark**: $3 billion (Port Authority); Terminal A completed 2023; 2,500 construction jobs; passengers 2019 46,389,037, 2023 49,100,000.
- Economic impact: JFK over $45 billion, LGA more than $13.6 billion, EWR nearly $29.3 billion. Source: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.

wikis.title: LaGuardia Airport completes Terminal B renovation with second skybridge
wikis.summary: Construction Dive (22 Feb 2022) on the opening of LaGuardia's second skybridge on Jan. 28, the final milestone of the nearly six-year Terminal B renovation.
wikis.body:
- Second skybridge opened Jan. 28 (2022), the final milestone of the nearly six-year Terminal B renovation. Terminal B renovation valued at $5.1 billion ($4 billion construction); overall project $8 billion. Overall project about 95% complete; remaining original terminal piece must be demolished to open remaining gates.
- Manager: LaGuardia Gateway Partners (Vantage Airport Group, Skanska, Meridiam, JLC Infrastructure); Skanska-Walsh JV led design-build; HOK and WPS architecture and engineering. Funding: about $2.5 billion project bonds, $1.5 billion Port Authority, $200 million equity. Described by Vantage as the largest public-private partnership in U.S. aviation.
- Terminal: 35 gates across two concourses, four-story retail, 850,000-square-foot Arrivals & Departures Hall. The new 485-foot western skybridge used over 2,500 tons of steel; the first skybridge (eastern concourse) opened in May (2021). Officials say LaGuardia is the only airport with dual pedestrian skybridges; adds 2 miles of taxiway space.
- Awards: 2021 UNESCO Prix Versailles, LEED Gold, structural engineering award. 43% water savings and 18% energy cost reduction. Rick Cotton: "We have gone from worst to best."
- Terminal C expected to be completed in spring 2022. Gov. Hochul nixed Cuomo's LaGuardia AirTrain in October; alternatives like an N train extension are being studied.

wikis.title: Delhi-Meerut RapidX renamed Namo Bharat, first section opens
wikis.summary: ThePrint (19 Oct 2023) on India's first RRTS, renamed Namo Bharat, whose 17 km priority section opened to the public on 21 October 2023.
wikis.body:
- Housing Minister Hardeep Singh Puri said the RRTS will be known as Namo Bharat; PM Modi to inaugurate the priority section on 20 October 2023. Second renaming: named RAPIDX in April 2023.
- Priority section: 17 km, Duhai Depot (Ghaziabad) to Sahibabad, five stations (Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Guldhar, Duhai, Duhai Depot), 15-minute travel time, trains every 15 minutes initially, open to the public 21 October, operating 6am-11pm. Fares Rs 30-50 standard, Rs 60-100 premium (premium has own lounge); luggage up to 25 kg.
- Trains run at 160 kmph (designed for 180 kmph). Six coaches, about 1,700 passengers, 134 seats including 62 in premium.
- Full 82 km Delhi-Meerut corridor costs Rs 32,724 crore, expected operational by June 2025; aims for under an hour Delhi-Meerut; ridership about eight lakh per day expected; "close to one lakh passenger vehicles" off the road. One of three RRTS corridors. Built by NCRTC.

wikis.title: RapidX named Namo Bharat, PM Modi launches rail service
wikis.summary: Business Standard (20 Oct 2023) on PM Modi inaugurating the 17 km first stretch of the Delhi-Meerut RRTS, now named Namo Bharat.
wikis.body:
- PM Modi inaugurated on 20 October 2023 the 17 km first phase between Sahibabad and Duhai Depot (part of the 82 km Delhi-Meerut corridor expected fully operational by 2025); public service from October 21. Five stops: Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Guldhar, Duhai, Duhai Depot.
- Corridor built by NCRTC, a joint venture of the Centre and Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh governments; Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut will cover 100 km in an hour.
- Six coaches including one premium coach; premium fare Rs 40-100, standard Rs 20-50 on the priority section. QR-code or card ticketing; UPI-enabled ticket vending machines.
- Average speed 100 kmph; train sets by Alstom in Gujarat. Features: six CCTVs per coach, luggage racks, Wi-Fi, charging at every seat, platform screen doors; cargo to move in non-peak hours.

wikis.title: Interborough Express moves ahead as state prepares environmental review
wikis.summary: Queens Daily Eagle (10 Sept 2026) on MTA progress on the 14-mile, $5.5 billion Interborough Express light rail and its upcoming Draft Environmental Impact Statement.
wikis.body:
- MTA and Gov. Hochul said the IBX Draft EIS is scheduled for release before the year is over (ahead of schedule), followed by public meetings; public workshops on design run through 2027.
- IBX: 14-mile light rail from Roosevelt Avenue/Jackson Heights to Brooklyn Army Terminal, 18 stations, on an existing rarely used freight track; 32 minutes end to end; projected 160,000 daily riders; 900,000 New Yorkers live near the line. All 18 stops to be ADA compliant. First trains expected in the 2030s; no estimated completion date.
- Accessibility upgrades under way at Broadway Junction, Junius St. and Avenue I subway stations.
