- March 31, 1889: dedicated in a ceremony presided over by Gustave Eiffel, with French Prime Minister Pierre Tirard and 200 construction workers.
- Built for the 1889 international exposition honoring the centenary of the French Revolution; chosen from more than 100 designs; open-lattice wrought-iron, almost 1,000 feet, then the world's tallest man-made structure. Completed under budget in just two years; only one worker died.
- 984 feet tall on four masonry piers, three platforms with observation decks. Otis Elevator Company designed the glass-cage elevators, not complete by March 31, so Eiffel climbed the stairs and raised a French tricolor; fireworks from the second platform.
- Exposition opened in early May. Tallest until the Chrysler Building in 1930. Nearly demolished in 1909 when the 20-year land lease expired, saved by its value as a radio antenna.

wikis.title: Seven Stars in Kyushu luxury excursion train
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the JR Kyushu Seven Stars in Kyushu sleeper excursion train: design, formation, routes, history.
wikis.body:
- Deluxe sleeping car excursion train run by JR Kyushu since October 2013; first service 15 October 2013; designed under industrial designer Eiji Mitooka; name from Kyushu's seven prefectures and seven coaches.
- DF200-7000 diesel locomotive built by Kawasaki Heavy Industries (Kobe), maroon livery, completed July 2013 (delivered 2 July 2013); coaches built by Hitachi (Kudamatsu) and JR Kyushu Kokura Works; operating speed 100 km/h.
- Formation: five sleeping cars, lounge car (piano, bar, observation), dining car; capacity 28 passengers; rear car has two deluxe suites. Cost approximately 3 billion yen. Some suites have porcelain bathrooms designed by Sakaida Kakiemon XIV.
- Routes from Hakata: 2-day (Hakata, Nagasaki; Aso, Yufuin, Hakata) and 4-day circular tours.

wikis.title: SCHEUERLE SPMT turns 40
wikis.summary: TII press release on the 40th anniversary of the SCHEUERLE Self-Propelled Modular Transporter, launched in 1983.
wikis.body:
- In 1983 Scheuerle Fahrzeugfabrik (now TII SCHEUERLE) developed and launched the Self-Propelled Modular Transporter (SPMT); the name SPMT itself originally came from TII SCHEUERLE.
- Several 10,000 SCHEUERLE SPMT axle lines are in use worldwide; "the global standard".
- The idea came from the needs of long-time customer Mammoet; module width 2,430 millimetres so it fits a standard container (flat rack) and can travel on motorways.
- Series named: SPMT InterCombi SPE, K24, K25 SPE. Loads moved: luxury yachts, industrial plants weighing thousands of tonnes, mining-vehicle components, offshore wind turbines, complete hotels, historical cultural assets.
- Quote (Dr Gerald Karch, CEO of the TII Group): customers' needs for functionality, cost-effectiveness, safety and efficiency are the incentive.

wikis.title: Self-propelled modular transporter (SPMT)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on SPMTs: what they are, specifications and history.
wikis.body:
- A platform heavy hauler with a large array of wheels, upgraded from the hydraulic modular trailer; carries bridge sections, refinery equipment, cranes, spacecraft, entire buildings and oil platforms. Used to replace bridge spans in the US, Europe, Asia and Canada.
- Grid of computer-controlled axles (usually 2 across, 4-8 along); each individually controllable, swivels 270 degrees (some 360). Loaded speed often under 1 mile per hour (1.6 km/h). Multiple SPMTs can be linked and run from one control panel.
- History: 1935 Gothaer Wagonfabrik motorized model of the Culemeyer trailer (32 ton load capacity); first modern modular units in the 1970s; early 1980s Mammoet set module width 2.44 m (ISO container flatrack) and added 360 degree steering, commissioned Scheuerle; deliveries started 1983 (4-axle, 6-axle, power pack).
- 2016: ESTA published the first SPMT best practice guide addressing trailers tipping over. Shipbuilders use SPMTs instead of gantry cranes for ship sections.

wikis.title: Meyer Werft delivers Norwegian Breakaway
wikis.summary: Meyer Werft press release (25 April 2013) on delivery of the 146,600 GT Norwegian Breakaway to Norwegian Cruise Line.
wikis.body:
- Bremerhaven/Papenburg, 25 April 2013: NCL took delivery of Norwegian Breakaway (146,600 GT) after an 18-month build; first of two Breakaway class ships (sister Norwegian Getaway to launch in Miami February 1, 2014). Yard number S.678.
- Features: The Waterfront, 678 Ocean Place, largest aqua park and ropes course at sea, first salt room in a spa; approx. 75% outside staterooms, solo staterooms, The Haven by Norwegian.
- Diesel-electric pod drive; support from Federal Ministry of Economics and Technology and Lower Saxony for innovation aid.
- Main particulars: 324.00 m overall, 39.7 m breadth, 18 decks, draught 8.30 m, engine output 62,400 kW, propulsion 35,000 kW, 21.5 kn.
- Route: Bremerhaven to Rotterdam, transatlantic from Southampton to New York (naming ceremony); 12 May 2013 to Bermuda for seven-day cruises.

wikis.title: Norwegian Breakaway (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on NCL cruise ship Norwegian Breakaway: naming, construction, design, service and incidents.
wikis.body:
- Ordered 17 August 2011; built by Meyer Werft, Papenburg; steel cut/laid down 21 September 2011; launched 30 April 2013 (per infobox); godmothers The Rockettes; delivered to NCL 25 April 2013; IMO 9606912.
- Named through a public contest (Kimberly Powell); announced 14 September 2011. With Norwegian Getaway, first two ships of Project Breakaway.
- 146,600 GT (infobox 145,655 GT), 325.64 m, capacity 3,963 passengers, 1,604 staterooms and 350 suites; ninth largest cruise ship by gross tonnage at launch; 21.5 kn; two ABB Azipods.
- Homeported at New York Passenger Ship Terminal (Bermuda cruises May-September, Bahamas/Florida October-April); leaving New York from late 2018 for New Orleans, Miami early 2019, Port Canaveral November 2019.
- Onboard: Ocean Blue restaurant by Geoffrey Zakarian, Second City comedy club, hull art by Peter Max. Incidents listed: 17 September 2013 balcony fall; 3 February 2014 child drowned in pool.

wikis.title: Claas Axion 960 Cemos wins Sustainable Tractor of the Year 2021
wikis.summary: HeavyQuip (January 8, 2021): the Claas Axion 960 Cemos won the Sustainable Tractor of the Year 2021 title.
wikis.body:
- Jury of 26 specialist agricultural journalists from 25 countries picked the Claas Axion 960 Cemos from 18 finalists (17 others); second time the Sustainable TotY has been awarded. The ceremony was virtual for the first time due to the corona pandemic.
- Jury: Cemos system and tyre pressure optimization give "remarkable fuel saving" and efficient performance.
- Claas introduced the Stage V Axion 900 series in September 2020, optionally equipped or retrofitted with Claas Ctic tyre inflation and self-learning Cemos for tractors. Cemos received the DLG approved label for fuel savings of up to 16.8 percent and 16.3 percent productivity increase (DLG test report 7096).

wikis.title: Claas Axion tractor (Wikipedia stub)
wikis.summary: Short Wikipedia stub on the Claas Axion tractor built at the former Renault tractor plant in Le Mans.
wikis.body:
- Built by the Claas-owned former Renault tractor plant at Le Mans; 163-225 hp (ECE R24); John Deere engine; Hexashift transmission (four ranges, six powershift stages).
- Early codename ET 97; development began 2003; Axion 850 manufactured 2006 to 2023.

wikis.title: Austrian Bundesheer receives heavy transporters
wikis.summary: ESUT (13 April 2021): Austrian defence minister handed over three heavy transporters for combat vehicles up to 70 tonnes (German text).
wikis.body:
- On 12 April 2021 Austrian Defence Minister Klaudia Tanner handed three heavy transporters to the Panzergrenadiere in Wels, Austria; they can carry combat vehicles up to 70 tonnes total weight.
- Each transport train: Rheinmetall MAN Military Vehicles HX81 8x8 semi-tractor with 500 kW diesel engine plus a 7-axle Doll low-loader semi-trailer. Supplied by MAN Truck & Bus Vertrieb Osterreich as prime contractor; matches the system used by the German Bundeswehr.
- Military fit: camouflage paint, infrared lighting, preparation for ICT extensions. Tanner: the systems strengthen the Bundesheer's performance and readiness and its core competence, military national defence.

wikis.title: RMMV HX range of tactical trucks (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Rheinmetall MAN Military Vehicles HX tactical truck range, its variants, history and orders.
wikis.body:
- Tactical military trucks by Rheinmetall MAN Military Vehicles (RMMV), in service 2007-present, production 2005-present, design date 2002. Estimated 19,535 confirmed orders (infobox, excluding options and some framework contracts).
- Variants: HX60 4x4, HX58 6x6, HX61 6x6, HX77 8x8, HX81 HET 8x8; HX2 range 40M 4x4, 42M 6x6, 44M 8x8, 45M 10x10.
- HX range announced 2003, first order 2004; first order came in October 2004 from the British Army (Support Vehicle requirement), contract March 2005. HX2 announced 2012, first delivered April 2016. HX3 unveiled May 2021 with series production scheduled from 2027. HX replaced the LX (2004) and FX (2005) ranges and the SX range in 2019.
- RMMV formed by the 2010 merger of MAN's military truck branch and Rheinmetall's wheeled military vehicle branch (51% Rheinmetall, 49% MAN).

wikis.title: Overburden Conveyor Bridge F60
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the F60, five giant overburden conveyor bridges used in Lusatian lignite mines.
wikis.body:
- Series designation of five overburden conveyor bridges in Lusatia, Germany, built by Volkseigener Betrieb TAKRAF in Lauchhammer (production 1969-1991); described as the largest movable technical industrial machines in the world.
- 502 m long, up to 80 m high, about 240 m wide (article figures); 13,600 metric tons; 27 MW externally powered; 760 wheels (380 powered) on two bogies on 1,435 mm rails; crew of 14. Cutting height 60 m.
- Build dates: first 1969-1972, second 1972-1974, third 1976-1978, fourth 1986-1988, fifth 1988-1991.
- Four still operating (Jaenschwalde, Welzow-Sued, Nochten, Reichwalde); the fifth, at Lichterfeld-Schacksdorf, is open to visitors.

wikis.title: MV Karadeniz Powership Yasin Bey
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Karpowership floating power plant Yasin Bey, converted from a 2000-built cargo ship and sent to Ambon, Indonesia in 2016.
wikis.body:
- Liberia-flagged floating power plant owned and operated by Karpowership; 125 MW generation; 162.15 m LOA, 20.73 m beam, 11,130 GT, 11,872 DWT. IMO 9214551.
- Built 2000 as a general cargo carrier by Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Company (China) with earlier names including Nirint Atlas and Beluga Intonation.
- Converted at Sedef Shipyard, Tuzla, Istanbul; on November 13, 2016 sailed to Ambon, Indonesia in a ceremony attended by President Erdogan and Prime Minister Binali Yildirim, with MV Karadeniz Powership Gokhan Bey; commissioned to supply Ambon's grid for five years.

wikis.title: Hellisheidi geothermal power station (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the largest geothermal power station in Iceland, at Hengill.
wikis.body:
- Eighth-largest geothermal station in the world and largest in Iceland; Hengill, 11 km from Nesjavellir. 303 MW electric and 200 MWth hot water for Reykjavik district heating; owned and operated by ON Power (Reykjavik Energy subsidiary). Flash steam, 50 wells, max depth 2,200 m.
- History: 2006 first two 45 MW turbines; 2007 33 MW low-pressure turbine; 2008 two more 45 MW; 2010 hot water plant; 2011 last two 45 MW; 2014 system reinjecting non-condensable gases (hydrogen sulphide); 2020 hot water raised to 200 MWth.
- 2016: ON announced new drilling due to falling steam levels (apparent from 2013), expected cost in 2017 of 19 billion Icelandic crowns.
- Educational tours; pilot Climeworks direct air capture facility capturing up to 4,000 metric tons CO2 a year, injected and mineralized.

wikis.title: USS Holland (SS-1)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on USS Holland, the US Navy first submarine, designed by John Philip Holland.
wikis.body:
- First US Navy submarine (not its first underwater craft, the 1775 Turtle). Built as Holland VI at Crescent Shipyard, Elizabeth, New Jersey, for the Holland Torpedo Boat Company (Electric Boat from 1899). Laid down November 1896; launched 17 May 1897; acquired 11 April 1900; commissioned 12 October 1900; decommissioned 17 July 1905; stricken 21 November 1910; sold 18 June 1913; displayed in Paterson, NJ, until sold for scrap in 1932.
- 63 ft 10 in long; 64 long tons surfaced, 74 submerged; gas engine 45 bhp surfaced, electric motor 55 bhp submerged; 6 knots surfaced; test depth 100 ft; one 18-inch torpedo tube (three torpedoes) and one 8 in dynamite gun; crew six or seven.
- Features: conning tower, ballast and trim tanks. John Holland held US Patent 702,729.

wikis.title: John Philip Holland (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia biography of Irish-American engineer John Philip Holland (1841-1914), developer of the first US Navy and Royal Navy submarines.
wikis.body:
- Born February 24, 1841 in Liscannor, County Clare, Ireland; died August 12, 1914 in Newark, New Jersey. Developed USS Holland (SS-1) and Holland 1, the first Royal Navy submarine; Holland Torpedo Boat Company.
- Early life: Irish Christian Brothers teacher, left in 1873 due to ill health, migrated to the US in 1873, taught six more years in Paterson, NJ. After breaking a leg in Boston he refined submarine designs in hospital.
- Projects: Holland I, II (Fenian Ram), III, IV, USS Plunger. Engineering Heritage Award (2011).

wikis.title: European Marine Energy Centre (EMEC), Orkney
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on EMEC, the wave and tidal energy test centre in the Orkney Islands.
wikis.body:
- World's leading wave and tidal power test and research centre, Orkney, Scotland; established in 2003 by public sector organisations after a 2001 House of Commons Science and Technology Committee recommendation. Offers full-scale grid-connected prototype testing plus support on regulation, grid connection, weather monitoring.
- Sites: Billia Croo wave test site (west Orkney Mainland; construction completed October 2003; highest wave recorded over 18 m), Fall of Warness tidal test site (Eday), Caldale renewables integration R&D site (Eday), scale wave site at Scapa Flow, scale tidal site at Shapinsay Sound, HQ in Stromness.
- Hosted projects on green hydrogen, battery storage, e-fuels, refuelling and data centres. Article flagged as containing promotional content (July 2020).

wikis.title: Chimelong Ocean Kingdom (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the marine theme park in Hengqin, Zhuhai, China.
wikis.body:
- Theme park at Chimelong International Ocean Resort, Hengqin, Zhuhai; owner and operator Chimelong Group; designed by PGAV Destinations. Broke ground 28 November 2010; soft-opened 28 January 2014; grand opening 29 March 2014. First phase cost RMB 10 billion.
- 12.63 million visitors in 2024 (infobox; 12.6 million in text), sixth-most visited theme park in the world and most visited not owned by Disney or Universal. Five Guinness World Records; one of the world's largest oceanariums, 48.75 million litres.
- Eight themed areas; 15 attractions, 3 roller coasters, 2 water rides. 5D Castle Theatre (opened 2015): 1,500 sq m curved screen, a world record, cost about 300 million yuan (US$50 million). Parrot Coaster is a Bolliger & Mabillard winged coaster.

wikis.title: Chimelong Ocean Kingdom opens in China as the world's largest aquarium
wikis.summary: HuffPost Travel reports that Guinness confirmed Chimelong Ocean Kingdom set five world records, including largest aquarium.
wikis.body:
- Published by HuffPost Travel, Apr 3, 2014 (Lisa_Miller, Associate Editor).
- Guinness World Records confirmed "Monday" that Chimelong Ocean Kingdom set five world records, including the title of largest aquarium in the world.
- Other records: "largest underwater viewing dome, largest aquarium tank, largest aquarium window and largest acrylic panel."
- Total water volume: 12.87 million gallons.
- The park has seven aquatic-themed areas, each symbolizing a different part of the ocean.
- It is part of Chimelong Hengqin Bay Hotel, described as the largest ecologically-themed hotel in China.
- Photo captions place it on Hengqin island, Zhuhai city, Guangdong province, south China (photo dated 28 January 2014), described as "the largest ocean theme park in the world".

wikis.title: Puy du Fou inaugurates the Grand Carillon attraction
wikis.summary: TourMaG short note on the 16 June 2017 inauguration of the Grand Carillon at Puy du Fou.
wikis.body:
- TourMaG.com was live on Friday 16 June 2017 from Puy du Fou for the inauguration of the new attraction, the Grand Carillon (video article).
- It stands in the centre of the 18th-century Village and is 16 metres high.
- At each performance it deploys its 72 bells.
- For about ten minutes, 4 "musiciens voltigeurs" (aerial musicians) move through the air to popular 18th-century melodies re-orchestrated by Puy du Fou.

wikis.title: Benjamin Woodgates composes music for Le Grand Carillon at Puy du Fou
wikis.summary: Composer's news post about the French folk-song suite behind Puy du Fou's new Grand Carillon attraction.
wikis.body:
- Posted March 06, 2017 on Benjamin Woodgates's site.
- Woodgates composed a suite of French songs forming the basis of Le Grand Carillon, Puy du Fou's new attraction.
- The suite is written for an ensemble of folk instruments and showcases a "brand new 48-bell carillon, built by Royal Eijsbouts".
- Puy du Fou is described as France's second-largest theme park, attracting over 2 million visitors each year.
- "Le Grand Carillon will open to the public in April 2017."

wikis.title: UPS first-quarter 2010 earnings release
wikis.summary: UPS press release (27 April 2010) reporting Q1 2010 results and operational milestones including the Worldport expansion and Shenzhen air hub.
wikis.body:
- Atlanta, April 27, 2010. UPS (NYSE:UPS) posted adjusted diluted EPS of $0.71 for 1Q 2010, up 37% from adjusted $0.52; revenue up 7% to $11.7 billion (vs $10.9 B). Reported diluted EPS $0.53 vs $0.40. Adjusted operating profit ~ $1.2 B (reported $1.0 B); reported margin 8.9%, adjusted 10.0%.
- Volume: 940 million packages, up 3%; average daily volume 14.93 M vs 14.54 M; revenue per piece up 3%.
- Charges in quarter: $98 M pre-tax restructuring (US Domestic Package reorganization), $38 M loss on sale of a specialized transportation business in Germany, $76 M non-cash tax charge; together they cut net income by $175 M / $0.18 per share.
- Free cash flow $1.3 B; dividends $470 M; capex $280 M; repurchased over 4 M shares for $260 M; ended with $3.1 B cash and marketable securities.
- Chairman/CEO Scott Davis: global strategy "clearly proved beneficial"; CFO Kurt Kuehn cited operating leverage.
## Segments
- **U.S. Domestic Package:** revenue $7.10 B; adjusted operating profit up 17% on revenue up 2%; margin expansion of 120 bp; first year-over-year daily volume growth in two years (12.73 M/day). During the quarter UPS opened the second phase of its Worldport air hub expansion, raising sort capacity from 350,000 to 416,000 packages per hour, enabling larger, more fuel-efficient aircraft. Also introduced UPS Smart Pickup, expected to eliminate an estimated 8 million miles of driving annually.
- **International Package:** revenue $2.64 B (+18%), operating profit $427 M (+45%), margin 16.2%; daily volume 2.20 M (+18%); export volume up more than 9%; non-U.S. domestic up 24% (Turkey acquisition plus 13% organic). UPS began operating its new intra-Asia air hub in Shenzhen, China, cutting at least a day off transit; opened a facility at Calgary International Airport.
- **Supply Chain and Freight:** revenue $1.99 B; reported operating profit $53 M (adjusted $91 M vs $40 M); service parts logistics network expanded to 89 cities in China (world's largest, 120 countries); UPS Freight LTL revenue up 6%.
- **Outlook:** adjusted 2010 EPS guidance raised to $3.05-$3.30, 32%-43% above adjusted 2009.

wikis.title: Hywind Scotland commissioned as the world's first floating wind farm
wikis.summary: WindEurope timeline entry dated 18 October 2017 on Hywind Scotland's commissioning.
wikis.body:
- Entry dated 18 October 2017: "Hywind Scotland: The world's first floating wind farm is commissioned."
- 5 turbines of 6 MW each are connected to test floating technology in a park layout.

wikis.title: Hywind Scotland floating wind farm
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Hywind Scotland, the world's first commercial floating wind farm off Peterhead, commissioned October 2017.
wikis.body:
- World's first commercial wind farm using floating turbines, 29 km (18 mi) off Peterhead, Scotland (Buchan Deep). Five 6 MW Siemens SWT-6.0-154 direct-drive turbines, 30 MW total; capacity factor 54%.
- Owners: Equinor (75%) and Masdar (25%); operator Hywind (Scotland) Limited. Construction began 2016; commissioned October 2017; construction cost £264m (£8.8m/MW, about three times fixed offshore).
- Site: water depth 95-120 m, 25 km from shore, ~15 km2; hub height 101 m, rotor diameter 154 m.
- Predecessor: Equinor (then Statoil) launched the 2.3 MW Hywind in 2009 off Stavanger, Norway (400 million NOK, US$71 million), in 220 m of water; it survived 40 m/s wind and 19 m waves.
- Permission for the Scotland farm was received in 2015; budgeted cost NOK 2 billion (£152m). Turbines assembled at Stord, Norway in summer 2017 with the Saipem 7000 crane. Each turbine held by three suction anchors (16 m high, 5 m diameter, 300 tonnes).
- LCoE about £180/MWh vs about £55/MWh for fixed offshore; partly offset by £165.27/MWh in Renewable Obligation Certificates.
- Survived Hurricane Ophelia and Storm Caroline (gusts 160 km/h, waves 8.2 m) by shutting down in worst conditions.
- Successor Hywind Tampen (88 MW, concrete foundations) operational 2023 in Norway, NOK 8 billion.
- May 2024: all 5 turbines towed to Norway for several months of heavy maintenance replacing main bearings; all operating again by October 2024.

wikis.title: Pierce Manufacturing launches Phase I of its High Flow production line
wikis.summary: Press release (March 25, 2026) on Pierce Manufacturing's new High Flow custom chassis line at Appleton, Wisconsin, part of a $150 million modernization.
wikis.body:
- APPLETON, Wisconsin (March 25, 2026): Pierce Manufacturing Inc., an Oshkosh Corporation (NYSE:OSK) business, announced the successful launch of Phase I of its High Flow production line at its Appleton campus, modernizing custom chassis assembly.
- Part of a multi-year modernization and an ongoing $150 million investment across facilities in Wisconsin, Florida and Tennessee to expand capacity, improve quality and cut fire apparatus lead times.
- The model focuses on balanced workloads, in-line quality controls and integrated technology; Phase I adds digital work instructions, improved tooling, ergonomic workstations and advanced inspection technologies.
- "Subsequent phases will transform the remaining final assembly operations in the second half of 2026."
- Marty Bass, president: lead times already reduced "by more than three months from their peak".
- Across operations Pierce has added more than 500,000 sq ft of facility space, invested over $70 million to date and hired approximately 800 new team members.
- Other Appleton investments: automation, robotics, fabrication technologies, expanded paint capacity.
- Boilerplate: Pierce is "the leading North American manufacturer of custom fire apparatus" and was first to introduce frontal airbags and Side Roll Protection on fire apparatus. Oshkosh employs over 18,000 worldwide.

wikis.title: Pierce Manufacturing (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Pierce Manufacturing, Oshkosh's Appleton, Wisconsin fire and rescue apparatus maker founded in 1913.
wikis.body:
- U.S. subsidiary of Oshkosh Corporation, based in Appleton, Wisconsin; makes customized fire and rescue apparatus. Founded 1913 by Humphrey Pierce and son Dudley as Pierce Auto Body Works Inc., building truck bodies for the Ford Model T.
- Infobox: revenue US$1 billion (2016); 2,600 employees (cited 2021).
- From the 1960s to early 1980s known for custom bodies on commercial chassis. Acquired wholly by Oshkosh in 1996. September 2021: took an ownership interest in Boise Mobile Equipment (BME), Idaho.
- The Arrow name (first custom chassis, 1979) has no affiliation with the Pierce-Arrow Motor Car Company of Buffalo.
- Aerial partners over the years included Snorkel, Pitman, LTI, Smeal, Bronto Skylift and Nova Quintech (assets acquired 1997); it now builds aerials in-house. Bradenton, Florida site makes the Saber chassis and Responder line.
- Page says (Dec 4, 2017) Pierce was the largest U.S. manufacturer of firefighting apparatus (citation needed); largest municipal fleet is Fairfax County, Virginia.
- Products: custom chassis (discontinued: Arrow, Contender, Dash, Quantum, etc.), aerials, pumpers, tankers, rescues, wildland, homeland security vehicles, foam systems, and Pierce Voltera electric truck.
- Page carries maintenance notices: relies on a single source; may contain original research.

wikis.title: Europa-Park: history, operator and growth to 2024
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on Europa-Park in Rust, Germany, covering its 1975 founding, expansion, fires, Rulantica and operator details.
wikis.body:
- Theme park in Rust, Baden-Württemberg, Germany; 95 hectares, twenty themed areas, around 100 attractions, fourteen roller coasters; six hotels, a camping site, tepee village, cinema and conference center. Owner: Mack family; season April to early January.
- Attendance 5.4 million in 2022 (over 6 million with Rulantica). AECOM 2020: 19th of 25 most-visited parks worldwide, third in Europe after Disneyland Paris and Efteling, most visited seasonal park in the world. Amusement Today Golden Ticket jury voted it best theme park in the world for the eighth year in a row in 2022.
- Founding: Franz Mack took over the family firm (now Mack Rides) in 1958; with son Roland (b. 1949) he visited the US in 1972. Planned first for Breisach (named after the Europaweiher, commemorating a 1950 poll in which 95.6% favoured European unification), moved ~30 km north to Rust (Balthasar castle park). Opened 12 July 1975 on 16 hectares; 250,000 visitors first year, 700,000 second, over a million in 1978.
- Themed areas: Italy (1982), Holland (1984), England (1988), France (1990), Scandinavia (1992), Spain (1994), German Alley (1996). Over 2 million visitors in 1991. First hotel in a German theme park, El Andaluz, 1995. 3.1 million visitors by 2001; first German theme park to operate in winter (180,000 visitors). MackMedia founded 2002.
- 2012: 90 hectares, eleven coasters, five hotels, turnover close to EUR 300 million, 3,000+ employees. 2017: Voletarium opened, "biggest flight motion simulator theater in Europe".
- 26 May 2018 fire near Holland and Scandinavia areas destroyed a building and part of Scandinavia; tens of millions of euros damage; seven firefighters minor injuries; park reopened next morning. Police said a technical failure in the fjørd water ride caused it. Scandinavian area and Pirates in Batavia reopened July 2020. Snorri Tours dark ride added 2019.
- Rulantica water park opened 28 November 2019, estimated cost EUR 180 million, 30+ slides. 2019 attendance over 5.7 million; 2020 and 2021 averaged around 2.75 million due to COVID-19.
- 2022: Jungle Rafts rethemed as Josefina's Magical Imperial Journey after colonial-Africa criticism; Eatrenalin restaurant opened; Croatia area construction began.
- 19 June 2023 control-room fire (believed corroded wiring), park evacuated, 450 responders, two firefighters lightly injured, reopened next day.
- 26 April 2024: Voltron Nevera powered by Rimac opened in the Croatian area (17th themed zone), delayed from 2023 by supply difficulties.
- Operator: Europa-Park GmbH & Co Mack KG; managing directors Roland, Jürgen, Thomas and Michael Mack. FY2020/21 revenue EUR 149,665,000; ~4,500 employees (2022). Park is now 21 themed areas (2026), 18 of them European countries/regions.

wikis.title: Europa-Park's 50th anniversary and the Mack family's plans
wikis.summary: IAAPA article (23 September 2025) profiling Europa-Park at 50, its growth, hotels, Rulantica and upcoming Monaco area.
wikis.body:
- IAAPA Funworld article by Juliana Gilling, September 23, 2025, on Roland Mack (co-founder, age 75, former IAAPA chairman and Hall of Fame member) and the Mack family.
- Next addition: a Monaco-themed area set to open in 2026, which will be the park's 21st themed area. Roland on what his late father Franz would say: "I think he'd say it's become too big."
- Opened July 12, 1975 on castle gardens in Rust after the 1972 US tour. Early skepticism: "News headlines predicted bankruptcy"; banks would not back it; the Macks put everything on the line, including the family home. Visitors: about 250,000 in 1975, 700,000 a year later, one million in 1978. Daily attendance now exceeds 20,000; site grown from 16 to 130 hectares; nearly 150 million visitors since debut.
- Mack family engineering dates to 1780 when Paul Mack began building wagons in Waldkirch.
- Rides named: Blue Fire Megacoaster, Silver Star, Pirates in Batavia (rebuilt after 2018 fire), Voltron Nevera powered by Rimac. Dining: two-star Michelin restaurant Ammolite; Eatrenalin. HALLOWinter event in November.
- Rulantica (2019) cost 180 million euros; mascot Snorri, a six-armed octopus. Krønasår four-star hotel opened same year. Six hotels, 5,800 beds combined, occupancy above 90%. Silver Lake City camp resort rebranded, accommodation for over 2,000 guests from 2026; new 120-room Riverside Western Lodge next year; Jürgen Mack predicts a 250-300 room hotel within five to 10 years.
- Management: Ann-Kathrin Mack joined brothers Michael and Thomas as managing partner, first woman on the management board in almost 250 years; Frederik Mack to steer HR, finance and controlling. MACK One umbrella covers MACK Rides, MACK Solutions, MACK Animation, MACK Research, 2112 Studios, MACK Connect. MACK Magic with Warner Bros. Film Productions Germany: animated movie "Grand Prix of Europe" starring mascots Ed and Edda; Grand Prix EDventure dark ride.

wikis.title: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Ferrari World, the mostly indoor Ferrari-themed park on Yas Island, opened 4 November 2010.
wikis.body:
- Mostly indoors theme park on Yas Island, Abu Dhabi, UAE; "the world's first Ferrari-themed park". Area 86,000 m2; owner Miral under license from Ferrari.
- Foundation stone laid 3 November 2007; developed by Aldar Properties, constructed by BESIX Group subsidiary Six Construct; three years to develop; opened 4 November 2010.
- Home of Formula Rossa, which held the world's fastest roller coaster record from 2010 until Falcons Flight opened.
- Six coasters: Fiorano GT Challenge (2010, Maurer Söhne), Formula Rossa (2010, Intamin), Flying Aces (2016, Intamin wing coaster, "world's tallest non-inverting loop"), Turbo Track (2017, Intamin), Formula Rossa Junior (2020, Zamperla), Mission Ferrari (opened January 2023, Dynamic Attractions).
- Other attractions: Viaggio in Italia (flying theater), Scuderia Challenge simulator, Roof Walk (90-min, 600 m), Zipline (400 m), Karting Academy, Turbo Towers drop tower, Made in Maranello factory tour, Junior GP, Nello's Adventureland, cinema film on Enzo Ferrari.
- Part of Yas Island complex with Yas Waterworld, Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi and Yas Marina Circuit.
- Awarded best theme park in the Middle East by World Travel Awards for eight consecutive years.

wikis.title: TARMAC Aerosave inaugurates its seventh maintenance hangar
wikis.summary: AviTrader report (9 October 2024) on TARMAC Aerosave's new EUR 15 million hangar at Teruel, Spain.
wikis.body:
- On October 8, 2024, TARMAC Aerosave inaugurated its seventh maintenance hangar, the fourth at Teruel, Spain. Built in a record nine months; "now the largest metal-textile hangar in the world". Investment: EUR 15 million.
- Company now has four hangars in Teruel, two in Tarbes and one in Toulouse. The original hangar (holds two A380s) is fully booked for the next two years.
- Dimensions: 95 m long, 85 m wide, nearly 34 m high; fits an Airbus A380 plus up to four A320s; over 7,700 m2 for aircraft maintenance.
- Design: steel and aluminium frame, Rockwool insulation panels, fully dismantlable and reusable.
- Fifty positions to be available at Teruel, where the company employs over 230 of 530 total staff, the largest employer at Teruel airport.

wikis.title: New John Deere W, T and S-Series combines for Europe (2012 season)
wikis.summary: Stackyard news item (2011-07-15) describing John Deere's new 11-model combine range for the 2012 harvest.
wikis.body:
- Dated 2011-07-15. New W, T and S-Series combines for European crops, 260 to 625 hp (ECE R120), for the 2012 harvest season.
- Top S690: most powerful combine engine, largest grain tank 14,100 litres (10 tonnes), emptied in 105 seconds. W and T-Series: active separation areas up to 3.36 m2; 11,000-litre tank, largest on a straw-walker machine.
- Range: W540, W550, W650, W660; T550, T560, T660, T670; S670, S680, S690. S-Series get a 66 cm rubber track option (road speeds to 30 kph, 3.42 m transport width), Variable Stream Rotor, platforms up to 10.7 m (35 ft).
- Engines: Stage IIIB John Deere PowerTech PSX 6.8, 9.0 or 13.5 litre, no urea (DOC + DPF).
- Transmissions: ProDrive (S680/S690), three-speed Push Button Shift (S670, T-Series). New Premium cab with 30% more space; GreenStar 3 CommandCenter; optional GreenStar 2630 with HarvestSmart, AutoTrac.
- Cleaning shoe 19% larger sieve; chopper with 44 winged knives spreading up to 9 m. HillMaster self-levelling compensates slopes up to 15% (22% with SlopeMaster).
- JDLink telematics free for the first year on new W, T and S combines.

wikis.title: Liebherr presents the LTM 1750-9.1 all-terrain crane at Customer Open Days
wikis.summary: Hub-4 news item (2 July 2012) on Liebherr's new 750-tonne nine-axle LTM 1750-9.1, shown at Ehingen on 13-14 June.
wikis.body:
- On 13 and 14 June (2012), at the Ehingen plant, Liebherr showed the new LTM 1750-9.1 to more than 2,000 customers worldwide. The 750-tonne, nine-axle crane sits between the LTM 1500-8.1 and LTM 11200-9.1.
- The complete telescopic boom (52 m) can be carried on public roads. Heights under hook up to 154 m, outreach up to 112 m; luffing fly jib to 91 m in 3.5 m steps; fixed lattice jib up to 62 m; 56-tonne auxiliary jib; Y-guying system.
- Travel weights: 108 tonnes gross with 12 tonne axle load; 99 tonnes / 11 tonnes with supports removed; can be dismantled below 40 tonnes.
- Sets up rear supports itself with an optional support; superstructure engine and hydraulics transported separately; crane functions can be run from the carrier engine by re-plugging three electrical connections (a first for this model).
- Carrier engine: eight-cylinder Liebherr diesel, 500 kW / 680 HP, 3,000 Nm; 12-speed ZF-TC-Tronic. Superstructure engine: four-cylinder, 270 kW / 367 HP, 1,720 Nm; four simultaneous working movements. Four rear axles actively steered; five steering programs.

wikis.title: Siemens Vectron locomotive: design, variants and homologation
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on the Siemens Vectron modular locomotive family introduced at InnoTrans 2010, covering design, variants and certification.
wikis.body:
- Vectron is a locomotive series by Siemens Mobility, introduced at InnoTrans 2010 in four prototype versions: diesel, multi-system, AC and DC electric. Bo'Bo', modular, successor to the EuroSprinter family; Smartron, a cheaper basic version, introduced 2018. The diesel version was replaced in 2018 by a dual-mode locomotive.
- Data (electric): length over buffers 18.980 m, width 3.012 m, height 4,248 mm, weight ~80-90 t, max axle load 22.5 t, power 5.2 or 6.4 MW, starting tractive effort 300 kN, top speed 160, 200 or 230 km/h. Catenary: 1.5 kV DC, 3 kV DC, 25 kV 50 Hz AC, 15 kV AC.
- Variants: MS (multi-system, Class 193/1293/383, up to 6,400 kW, 230 km/h with Vectron 230 package); AC (Class 193/1193/EB); DC (5,200 kW, Class 191/170); Smartron (83 t, 160 km/h, "capriblue", Class 192 / 080); DE diesel (MTU 16V 4000 R84, 2,700 kW, Class 247); Dual Mode Diesel (Class 248/3193); Dual Mode Light (Cummins QST30-L, 120 km/h, Class 249); Dual Mode Electric/Battery.
- Testing: first AC and multisystem locomotives presented at Wegberg-Wildenrath in June 2010. A modified Vectron was tested in the Channel Tunnel over 25-26 January 2013.
- Certification: Romania 2012; Poland (DC) 2012; Germany (AC) December 2012; Austria early 2013; Sweden April 2013; Hungary late 2013; Norway July 2014; Turkey November 2014; Czech Republic March 2015; Slovakia May 2015; Italy (DC) July 2015; Croatia and Slovenia September 2015; Netherlands (MS) September 2017. A Siemens press release at 500 locomotives sold cited further homologations for Bulgaria, Serbia and Switzerland.
- Orders start with Railpool (6 AC, 2010), FuoriMuro (2 DC, 2012) and DB Cargo Polska (23 DC, 2012).

wikis.title: Polymetal installs the Amursk POX-2 autoclave
wikis.summary: International Mining item (17 Aug 2020) on the autoclave vessel installed at Polymetal's Amursk POX-2 site.
wikis.body:
- Posted 17 Aug 2020. Polymetal announced the autoclave vessel was installed at the Amursk POX-2 construction site on schedule.
- POX-2 processes double-refractory ore, aimed at having 100% of the company's refractory ore processed in-house. Versus POX-1 it runs at two times higher pressure and 40 C higher temperature, with a larger, more advanced autoclave lined with titanium rather than brick.
- Group CEO Vitaly Nesis: milestone accomplished "on time despite the COVID-related restrictions and complex logistics"; "start-up in Q3 2023".
- Autoclave: assembled by Coek Engineering in Belgium; 50 m long, 6 m diameter, 1,100 t, "the largest in the gold industry globally"; steel with titanium lining; up to 240 C and 45 bar.
- Shipment took 55 days and 25,000 km: Antwerp in late May, to De Kastri (Tatar Straits), river barge to Amursk, then multi-axle trailer. Equipment and logistics cost about $27 million.

wikis.title: Chornobyl New Safe Confinement construction project
wikis.summary: Chornobyl NPP web page describing the New Safe Confinement (NSC) built over Unit 4's Shelter Object, its design, milestones and results.
wikis.body:
- After the 1986 accident the ruins of Unit 4 were enclosed in the Shelter Object, which does not meet safety norms and has "an undefined lifetime"; the NSC was chosen as the way to reduce hazard significantly.
- Design: arch main building with 257 m span, 108 m height, 162 m length; a technological building (decontamination, fragmentation, packaging, etc.); auxiliary facilities.
- 10 August 2007: contract signed between SSE "Chornobyl NPP" and consortium NOVARKA (VINCI Construction Grands Projets and Bouygues Travaux Publics). First metal structures delivered 13 February 2012.
- 29 November 2016: arch installed in design position. 45 donor countries plus Ukraine pledged more than 1.5 billion euros; about 10,000 workers from 40 countries (5,000 Ukrainians).
- Effects: gamma radiation in former arch construction zone down on average 10 times; contaminated water pumped in first half of 2017 down more than 4 times; releases down on average 5 times.
- 8 November 2017: "Enclosing Perimeter" accepted into operation. 10 July 2019: NOVARKA handed over the NSC to Chornobyl NPP. 24 April 2020: NSC commissioned in trial operation.
- Functions: limit radiation impact, contain radioactive substances, enable dismantling of unstable structures and retrieval of radioactive materials, monitoring, prevent unauthorized access.

wikis.title: Chernobyl arch reaches its resting place
wikis.summary: EBRD press release (29 Nov 2016) on completion of the sliding of Chernobyl's New Safe Confinement over reactor 4.
wikis.body:
- 29 Nov 2016, EBRD Press Office: a ceremony marked the conclusion of the sliding operation, thirty years after the disaster. The NSC moved 327 metres from its assembly point to its final position, enclosing the 1986 makeshift shelter.
- Next: equipment connected to a new technological building serving as control room; the NSC will be hermetically sealed; handover to Chernobyl NPP expected in November 2017 after testing and commissioning.
- Size: "largest moveable land-based structure ever built": span 257 m, length 162 m, height 108 m, 36,000 tonnes equipped; lifetime of 100 years.
- Built by Novarka (VINCI Construction and Bouygues Construction); works started 2010; cost EUR 1.5 billion. Part of the EUR 2.1 billion Shelter Implementation Plan (300+ projects) financed by the Chernobyl Shelter Fund, established 1997, over EUR 1.5 billion from 45 donors; the EBRD manages it and is the largest contributor to the NSC.
- Quotes: EBRD President Sir Suma Chakrabarti expects completion "on time and within budget a year from now"; ChNPP Director-General Igor Gramotkin: "We were building it for our children, for our grandchildren and for our great-grandchildren."

wikis.title: Ariane flight VA261, the last Ariane 5 launch
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on VA261, which launched Heinrich Hertz and Syracuse-4B on 5 July 2023 as the 117th and final Ariane 5 flight.
wikis.body:
- Ariane 5 ECA+ flight VA261 (serial no. 5119), operator Arianespace, from ELA-3, Guiana Space Centre, 5 July 2023 at 22:00 UTC. Payloads: Heinrich Hertz (DLR) and Syracuse-4B (DGA). Outcome: success; "the 117th and last Ariane 5 rocket launch".
- Preparation: in May 2023 the core stage arrived at Kourou; boosters and cryogenic upper stage integrated soon after. Launch set for 15 June was delayed by a problem in the booster separation system; next date 4 July; rollout 3 July; postponed one day for weather.
- Launch called perfect after delivering payloads to the desired orbit.
- Afterwards there were concerns about European launcher availability: Vega C had suffered a failure on VV22 (Pléiades Neo 5 & 6), Ariane 6's first flight was delayed, and only two Vega flights remained in the manifest.

wikis.title: Ariane 5 to retire after 27 years of service
wikis.summary: Spaceflight Now piece (4 July 2023) on the final Ariane 5 launch VA261 and the rocket's record.
wikis.body:
- Published July 4, 2023 (Clive Simpson). Final Ariane 5 to lift off from Kourou, French Guiana, no earlier than July 5, carrying French military satellite Syracuse 4B and German communications satellite Heinrich Hertz to geostationary transfer orbit; 65-minute window 2200-2305 UTC; weather delayed launch from July 4. The launch had been delayed two weeks "because of faulty pyrotechnical transmission lines".
- Record: debut June 1996 failed; second launch a year later partially successful; then 96-percent success rate; final launch is the 117th (two failures and three partial failures in total). Operated by Arianespace for ESA. Up to 10 tons to GTO.
- Missions: XMM-Newton, Envisat, Rosetta, Herschel, Planck, BepiColombo, JUICE (launched April 2023, EUR 1.6 bn / $2 bn, eight-year voyage to Jupiter), five ATV cargo missions to the ISS, and the James Webb Space Telescope (25 Dec 2021), whose precise orbit doubled its estimated lifetime to 20 years.
- Only Ariane 5 ECA remained operational; earlier 5G, 5G+, 5GS and 5 ES were retired.
- ESA's Toni Tolker-Nielsen: "Ariane 5 leaves behind an incredible legacy". Veteran Stephan Osmann: "You can feel that something big is coming to an end."

wikis.title: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Monaco museum of marine sciences inaugurated in 1910 by Prince Albert I.
wikis.body:
- Museum of marine sciences in Monaco-Ville (Le Rocher), part of the Institut océanographique; established 1910; inaugurated by Prince Albert I, who invited leading oceanographers to develop a future Mediterranean Commission (now the Mediterranean Science Commission).
- Jacques-Yves Cousteau was director from 1957 to 1988. Centenary celebrated March 2010 after extensive renovations.
- Collections: sea fauna, model ships, skeletons, tools, weapons, pearl/mollusc/nacre objects. First floor "A Sailor's Career" on Albert I's work, including the laboratory of the yacht L'Hirondelle (observations there led to understanding anaphylaxis; Charles Richet Nobel Prize 1913).
- Basement aquarium: four thousand species of fish and over 200 families of invertebrates; Mediterranean and tropical ecosystems. Artists shown include Damien Hirst and Philippe Pasqua.
- Architecture: Baroque Revival facade 279 feet (85.04 m) above the sea; took eleven years, 100,000 tons of stone from La Turbie; names of twenty oceanographic research vessels chosen by Albert I inscribed in the frieze.

wikis.title: Prince Albert I of Monaco and the Oceanographic Museum
wikis.summary: Institut océanographique biography page on Prince Albert I (1885-1910 activity), founder of the Monaco Oceanographic Museum.
wikis.body:
- From 1885 Albert I planned a marine biology laboratory in Monaco; his collections at the 1889 Paris Universal Exhibition drew great interest, leading to the museum project. Foundation stone 25 April 1899. Page gives inauguration as "March 29, 1910" in one place and "March 25, 1910" in another; the Paris Oceanographic Institute (now Maison des Océans) was inaugurated 23 January 1911.
- Worked with Professor Milne-Edwards of the Museum of Natural History in Paris to create "a temple entirely dedicated to the sea".
- 25 April 1921: gave the "Studies of the Ocean" speech (in English) to the US National Academy of Sciences in Washington, warning of overexploitation of resources by new technologies such as steam trawlers; received at the White House by President Harding; awarded the Agassiz Medal.
- Nicknamed "Prince of the Seas"; became Prince of Monaco in 1889; gave the principality a constitution; founded an International Institute of Peace; campaigned with Zola and Clémenceau for a review of Dreyfus's trial. Died June 26, 1922.

wikis.title: Alstom press release: V150 TGV sets 574.8 km/h world rail speed record
wikis.summary: Alstom press release (3 April 2007) on the V150 record run at 574.8 km/h by RFF, Alstom Transport and SNCF.
wikis.body:
- 3 Apr 2007: new world rail speed record of 574.8 km/h set at 13h13 on the East European LGV, by the V150 trainset, jointly by Réseau Ferré de France (RFF), Alstom Transport and SNCF.
- Previous record: 515.3 km/h, held since 18 May 1990 by SNCF's no. 325 TGV Atlantique trainset at PK 166 near Vendôme.
- Test programme began 15 January 2007; over 300 engineers and technicians; over a 14-month period of project work; 40 trial runs above 450 km/h, over 200 hours of tests and 3,200 km covered.
- V150 trainset: 2 TGV POS power cars, 3 TGV Duplex coaches and 2 latest-generation AGV motorized bogies; total output 19.6 MW (25,000 horsepower). On-board laboratory analysed data from 600 sensors.
- Quotes from Hubert du Mesnil (RFF), Philippe Mellier (Alstom Transport) and Anne-Marie Idrac (SNCF CEO), who names four priority areas: life on board, safety & performance, journey and environment.

wikis.title: Project V150: the 2007 TGV world rail speed record
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Operation V150, the 2007 LGV Est trials in which a modified TGV reached 574.8 km/h.
wikis.body:
- V150 (150 = target speed in m/s): trials on the LGV Est before its June 2007 opening, by SNCF, Alstom and RFF between 15 January and 15 April 2007. Official record on 3 April 2007: 574.8 km/h (159.7 m/s, 357.2 mph) at kilometre point 193 near Le Chemin, between the Meuse and Champagne-Ardenne TGV stations, beating 515.3 km/h set in 1990.
- Unofficial breaks of the 1990 record: 554.3 km/h on 13 February 2007; last 542.9 km/h on 15 April 2007. Cumulative distance at 500 km/h or more: 728 km.
- Train: TGV POS trainset 4402 power cars with three modified Duplex cars and two AGV-style powered bogies; 265 tonnes; 19.6 MW (26,300 hp) versus 9.3 MW for standard POS; 15% drag reduction from aerodynamic changes; 600+ sensors; wheels 1,092 mm instead of 920 mm.
- Track: 140 km section of track 1; catenary raised to 31 kV from 25 kV and wire tension to 40 kN from 25 kN (transverse wave speed 610 km/h); superelevation increased. Acceleration over 70 km; a TGV POS set 4404 swept the track at 380 km/h before each run; an Aérospatiale Corvette aircraft chased some runs.

wikis.title: MTU Friedrichshafen: history and ownership
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on MTU Friedrichshafen (MTU Solutions), the Maybach-founded German engine maker now owned by Rolls-Royce.
wikis.body:
- MTU Friedrichshafen GmbH, trading as MTU Solutions; German maker of commercial diesel engines, generators and molten carbonate fuel cells (trains, ships, oil and gas, military vehicles, agriculture, mining, construction). Headquarters Friedrichshafen; owner Rolls-Royce Power Systems; CEO Joerg Stratmann.
- Founded 23 March 1909 by Wilhelm Maybach with son Karl as Luftfahrzeug-Motorenbau GmbH (Bissingen an der Enz, part of Zeppelin corporation), making airship engines; moved to Friedrichshafen 1911/12; renamed Maybach-Motorenbau 1918. MTU means Motoren- und Turbinen-Union.
- Timeline: 1966 merger with Mercedes-Benz Motorenbau; 1969 renamed Motoren und Turbinen-Union Friedrichshafen; 1989 into DASA; 1994 cooperation with Detroit Diesel; 1995 direct Daimler-Benz subsidiary; 2001 renamed MTU Friedrichshafen GmbH; 2005-06 sold to EQT, core of Tognum; 2009 centenary and Series 1600; 2011 Rolls-Royce and Daimler announced buying Tognum; 2014 renamed Rolls-Royce Power Systems, 100% Rolls-Royce Holdings from 26 August.
- Produced tank engines in WWII and supplied the Leopard 2. Criticism section: makes the MT-883 engine for Israel's Merkava Mk. 4 and 5 tanks; cites a Pentagon $73.5 million contract report (23 February 2026) and NGO/UN sources on the Gaza war.
- Page carries an "needs more citations" notice.

wikis.title: Rolls-Royce marks 25 years of mtu Series 2000 and Series 4000 engines
wikis.summary: Rolls-Royce press release (27 October 2021) on the 25th anniversary of the mtu Series 2000 and 4000 engines.
wikis.body:
- 27 Oct 2021. More than 100,000 engines sold, over 320 million operating hours. Rolls-Royce Power Systems has shipped 52,000 Series 4000 engines and over 65,000 Series 2000s.
- Unveiled by MTU Friedrichshafen at the SMM shipping show in Hamburg in October 1996; the Series 4000 diesels were "the first of their kind to feature common-rail injection as standard".
- Series 4000: 8, 12, 16 or 20 cylinders, 720 to 4,300 kW. Series 2000: 8, 10, 12, 16 or 18 cylinders, 452 to 1,939 kW. Share a common platform. Uses: gensets, haul trucks, yachts, locomotives, ferries, construction vehicles.
- Gas version of Series 4000 launched 1999; first mobile marine use on 1 July 2020 on two Doeksen ferries in the Netherlands; below IMO III limits without aftertreatment.
- Both series to be certified for sustainable fuels from 2023 ("carbon-neutral operation possible from 2023"). Series 4000 yacht/commercial-vessel engines reached EPA Tier 4 certification.
- Quotes: Otto Buecheler (development), Andreas Schell (CEO Rolls-Royce Power Systems), Dr Otto Preiss (COO). Examples: Ferretti custom-line 106 yacht (32.79 m, 26.0 kn) with Series 2000 M97L; Hitachi EH4500 dump truck with 16V 4000 C21L (2014 kW) at Lumwana mine, Zambia.

wikis.title: ADAC Air Rescue orders 14 EC145 T2 and 3 EC135 P2e helicopters
wikis.summary: HeliHub/Eurocopter item (13 Sep 2012) on ADAC's framework order signed at ILA Berlin.
wikis.body:
- 13-Sep-2012 (source: Eurocopter). ADAC Air Rescue signed an order under a framework agreement for 14 EC145 T2 and three EC135 P2e, delivery between 2013 and 2017, at the ILA Berlin Air Show; signed by Stefan Wessling (ADAC) and Wolfgang Schoder (Eurocopter).
- Part of renewal of the BK117 fleet. ADAC has 49 helicopters (32 EC135s with over 100,000 flight hours); commitment to new helicopters and SAR equipment "over 130 million euros"; more than 40 years of cooperation with Eurocopter.
- EC145 T2: two Turbomeca Arriel 2E engines with FADEC, Fenestron tail rotor, four-axis autopilot, new avionics. EC135 P2e: increased maximum takeoff weight; more than 1,000 EC135s in service.
- Yellow livery "yellow angels", IFR and night vision goggle certified; more than 35 bases in Germany, four in collaboration with neighbouring countries.

wikis.title: Eurocopter EC145 / Airbus Helicopters H145: development and origins
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on the EC145 (now H145) twin-engine light utility helicopter, covering its origins and development.
wikis.body:
- Twin-engine light utility helicopter by Airbus Helicopters (formerly Eurocopter) with Kawasaki. First flight 12 June 1999 (Donauwörth); introduced 2002; 1,600 built (June 2023). Based on MBB/Kawasaki BK 117 C1 (originally BK 117 C2); EC145 T2 renamed H145 in 2015; 2020s update with fenestron and 5-blade main rotor. Up to nine passengers plus two crew; used for EMS, SAR, corporate, and military (H145M, UH-72 Lakota; US operates nearly 500 with National Guard).
- Built from the EC135 cockpit/avionics and BK 117 rear section ("90% a combination"); noise reportedly 60% lower than BK 117 C1. December 1997: French Defense and Civil Guard selected it, 31 ordered to replace Alouette IIIs for $170 million.
- Certification: German LBA and Japanese CAB December 2000; FAA January 2002. Workshare: Eurocopter 60%, Kawasaki 40%; partnership extended to at least 2025 (announced August 2010).
- EC145 T2 unveiled at Heli Expo 2011 with Arriel 2E engines, dual FADEC, Fenestron, 4-axis autopilot; EASA certification April 2014, FAA October 2014. Donauwörth is the main plant; 50 T2s planned for 2015, rising to 70 per year.
- Optionally piloted vehicle variant in development since 2011, test flights from 2013.

wikis.title: Salamanca (locomotive), 1812 rack steam locomotive
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Salamanca, the first commercially successful steam locomotive, built 1812 for the Middleton Railway.
wikis.body:
- Built 1812 by Matthew Murray of Holbeck (Fenton, Murray and Wood) for the edge-railed Middleton Railway between Middleton and Leeds; "the first commercially successful steam locomotive", predating Stephenson's Rocket by 17 years. First to have two cylinders (8"x20"); loco weight 5 tons; gauge 4 ft 1 in (1,245 mm).
- Named after Wellington's victory at the Battle of Salamanca (1812). First rack and pinion locomotive, using John Blenkinsop's patented rack: a rack outside the rails engaged by a cog wheel on the left side. Four such locomotives were built; service of up to twenty years.
- Appears in the first painting of a steam locomotive (George Walker watercolour, 1813, in The Costume of Yorkshire).
- Salamanca was destroyed six years later when its boiler exploded; George Stephenson told a parliamentary committee the driver had tampered with the safety valve.
- A model built by Murray in 1811, held by Leeds Industrial Museum, is "the world's oldest model locomotive".

wikis.title: The Salamanca: the world's first commercially successful steam locomotive
wikis.summary: Real Yorkshire blog post (26 May 2020) telling why and how the Salamanca was built for the Middleton coal mine in 1812.
wikis.body:
- Blog post by timbarber, May 26, 2020 (updated Dec 17, 2020), after a visit to the Middleton Railway, Leeds.
- Trevithick's first steam locomotive (1804) could pull only about four times its weight. At Middleton, horses hauling coal were short of fodder because of the Napoleonic Wars demand; mine owner Charles John Brandling; manager John Blenkinsop devised and patented a rack and pinion system (cog wheel engaging a toothed rail) to improve adhesion.
- Blenkinsop engaged Matthew Murray (Fenton, Murray & Wood, Holbeck). Murray built The Salamanca, a two-cylinder engine, delivered to Middleton in 1812 with metal track and toothed rail; named after the Duke of Wellington's victory earlier that year.
- "An immediate success, being able to pull over 20 times its own weight." Quotes Annals of Philosophy, September 1814. The rack system was obsolete by the late 1830s as adhesion locomotives spread under George Stephenson. Author: "not the first locomotive" but the world's first working commercial one.

wikis.title: The history of London Bridge station
wikis.summary: Network Rail history of London Bridge station from its 1836 opening to the 2018 Thameslink redevelopment.
wikis.body:
- London Bridge is "the capital's oldest railway station". First station opened at Tooley Street on 14 December 1836 by the London & Greenwich Railway (LGR), with two platforms and no trainshed; the LGR leased its line and terminus to other companies.
- The London & Croydon Railway opened its own building north of the LGR station in June 1839. By the 1840s four companies used the viaduct; in 1844 the companies swapped stations to avoid dangerous track crossings. A joint terminus opened 1844 but was only partially built; in 1846 the LCR and London & Brighton merged into the LBSCR, and the South Eastern Railway (SER) left for Bricklayers Arms, later returned. LBSCR demolished the unfinished building in 1849; in 1850 the SER built a dividing wall and its own terminus.
- 1864: SER side became a through station via Charing Cross extension; LBSCR remained a terminus. 1923: Southern Railway took control and opened the wall and built a footbridge. 1940: bomb damage. Late 1960s: British Rail redevelopment with new concourse, office block and bus station, opened 1978.
- Thameslink Programme: since 2013 a five-year, GBP 1bn redevelopment completed 2018, with new Tooley Street and St Thomas Street entrances, a unified concourse and step-free access to every platform; officially reopened by Prince William on Wednesday 9 May 2018.
- Did you know: the first section of the London & Greenwich Railway opened from Spa Road, Bermondsey to Deptford in February 1836, making Spa Road technically the first station in the capital (closed 1838).

wikis.title: London Bridge station redevelopment (Network Rail, Thameslink Programme)
wikis.summary: Railway Technology project profile of the GBP 500m London Bridge station redevelopment, 2013 to 2018.
wikis.body:
- Published on the page as April 15 2012.
- London Bridge station, "built in the 1830s", is one of the oldest stations in the world; south-east of London Bridge on the River Thames, near Tooley Street. Managed by Network Rail.
- Opened 1836 (first opened December 1836 as London and Greenwich railway station). Currently 15 platforms (six through, nine terminating).
- Redevelopment: start 2013, completion 2018, estimated investment GBP 500m ($795.1m), part of the GBP 6bn ($9.5bn) Thameslink Programme. Contractors: Costain, Balfour Beatty, Invensys Rail.
- Station handles up to 42 million passengers a year; expected capacity of 50 to 75 million a year after completion.
- Plans prepared April 2011; contractor selected November 2011; Southwark planning committee approved in December 2011. Main construction "expected to begin after the completion of the Olympic Games, in summer 2013", initial works started 2011.
- Phase 1 (done 2012): new street-level concourse, removing railway arches at Stainer Street and Weston Street; the largest concourse in the UK, adding 66% more space. New entrances at Tooley Street and St Thomas Street and a permanent Stainer Street walkway.
- Phase 2 (2013): realign all tracks, add three more through platforms, giving nine through and six terminating platforms.
- Phase 3: undulating canopies over the full platform length; first new platform to open spring 2014. Station to stay fully operational throughout.
- July 2011: Invensys Rail awarded the re-signalling design and delivery contract.
- History: 1839 Croydon station; joined 1844, demolished after six years; 1851 SER and LBSCR stations; LBSCR rebuilt 1853, extended 1866; 1978 GBP 21m re-signalling by British Railways.

wikis.title: Seaway Heavy Lifting takes delivery of crane vessel Oleg Strashnov
wikis.summary: April 2011 news item on delivery of the new-build DP3 crane vessel Oleg Strashnov and its first scheduled projects.
wikis.body:
- Seaway Heavy Lifting took delivery of its new-build DP3 crane vessel Oleg Strashnov; sea trials and test lifts were completed over the previous two weeks.
- DNV witnessed a 5,500 mt overload test; the 800 mt auxiliary hook and 200 mt whiphoist were tested earlier in the month.
- Sailing speed 14 knots.
- First project scheduled for April 2011: installing Sheringham Shoal Windfarm mono pile foundations, transition pieces and substation decks. Then scheduled to install the Clipper deck "later this Summer".
- Dated April 1, 2011.

wikis.title: Oleg Strashnov (Wikidata item Q30133800)
wikis.summary: Wikidata record for the ship Oleg Strashnov, IMO 9452701, built in 2011.
wikis.body:
- Description: ship built in 2011; IMO 9452701.
- Manufacturer: Royal IHC. Service entry: 2011. Yard number 7716.
- Port and port of registry: Limassol; country of registry: Cyprus.
- Length 183.00 metre; beam 47.00 metre; draft 13.84 metre; gross tonnage 47,426.
- Call sign 5BNL2; MMSI 212905000; DNV Vessel register ID 26865.
- Also categorised as Seaway Strashnov (ship, 2011); Wikipedia pages in German, French, Ukrainian.

wikis.title: First Volvo truck built at New River Valley plant returns home
wikis.summary: Aug. 22, 2018 article on a 1982 Volvo F7 donated to the Volvo Trucks Customer Center beside the New River Valley plant.
wikis.body:
- Volvo Trucks North America welcomed the first Volvo truck to roll off the assembly line at its New River Valley facility in Dublin VA: a 1982 Volvo F7.
- Donated by the Wilson family, founders of the former Wilson Trucking Corporation; it will reside at the Volvo Trucks Customer Center adjacent to the plant.
- Wilson Trucking bought the first Volvo F86 sold in the United States in the 1970s; in 2011 it took delivery of the 500,000th US-built Volvo truck.

wikis.title: Airbus inaugurates A320 structure assembly line in Hamburg
wikis.summary: Airbus press release of 01 October 2019 on its automated A320 Family fuselage structure assembly line in Hamburg.
wikis.body:
- Airbus inaugurated a highly automated fuselage structure assembly line for A320 Family aircraft in Hamburg, with a focus on longer sections for the A321LR.
- Features 20 robots, a new logistics concept, automated positioning by laser measurement and digital data acquisition.
- Initial section assembly uses a modular lightweight system called "Flextrack": eight robots drilling and counter-sinking 1,100 to 2,400 holes per longitudinal joint.
- Next step: 12 seven-axis robots join centre and aft fuselage with the tail, drilling, sealing and inserting 3,000 rivets per orbital joint.
- New logistics: separated logistics and production levels, demand-oriented replenishment, autonomous guided vehicles.
- Facility joins fuselage shells into sections and sections into fuselages, equips them with systems, and delivers them to final assembly lines in France, Germany, China and the U.S.
- COO Michael Schoellhorn: "an essential enabler for the A320 Family ramp-up".
- A320neo Family has captured more than 6,500 orders from over 100 customers.

wikis.title: Airbus opens new A320 fuselage assembly line in Hamburg (Simple Flying)
wikis.summary: Simple Flying report of 2 Oct 2019 on Airbus's new automated A320 fuselage line in Hamburg and A320 family orders.
wikis.body:
- Published Oct 2, 2019 by Joanna Bailey.
- Airbus opened a new assembly line for the A320 family using digital automation; hoped to improve efficiency and cut long lead times.
- Joins fuselage shell elements into sections and whole fuselages, fits mechanical and electrical systems, then ships to final assembly lines in France, China, Germany and the US.
- Flextrack: eight robots drilling 1,100 to 2,400 holes per joint; then 12 robots combining rear, centre and tail sections, about 3,000 rivets per joint.
- Quote from COO Michael Schoellhorn on setting new standards in A320 Family production.
- Neo range has more than 6,600 orders; customers named: IndiGo 440 (A320neo and A321neo), AirAsia 395, Wizz Air 276.
- Airbus backlog around 7,172 aircraft, 5,810 of them A320 family. Planned rise from 60 to about 65 aircraft per month by 2022.

wikis.title: Hebron topsides joined to gravity based structure at Bull Arm
wikis.summary: CBC News, Dec 15 2016: Hebron oil project topsides attached to the concrete GBS at Bull Arm, Newfoundland and Labrador.
wikis.body:
- Hebron topside facilities were attached to the concrete gravity based structure (GBS) at Bull Arm "this week"; work completed Dec. 13 and 14 per ExxonMobil Canada, the lead partner.
- NOIA's Bob Cadigan: "It's a very, very key milestone of the project."
- Method (Geoff Parker, Hebron senior project manager): topsides picked up with two barges and floated over the GBS; GBS then deballasted to lift the topsides off the barges.
- Hook up and commissioning to continue until the middle of 2017, when the complete platform will be towed to the Hebron field.
- ExxonMobil said in June the $14B project was 80 per cent complete and on track for first oil in late 2017.
- Cadigan: shift from development phase to operations phase with fewer people working "for the next 30 years".

wikis.title: Fagioli and RINA Services on Hebron platform topsides installation
wikis.summary: RINA press release of 04 Jan 2017 on verification of heavy lifting and transport of Hebron topsides.
wikis.body:
- Hebron oil field is offshore Newfoundland and Labrador, in the Jeanne d'Arc Basin; stand-alone concrete gravity based structure; first oil scheduled for late 2017.
- Fagioli (Italian heavy transport and lifting) was contracted for lifting and installing the topsides and partnered with RINA Services for verification.
- A 45,000 tonne Utilities Process Module was shipped from Korea to Bull Arm by Heavy Transport Vessel.
- The Living Quarter Module (more than 4,000 tonne) was installed with a heavy lifting barge; RINA analysed barge stability, weather-induced motions, design and structure.
- Quotes from Dino Cervetto (RINA Services), Andrea Massera and Paolo Cremonini (Fagioli): the phase was "a great success".

wikis.title: The opening of the Forth Bridge (Network Rail)
wikis.summary: Network Rail story of 4 March 2019 on the Forth Bridge, opened 4 March 1890, with history and dimensions.
wikis.body:
- Published 4 March 2019. Forth Bridge opened March 4 1890; 200 trains use it each day, carrying three million passengers a year (Transport Scotland).
- First major British structure made of steel (53,000 tonnes); completed a continuous East Coast route London to Aberdeen.
- History: Bouch's suspension bridge begun 1878, halted after the Tay Bridge collapse in December 1879, abandoned 1881. John Fowler and Benjamin Baker designed a cantilever bridge; contract to Arrol & Co of Glasgow 1882, work started 1883.
- Three double cantilevers with two 1,700ft suspended spans, then the longest in the world. Rail level 150ft (46m) above high water; towers 361ft (110m) above high water, 137 metres foundations to top. Total length 2,467 metres; main structure 1,630 metres. Cost GBP 3m; 4,600 workers at peak.
- Prince of Wales (later Edward VII) opened it, driving a gold-plated final rivet, and knighted Benjamin Baker.

wikis.title: 4 March 1890: The Forth Bridge is opened (MoneyWeek)
wikis.summary: MoneyWeek on-this-day feature on the Forth Bridge's opening and its background in the Tay Bridge disaster.
wikis.body:
- Last updated 4 March 2020, by Chris Carter.
- The Prince of Wales opened the Forth Bridge in Scotland on 4 March 1890; described as the longest bridge in the world (over a mile and a half).
- Work began in 1882 nine miles west of Edinburgh; the Tay Bridge collapsed in 1879 (designer Sir Thomas Bouch, largely blamed, died months later); Bouch's Forth design was halted.
- Sir John Fowler and Sir Benjamin Baker produced a cantilever design using the latest steel manufacture. Finished November 1889, officially opened March 1890.
- Rumour: painting never ends, giving "painting the Forth Bridge".

wikis.title: AIDAnova handed over to AIDA Cruises
wikis.summary: Meyer Werft press release of 12.12.2018 on handover of AIDAnova, the world's first LNG cruise ship.
wikis.body:
- Dated 12.12.2018: Meyer Werft (Papenburg) handed over the world's first LNG cruise ship to AIDA Cruises (Rostock) in Bremerhaven; largest cruise ship built in Germany.
- Passed three North Sea sea trials. Engine room unit made at Neptun Werft, Warnemuende; four dual fuel engines from Caterpillar (Kiel/Rostock) can run 100% on LNG at sea and in port.
- First of three new ships for AIDA; the others (over 183,000 GRT, more than 2,500 cabins each) due end of 2021 and 2023. Six other ships for Carnival Corporation ordered at Papenburg and Meyer Turku.
- Received innovation grants from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWi) and Lower Saxony.

wikis.title: Mercedes-Benz Woerth plant: first truck produced 60 years ago
wikis.summary: Daimler Truck press release of 23.07.2025 marking 60 years since the first complete truck was built at Woerth.
wikis.body:
- Dated 23.07.2025. In July 1965 the Woerth workforce assembled the first complete truck to roll off the line there, a green Mercedes-Benz LP 608.
- Production began almost two years earlier, October 1963, with around 100 employees; initially truck cabs, delivered to Gaggenau (heavy trucks) or Mannheim (medium and light trucks). From 1965 Woerth became the focus of commercial vehicle production.
- Originally planned as a "production plant for aggregates"; Daimler-Benz realigned its commercial vehicle strategy in the early 1960s so Woerth became the large-scale plant for all truck classes.
- More than 4.4 million trucks built in over 60 years, more than 800,000 of them Completely Knocked Down kits for overseas assembly.
- Today builds Actros, Arocs, Atego, plus Econic, Unimog and Zetros. Series production: eActros 300/400 from 2021, eEconic in 2022, eActros 600 celebrated at end of 2024.

wikis.title: Survivor R protected vehicles delivered to Saxony State Police
wikis.summary: Army Recognition item of 15 Dec 2017 on Rheinmetall handing the first of two Survivor R vehicles to Saxony police.
wikis.body:
- On 15 December 2017 Rheinmetall transferred the first of two heavily protected Survivor R transport vehicles to the Saxony State Police; the second was to follow before Christmas. Saxony ordered them from Rheinmetall MAN Military Vehicles (RMMV) in February 2017 as part of an anti-terror package for special police units.
- Developed with Achleitner, a maker of special vehicles. Used to carry police special operators or evacuate persons from danger zones.
- Features: special signalling system, remotely controlled observation turret with optronics and effectors, high-performance loudspeaker, hydraulic rear ramp.
- 340 HP engine, 1,250 Nm torque, 17-tonne vehicle, Euro 6. Armoured monocoque cabin. Built from serial commercial and military components for low lifecycle costs.
- The Berlin State Police have also ordered the Survivor R. Shown at Milipol Paris 2017.

wikis.title: Lufthansa takes delivery of its first A350 (Airbus press release)
wikis.summary: Airbus release of 21 December 2016 on Lufthansa Group's first A350-900 delivery.
wikis.body:
- 21 December 2016. Lufthansa Group, Airbus' largest airline customer, took delivery of its first A350 XWB, first of 25 A350-900s on order.
- First routes: Munich to Delhi and Munich to Boston.
- Rolls-Royce engines; three-class cabin with 48 Business, 21 Premium Economy and 224 Economy seats; new seats, new inflight entertainment and, for the first time, inflight connectivity.
- Carbon fibre fuselage and wings; 25 per cent reduction in fuel burn and emissions.
- Airbus had recorded 810 firm A350 XWB orders from 43 customers.

wikis.title: Lufthansa takes delivery of first A350-900 (World Airline News)
wikis.summary: World Airline News report of December 21, 2016 on Lufthansa's first A350-900 arriving at Munich.
wikis.body:
- First A350 XWB, A350-941 D-AIXA (msn 074), pictured arriving back at Toulouse December 21, 2016 after a training flight; first of 25 A350-900s on order.
- First routes Munich to Delhi and Munich to Boston; Rolls-Royce engines; cabin 48 Business, 21 Premium Economy, 224 Economy.
- Lufthansa: first A350-900 landed at Munich on December 21, 2016; with ten aircraft in total Lufthansa stations "the world's most modern long-haul fleet" at the Munich hub. Flown by Captain Martin Hoell; flight LH 9921 from Toulouse, greeted by water arches from the fire brigade.
- A Lufthansa Christmas angel on board gave a 10,000 euro cheque to a Munich orphanage from help alliance (over 17 years old, 140+ aid projects, 10+ million euros donated).

wikis.title: Knaack-Krane adds Liebherr LTM 1750-9.1 crane
wikis.summary: KHL news item of 14 January 2014 on Hamburg heavy transport firm Knaack-Krane buying a 750 tonne Liebherr mobile crane.
wikis.body:
- 14 January 2014. Knaack-Krane (Hamburg, Germany) added a Liebherr LTM 1750-9.1 wheeled mobile telescopic crane to its fleet.
- 750 tonne capacity, nine-axle carrier, can travel public roads with telescopic boom at 12 tonne axle load, per the manufacturer.
- Spokesperson: it "will enable us to enter into a completely new performance range".
- First job: assembling wind turbines at Stoessen-Teuchern wind farm near Leipzig; also for large prefabricated construction components.

wikis.title: Knaack-Krane adds 750 tonne Liebherr LTM 1750-9.1 (Vertikal)
wikis.summary: Vertikal.net item of 15.01.2014 on Hamburg crane rental firm Knaack-Krane adding a 750 tonne all terrain crane for its 50th anniversary.
wikis.body:
- 15.01.2014. Knaack-Krane (Hamburg, Germany) celebrated its 50th anniversary by adding a 750 tonne Liebherr LTM 1750-9.1 All Terrain crane.
- Nine axles, complies with 12 tonne axle loads, carries its 52 metre telescopic boom on public roads; suited to industrial, construction and wind power jobs.
- After delivery it went straight to assemble wind turbines at Stoessen-Teuchern wind farm near Leipzig.
- Company founded 1963; fleet of mobile cranes from 30 to 750 tonnes, industrial cranes up to 60 tonnes, plus access platforms and heavy haulage trailers.

wikis.title: BMW Group Plant Berlin history (motorcycles)
wikis.summary: BMW Group timeline of the Berlin motorcycle plant by decade, from the 1960s to 2023.
wikis.body:
- Motorcycle production in Berlin since 1967 (per the page's timeline; 42 years of production by 2011).
- 2001 (Feb 6): one-millionth BMW motorcycle made in Berlin, an R 1150 RT auctioned for UNICEF; 2006: first year over 100,000 motorcycles; 2009: 500,000th GS (R 1200 GS) on May 12 and start of S 1000 RR production; 2011: two-millionth motorcycle, Ludwig Erhard Award (Nov 30), C 600 Sport and C 650 GT start Dec 1.
- 2003: Assembly Hall 7 opened (February); 2004: new paint shop.
- 2012: more than 110,000 motorcycles in a year; adjacent property bought, premises 220,000 sqm.
- 2013: R nineT series production; 2014: BMW C evolution electric maxi-scooter series production from April 4.
- 2015: further investment of over 100 million euros; 2016: logistics centre topped out, 36-meter high-bay warehouse, saving up to 500 in-house transports daily.
- 2017: record over 155,000 units a year, 25 models on five assembly lines. 2018: own CHP plant covers one third of electricity, about 7 million euros; R 1250 GS and RT.
- 2019: three-millionth motorcycle (BMW S 1000 RR), 50 years of Berlin motorcycle production. 2020: Covid-19 challenges yet second best sales result in BMW Motorrad history. 2021: fully electric CE 04 production starts. 2023: 100 years of BMW Motorrad.

wikis.title: The BMW motorcycle plant in Berlin-Spandau (BMW Classic blog)
wikis.summary: BMW Group blog history of how the Berlin-Spandau plant grew from aero engines to the world's most advanced motorcycle plant.
wikis.body:
- Apart from the entry-level G 310 R/GS, all BMW motorcycles for the European and North American market are built in Berlin-Spandau.
- Plant began as Brandenburgische Motorenwerke (BRAMO), a Siemens aero engine firm; merged with BMW in 1938 (page also says BMW was acquired in 1939). Built nine-cylinder radial engines up to 1,000 hp for the Junkers Ju-52.
- Post-war: factory pulled down; production restarted 1949 on components and spare parts for Munich.
- First motorcycle assembled in Berlin: BMW R 60/2, 1966. Final assembly moved 6 September 1966; from 1969 every BMW motorcycle made in Berlin; 400 employees built 30 a day, including the R 75/5 with 50 hp.
- 1970: 10,000th motorcycle; halls added 1975 and 1983; 18 March 1991 K 75 RT was BMW's 1,000,000th motorcycle; 2001 millionth "made in Spandau"; 100,000 a year in 2006; two millionth in 2011. Today as many as 700 bikes leave the factory every day.

wikis.title: History of the Sewers of Paris (Musee des Egouts)
wikis.summary: Paris sewer museum's account of the growth of the Paris sewer network through the 19th century and Belgrand's role.
wikis.body:
- In 1800 only 16 km of sewers existed for 550,000 inhabitants. 1806: sewer service entrusted to engineers of the Bridges and Causeways. 1833: first sewer system for rainwater and street water.
- 1865: fresh spring water distributed through the network, with non-drinking water for parks and streets. 1867: during the World's Fair the public could visit galleries whose height had been increased. 1894: final sewers form a complete network ("tout-a-l'egout" era of carrying solid waste and sewage).
- Wastewater irrigation rose until 1909, then declined. Sewers also came to hold drinking water pipes, non-potable water and pneumatic mail; today they house 141,259 km of fibre optics.
- Cholera epidemics in 1832, 1849 and 1884; mortality in Paris was the highest in France since the 18th century.
- Eugene Belgrand, appointed by prefect Haussmann in 1854 to run the Paris water service, set up spring water catchments from 1865 and became head director of Waters and Sewers in 1867; developed cleaning machines.
- Victor Hugo's "The Intestine of Leviathan" quoted throughout.

wikis.title: Wicker Man: creation of Alton Towers' wooden roller coaster
wikis.summary: Blooloop feature (Mar 28, 2018) on how the GBP 16 million Wicker Man woodie at Alton Towers was designed and themed.
wikis.body:
- By Owen Ralph, Mar 28, 2018. GBP 16 million ($22.6m/EUR 18.3m) wooden coaster; first new wooden coaster in the UK for over 20 years (last was Megafobia at Oakwood, 1996).
- Officially launched March 24 after a media preview the previous week; four years in planning. Built by Great Coasters International (GCI). Alton Towers' 10th coaster.
- 795m (2,610ft) of track, 72.5 ft (22m) triple down first drop, three passes through the 15.55-metre tall Wicker Man structure, up to 68km/h (42mph). Three 24-seater trains, theoretical capacity 1,000 passengers per hour. Sits on the site of the former log flume between Mutiny Bay and Katanga Canyon.
- Not based on the 1973 film or 2006 remake; theming by Merlin Magic Making offshoot Studios North, story of the Beornen community. Real flames; the figure is carved render, not wood. Ride experience about three and a half minutes including pre-show.
- Soundtrack by IMAscore; pre-show and AV by Holovis with effects from Back Stage Technologies; Millennium Flyer trains.

wikis.title: Weinberg Tunnel, Zurich (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the 4,800 m Weinberg railway tunnel under Zurich, opened 14 June 2014.
wikis.body:
