wikis.summary: TechRepublic article (Jun 12, 2025) on the o3-pro launch: availability, benchmarks versus o3 and o1-pro, and limitations.
wikis.body:
- OpenAI launched o3-pro, described as "a version of our most intelligent model, o3, designed to think longer and provide the most reliable responses".
- Available to Pro and Team users in ChatGPT and the API; Edu and Enterprise expected "next week".
- Human testers preferred o3-pro over o3: all queries 64%, scientific analysis 64.9%, personal writing 66.7%, programming 62.7%, data analysis 64.3%.
- Pass@1: AIME 2024 o3-pro 93%, o3 90%, o1-pro 86%; GPQA Diamond 84%/81%/79%; Codeforces 2748/2517/1707.
- 4/4 reliability: AIME 90%/80%/80%; GPQA 76%/67%/74%; Codeforces 2301/2011/1423.
- Limitations: temporary chats disabled at time of writing pending a technical issue; no image generation (use GPT-4o, o3 or o4-mini); no Canvas. OpenAI admits it can be slower than o1-pro in some instances.

wikis.title: Products and applications of OpenAI (Wikipedia), incl. GPT-OSS
wikis.summary: Wikipedia overview of OpenAI's products since 2015, reached via the GPT-OSS redirect; its GPT-OSS section covers the open-weight models released August 5, 2025.
wikis.body:
- The page (redirect from GPT-OSS) surveys OpenAI products: reinforcement learning work (Gym 2016, Gym Retro 2018, RoboSumo 2017, OpenAI Five for Dota 2), GPT models, Deep Research, CLIP, DALL-E (DALL-E 3 announced September 2023), Sora and others.
- **GPT-OSS**: open-weight reasoning models released by OpenAI on August 5, 2025, in two variants: gpt-oss-120b (117 billion parameters) and gpt-oss-20b (21 billion). Released under the Apache 2.0 licence (commercial and non-commercial use). OpenAI says they are comparable to o4-mini and o3-mini respectively. gpt-oss-20b is small enough to run on a device with over 16 gigabytes of RAM.
- Deep Research: reports within 5 to 30 minutes; 26.6 percent on Humanity's Last Exam with browsing and Python tools; a lightweight version rolled out to free ChatGPT users in April 2025.

wikis.title: Jensen Huang on AI safety and doubling chip sales at King Charles's AI summit
wikis.summary: Fox Business (Sept 17, 2026) on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's remarks at a Scottish AI summit convened by King Charles III: safety, regulation, energy and expected doubling of chip sales.
wikis.body:
- Published September 17, 2026 (Fox Business, Bradford Betz). Huang spoke at a summit convened by King Charles III at Dumfries House, Cumnock, Scotland (Sept. 17, 2026), alongside leaders from Google DeepMind, OpenAI and Anthropic.
- "I expect Nvidia to sell twice as many chips this next year as we do this year," attributing growth to nations investing in localized AI infrastructure and cloud data centers.
- Safety: "It is the responsibility of the AI companies ourselves to develop the technology safely and to properly test it." "If it's not ready, just hold it back. You should go as fast as you can, but no faster than that." He urged "good old-fashioned engineering".
- Rejected comparison with social media; AI is a foundational technology like an airplane engine; suggested adapting the "incredible number of laws" in sectors like healthcare and transportation.
- Energy: acknowledged an "interesting dichotomy" of AI factories needing immense energy, but argued demand will spark investment in fusion, fission, air and hydro.
- A video clip cited Huang dismissing AI doomsday fears as "not grounded in science".

wikis.title: Huang expects Nvidia to sell twice as many chips next year
wikis.summary: The Next Web (Sept 17, 2026) contrasts Huang's doubling remark at King Charles III's Scotland AI summit with Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance and Europe's AI gigafactory needs.
wikis.body:
- Published September 17, 2026. Huang told reporters at King Charles III's AI summit in Scotland he expects to sell twice as many chips in the coming year (per Bloomberg), citing AI spreading across industries.
- Nvidia's August guidance was 70% revenue growth for its next fiscal year; CFO Colette Kress said it was supply constrained and revenue could double if not. Units and revenue are different measures.
- Nvidia posted $96.2B revenue for the quarter to 26 July (more than double a year earlier) and guided to $108B for the current one.
- Europe plans up to seven AI gigafactories: Commission budget around EUR 30B, roughly EUR 1B of the public share committed; tender call went out 30 July; about 100,000 chips per gigafactory (four times an AI factory); construction of the first starts in 2027, running from 2028; 77 proposals from 16 member states across 60 sites.
- Huang also argued AI should not be regulated like social media and that an unsafe product should be held back; around 30 executives, policymakers and researchers attended. Nvidia shares rose as much as 2.8%, up about 17% this year.

wikis.title: Huang projects $1 trillion in Blackwell and Vera Rubin orders
wikis.summary: TechCrunch brief (March 16, 2026) on Jensen Huang's GTC 2026 keynote projection of at least $1 trillion in orders for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips through 2027.
wikis.body:
- Posted March 16, 2026 (Kirsten Korosec). At the keynote opening GTC in San Jose, Huang projected $1 trillion worth of orders for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips.
- Last year Nvidia saw about $500 billion in demand for Blackwell and upcoming Rubin through 2026. Huang: "right here where I stand, I see through 2027, at least $1 trillion."
- Rubin was first announced in 2024. In January Nvidia said it officially started Rubin production, 3.5x faster than Blackwell on model training, 5x faster on inference, up to 50 petaflops. Production ramp expected in the second half of the year.

wikis.title: Nvidia's first year-ahead forecast: 70% growth, and a defense against 'circular financing'
wikis.summary: Fortune (Aug 26, 2026) on Nvidia's Q2 results and its first-ever full-year guidance of 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, plus its response to circular-financing critics.
wikis.body:
- Published August 26, 2026 (Fortune, Amanda Gerut). Nvidia projected revenue would rise 70% next fiscal year and said demand for AI chips is growing at 100%; stock rose more than 4% after hours.
- 70% "preliminary expectation" exceeded fiscal 2028 analyst projections of roughly $570 billion (44% growth); implies roughly $690 billion to $700 billion. Huang: "we've never forecasted, never guided to a year in advance."
- Q2 revenue $96.2 billion, up 106% year on year (analysts $92.2 billion); non-GAAP EPS $2.22 vs $2.06 to $2.09 expected. Q3 guidance $108 billion.
- Supply constrained: "Even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%."
- Non-hyperscalers are "about half our business, and that's growing 100% a year". Agents use 15 to 100 times more compute than a human user.
- Market cap over $5 trillion. CFO Colette Kress on "circular financing": "We see it differently." Maximum gross guarantee exposure $108.5 billion (mostly credit support for SB Energy's Ohio campus hosting compute leased to OpenAI; $3.5 billion for cloud partner leases). Investments of nearly $50 billion in frontier AI labs; partnership with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Goldman Sachs and KKR to raise more than $500 billion. AI labs to be about a quarter of business next year.

wikis.title: Nvidia CFO predicts 70% revenue jump for fiscal 2028
wikis.summary: CFO Dive (Aug 27, 2026) on Nvidia's fiscal Q2 2027 results, its 70% fiscal 2028 revenue expectation, Vera Rubin and memory-cost pressure.
wikis.body:
- Published Aug. 27, 2026. CFO Colette Kress said Wednesday on the fiscal Q2 call that Nvidia's "preliminary expectation" for fiscal 2028 includes a 70% revenue jump; supply to "remain a bottleneck" at least until the end of that year.
- Huang said full-stack visibility allowed the first full-year forecast; demand is "much greater" than 70% but supply "allows us to confidently deliver 70%."
- Quarter ended July 26: revenue $96.2 billion (fourth consecutive quarter of growth, +106% YoY), net income up 126% to approximately $60 billion. Hyperscale revenue up 13% sequentially to $49 billion.
- Shares spiked nearly 10% on Wednesday per Nasdaq data (as stated by the article).
- $40 billion revenue opportunity for Vera Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs (agentic AI). Kress: Vera Rubin expected "to mark the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history".
- Nvidia announced extended AWS partnership: an additional 2 million GPUs.
- Margin concerns: memory chip "extreme pricing conditions"; memory scarcity is driven by the AI build-out itself.
- Crunchbase: over 70% of Q2 2026 global startup capital went to AI; about a third of global venture funding went to Anthropic.

wikis.title: Germany's first Tranche 4 Eurofighter makes maiden flight
wikis.summary: The Aviationist (Jul 16, 2026) on Airbus's announcement that the first Project Quadriga Tranche 4 Eurofighter for the Luftwaffe flew from Manching.
wikis.body:
- Published July 16, 2026 (Parth Satam). Airbus announced on Jul. 15, 2026 the maiden flight of the first Tranche 4 Eurofighter Typhoon for the Luftwaffe, from Manching, Germany; delivery expected later this year.
- Project Quadriga, announced November 2020: 38 Tranche 4 jets (30 single-seat, eight twin-seat) replacing the oldest Tranche 1 aircraft; Hartpunkt says deliveries complete by 2030.
- Aircraft 34+02, flown by Airbus test pilot Stefan Auer in a Production Flight Acceptance Test of little more than an hour, testing flight characteristics, engines, flight controls, hydraulics, electrics, cockpit, navigation and communications.
- Manching is building 58 Eurofighters: 38 Tranche 4 plus 20 Tranche 5 (contract signed October 2025). Tranche 5 due 2031 to 2034, replacing part of the Tornado ECR fleet; 15 older Eurofighters to be converted to Eurofighter EK SEAD standard.
- Airbus: "a huge step forward for European defense and sovereignty". Quadriga and Spanish Halcon programs create 7,800 direct jobs, add Euro 6.5 billion to GDP and Euro 3.6 billion tax revenue; Tranche 5 and Halcon II: 19,500 jobs, Euro 15.3 billion and Euro 8.2 billion.
- Tranche 4 and 5 carry the ECRS Mk 1 AESA radar, being tested on an Airbus A320 ATRA testbed.

wikis.title: Airbus flies first 'Quadriga' Eurofighter for Germany
wikis.summary: Janes (15 July 2026) on the first flight of the first of 38 Project Quadriga Eurofighters, aircraft 34+02.
wikis.body:
- Published 15 July 2026 (Gareth Jennings). Aircraft 34+02 departed Airbus' Military Aircraft Centre in Manching on 14 July 2026 for a one-hour Production Flight Acceptance Test, ahead of delivery later in 2026.
- Luftwaffe acquiring 30 single-seat and eight twin-seat Tranche 4 jets to replace the same number of Tranche 1 aircraft.
- Jets will have ECRS Mk 1 Step 0 radar (essentially ECRS Mk 0 for Kuwait and Qatar with modifications), later upgraded to Step 1. The Bundeswehr previously told Janes 15 of the 38 are to get Saab Arexis wingtip pods under Eurofighter EK Step 1.
- With 20 Tranche 5 jets ordered in 2025, they will sustain the Luftwaffe Eurofighter force into the 2060s.

wikis.title: Germany's first Quadriga Eurofighter takes maiden flight
wikis.summary: The Defense Post (July 17, 2026) short report on the first Project Quadriga Tranche 4 Eurofighter's maiden flight at Manching.
wikis.body:
- Published July 17, 2026 (Christine Casimiro). The Luftwaffe's first Tranche 4 Eurofighter EF-2000 under Project Quadriga completed its maiden flight at Airbus' Military Aircraft Centre in Manching.
- Berlin ordered 38 Tranche 4 jets in November 2020 (30 single-seat, eight two-seat), replacing retiring Tranche 1 aircraft, per Janes. Airbus said the first aircraft is on track for delivery later this year; all 38 by 2030.
- With 20 Tranche 5 ordered in 2025, planned acquisition totals 58 new-build Eurofighters. Mentions the cancellation of the Franco-German Future Combat Air System has cast uncertainty over Europe's next-generation combat aircraft.
- Tranche 4 primary upgrade: ECRS Mark 1 AESA radar. Expected eventually to carry the Taurus KEPD 350 cruise missile (per Defence Blog).

wikis.title: Mjøstårnet becomes world's tallest timber tower
wikis.summary: Dezeen (19 March 2019) on Norway's Mjøstårnet, verified by the CTBUH as the world's tallest timber building at 85.4 metres.
wikis.body:
- Published 19 March 2019 (India Block). Mjøstårnet in Brumunddal, Norway, designed by Voll Arkitekter for AB Invest, was verified as the world's tallest timber building by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH).
- 85.4 metres high, 18 storeys, cross-laminated timber (CLT) with glulam columns; the third-tallest building in Norway. Contains apartments, the Wood Hotel, swimming pool, offices and a restaurant.
- Took the title from the 53-metre hybrid Brock Commons Tallwood House in Vancouver; Treet in Bergen (49 metres) was previously the tallest all-timber building. Mjøstårnet completed in March 2019.
- Timber structure installed by Moelven Limitre, including elevator shafts entirely of CLT. Built four storeys at a time in five construction stages using internal scaffolding and a large crane; materials sourced locally.
- CTBUH recently revised its guidelines to recognise timber as structural material.

wikis.title: Mjøstårnet: the world's highest timber building opens in Norway (PEFC)
wikis.summary: PEFC case story (15 July 2019) on the opening of Mjøstårnet, an 85.4 m PEFC-certified glulam tower in Brumunddal.
wikis.body:
- Published 15 July 2019. Mjøstårnet is 85.4 metres, "the world's tallest timber building", opened "this spring".
- 18 floors: rentable meeting rooms, five floors of office space, 72 hotel rooms and 33 apartments; about 11,300 square metres of floor area. In Brumunddal, north of Oslo, on a river bank overlooking Norway's largest lake (Mjøsa).
- Designed by Voll Arkitekter, constructed by Hent AS and Moelven Limtre AS. Assembled in five stages, four storeys at a time, without external scaffolding; PEFC-certified glulam structure was pre-assembled at the Moelven factory and on the ground before hoisting.
- Glulam: layers of solid lumber glued together; described as cost-effective and fire resistant; wood stores CO2; glulam production needs little energy.

wikis.title: Lamborghini Huracan Evo debuts with 640 hp
wikis.summary: autoevolution (7 Jan 2019) on the debut of the Lamborghini Huracan Evo: Performante-derived V10, all-wheel steering, performance figures and price.
wikis.body:
- Published 7 Jan 2019 (Andrei Tutu). Huracan Evo is the mid-cycle facelift of the best-selling Lamborghini.
- Engine borrowed from the Performante: 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10, 640 horsepower and 600 Nm. Dry weight 1,422 kg.
- 0-100 km/h in 2.9 s (pre-facelift 3.2 s), 0-200 km/h in 9.0 s (9.9 s), top speed over 325 km/h.
- All-wheel steering and all-wheel torque vectoring; first LDVI central processing unit, second-generation LPI sensors and second-gen magnetorheological suspension; modes STRADA, SPORT, CORSA.
- Aero: no active aero (reserved for Performante); new splitter, Ypsilon-shaped intakes, rear slotted active spoiler mention, diffuser; Lamborghini says downforce and efficiency improved "more than five times over the first generation". New colour Arancio Xanto.
- Cabin: new 8.4-inch touchscreen with multi-finger gestures and voice commands.
- Deliveries "kick off this Spring", prices from $261,274.

wikis.title: Frankfurt Airport Terminal 3 foundation engineering
wikis.summary: Fraport's Terminal 3 site page on the excavation, sheet-pile walls, underwater concreting and divers for the foundation of the new terminal.
wikis.body:
- Terminal 3 is called Europe's largest privately funded infrastructure project. Building permit issued 2012 after more than 15 years of planning; groundbreaking October 5, 2015 with about 400 Fraport employees (600+ guests in total) incl. CEO Stefan Schulte and Hesse governor Volker Bouffier.
- Dry excavation: pit 5.5 m deep, just above the water table, area given as 65,900 m2 in the intro and 69,500 m2 (nine soccer fields) later; five excavators (up to 2 m3 shovels), three bulldozers; done in half a year; up to 5,500 m3 or about 300 truckloads per day.
- Special foundation work from mid-2017: sections dug 8 to 11 m below the water table, enclosed by 7,100 tonnes of steel sheet piles up to 14 m long (46,000 m2 of walls), held by 550 anchors.
- Underwater concreting: about 3,500 uplift anchors; 39,000 m2 of concrete poured underwater with certified divers (gear up to 35 kg, 12 kg helmet; about a metre visibility). Underwater concrete flowed into the last flooded pit in October 2019. Groundwater is returned via a percolation system.
- Two subterranean levels for equipment so check-in to boarding is on a single level. Site is the former Rhein-Main Air Base (US Air Force 1945 to 2005).

wikis.title: Porsche Taycan production starts September 9 at new factory
wikis.summary: Electrek (Sep 6, 2019) on Porsche confirming Taycan production start on September 9 at a new Zuffenhausen plant.
wikis.body:
- Published Sep 6 2019 (Fred Lambert). After the launch that week, Porsche confirmed Taycan production starts September 9 at its new factory. Wednesday's unveiling covered the Turbo and Turbo S.
- New plant at Zuffenhausen built over four years: body shop, paint shop, electric-motor and component plant, assembly hall and transport technology. Albrecht Reimold: "We've built a factory inside a factory".
- Capacity 20,000 to 40,000 units annually depending on demand. Deliveries first in Europe; North America early next year.
- Electrek's take: price starts at $150,000 up to $200,000; the writer thinks about 20,000 a year is more reasonable.

wikis.title: Porsche Taycan enters production in Zuffenhausen
wikis.summary: Motor Authority reports that first customer Porsche Taycan cars started production on Monday, 9 September 2019, on schedule.
wikis.body:
- First customer examples of the Taycan electric sport sedan began rolling off the line on Monday, the automaker confirmed (article dated September 9, 2019).
- Built in a new wing of Porsche's main plant in Zuffenhausen, Germany, construction of which commenced about four years earlier.
- Plant uses renewable energy for power and heating to ensure CO2-neutral production.
- Decision to build was made shortly after the Mission E concept was previewed at the 2015 Frankfurt show; in 2017 a source said production would start just before the 2019 Frankfurt show, so no delay occurred.
- Planning involved city sustainability requirements and more than 130 companies, mostly suppliers; production went smoothly while the rest of the plant ran at full capacity.
- First Taycans reach US dealerships in December as 2020 models, initially Taycan Turbo and Turbo S.
- Prices: Turbo from $152,250 (launch pricing $154,660); Turbo S $186,350 (launch $188,960). Both 616 hp standard; with launch control Turbo 670 hp, Turbo S 750 hp.

wikis.title: Olympia Looping (Five Loops) at Oktoberfest
wikis.summary: Oktoberfest.de describes the Olympia Looping, billed as the largest transportable roller coaster in the world with five inversions.
wikis.body:
- Described as the largest transportable rollercoaster in the world and the only one with five full inversions.
- History: first looping coaster in Germany premiered 1978; two loops the year after; since 1989 Barth's Olympia Looping has been the largest transportable coaster and the only one rolling over five times.
- Ride is 1,250 m long with five loops; speeds up to 100 km/h; up to 5.2 g.
- Up to five trains can run at once, each seating 20 to 28 people.
- Children 8 and older may ride; under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.
- Erection and dismantling take one week each with 10 full-time fitters; the site could hold 33 three-room apartments; it weighs as much as 900 mid-class cars or 150 African elephants; moved by train it takes 50 wagons loaded with 20 large containers.

wikis.title: Olympia Looping travelling roller coaster (Coasterpedia)
wikis.summary: Coasterpedia entry on the Olympia Looping, a travelling steel coaster with five inversions, covering its specs, history, Prater and London appearances and a 2008 incident.
wikis.body:
- Steel travelling coaster owned by R. Barth and Sohn KG; manufacturer BHS; designers Ing.-Buro Stengel GmbH and Schwarzkopf; opened 17 September 1989 (debuted at the 1989 Oktoberfest).
- Specs listed: 1,250 m long, 32.5 m tall, 80 km/h, 5 inversions, 28 riders per train (7 cars), duration 1:45, booster wheel lift hill; the text calls it the largest portable roller coaster in the world (4,101 ft track, mass 900 tonnes) with up to 5.2 g.
- 2013: renovation with full repaint and LED lighting.
- March 2016: announced it would sit at Prater (Vienna) for the summer season for the park's 250th anniversary; appeared there until 15 March-24 August 2025, when the park said it would likely be the last time because a theatre is being built on its site.
- Since 2016 it travels to Hyde Park Winter Wonderland, London, as 'Munich Looping', its first time leaving mainland Europe; present at every Winter Wonderland since (semi-confirmed 5 November 2016).
- Incident: on 27 September 2008 a driving motor failed, stranding over 20 Oktoberfest attendees at the top of the first hill; freed by the Munich fire department.
- Usually runs 5-car trains away from Oktoberfest; extra cars were brought for London.

wikis.title: Visiting the HMS Erebus wreck with Adventure Canada (2019)
wikis.summary: A guest's account, published 5 August 2020, of Adventure Canada's Out of the Northwest Passage expedition becoming the first public visitors to the HMS Erebus wreck site in 2019, with Parks Canada.
wikis.body:
- Article by Bunny Laden, August 05, 2020. In 2019 guests on Adventure Canada's Out of the Northwest Passage expedition (ship Ocean Endeavour, September 2019) became the first public visitors to the HMS Erebus wreck site, in partnership with Parks Canada.
- Background stated: Franklin set sail in 1845; ships ice-bound in 1846 near King William Island; Franklin died 1847; crew abandoned ships in 1848. Erebus rediscovered September 2014 near Uqsuqtuuq (Gjoa Haven), Nunavut; Terror located September 2016 to the north; Inuit oral history was instrumental.
- Adventure Canada reportedly made five unsuccessful attempts before this sixth succeeded.
- Visit: guests went by Zodiac to the Research Vessel David Thompson and the Research Barge Qiniqtiryuaq (Inuktitut: 'searching for something or someone which was lost'), a floating station above the wreck with three containers (archaeology lab, air compressor/warm water circulator for divers, dive-monitoring). Finds that day included a boot, a bottle and an unidentified metal object. Divers wear warm-water suits.
- Inuit Guardians work with Parks Canada to monitor the wreck sites and keep unauthorized people out of the 'do not sail' area; they and Parks Canada gave presentations aboard.
- Page also lists 2027 trips: Into the Northwest Passage (Aug 25-Sep 10, 2027) and Out of the Northwest Passage (Sep 10-26, 2027), from $18,995 to $37,495 USD per person.

wikis.title: Emma Maersk, world's largest containership, enters service
wikis.summary: Professional Mariner (27 February 2007) describes Maersk's Emma Maersk, delivered 1 September 2006, with dimensions, capacity and machinery.
wikis.body:
- Delivered Sept. 1, 2006 at A.P. Moller-Maersk's Odense Steel Shipyard, Denmark; described as 'very large'.
- 1,303 ft long, 184 ft beam, 22 container rows across (four more than the next largest ship in service).
- Capacity about 11,000 TEUs including one thousand 40-ft reefers; some experts suggested as many as 13,000 TEUs.
- Highly automated; crew of 13.
- Engine: Wartsila 14-cylinder RT-flex 96C low-speed diesel, 80,080 kW (108,920 bhp) at 102 rpm, built by Doosan, 2,300 tons; common-rail. Two shaft electric motors; five diesel generators totalling 20,700 kW plus a 8,500 kW gas/steam turbine generator; waste heat recovery up to about 12% of main engine power.
- Two bow and two stern thrusters of 25 tons each; active stabilizer fins; silicone antifouling coating; Maersk estimated fuel savings of 1,200 tons annually; fuel tanks placed centrally.
- Operates on Maersk's Europe-Far East service.

wikis.title: Tonsberg, Wilhelmsen's Mark V ro-ro, the largest afloat
wikis.summary: Motorship article on Wilh. Wilhelmsen's first 'Mark V' Panamax ro-ro Tonsberg, claimed to be the largest of its type afloat, with its specifications.
wikis.body:
- Wilh. Wilhelmsen group (Norway) marked its 150th anniversary with the first 'Mark V' Panamax ro-ro, Tonsberg, claimed to be the largest such vessel afloat.
- 31,824 dwt, 265 m long, cargo volume 138,000 m3 over six fixed and three hoistable decks; built at Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Nagasaki; lead ship of a four-ship series ordered by Wilh Wilhelmsen and Wallenius Lines; second vessel due August 2011, last two in 2012 (page date shown only as '15 years ago').
- 5% to 7% more capacity than Mark IV; 15% to 20% less fuel per unit transported.
- Deck area about 50,335 m2 (31,250 m2 for high and heavy cargo); stern ramp 12 m wide, safe working load 505 tonnes (previous 380); headroom up to 7.1 m; crew of 36.
- Engine: single MAN B&W L70ME-C8 7-cylinder, MCR 20,100 kW at 108 rpm; MHI 7.3 m six-blade propeller; service speed 20.25 knots; electric winches used to avoid hydraulic oil spills.
- Serves the Wallenius Wilhelmsen 'Round the World' service, a 110 to 120 day round trip.

wikis.title: MHI RO/RO ship Tonsberg
wikis.summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries product page saying Tonsberg is the world's largest RO/RO ship, completed March 2011 and named Ship of the Year 2011.
wikis.body:
- TONSBERG is described as the world's largest RO/RO ship, built by MHI Group for the Wilhelmsen Group (Norway) and the Wallenius Group (Sweden).
- First of a four-ship order, completed at the Nagasaki Shipyard & Machinery Works in March 2011.
- Awarded 'Ship of the Year 2011' (Japan Society of Naval Architects and Ocean Engineers) for transportation efficiency and environmental performance; the sixth such award for MHI merchant ships since Crystal Harmony in 1990.

wikis.title: Sany opens world's largest excavator factory near Shanghai
wikis.summary: Rental Equipment Register (24 Aug 2012) reports Sany opened what it calls the world's largest excavator factory near Shanghai.
wikis.body:
- Sany says the factory is the world's largest and most advanced excavator plant, able to produce an excavator every five minutes.
- Cost $818.5 million; computerized production management from raw steel plate to final assembly.
- Mainly 20-ton to 30-ton excavators; parts move automatically through underground tunnels.
- Has 43,000 sq ft of gardens, pools, bamboo and marble patios.
- Sany America chairman Tim Frank: the team produces almost as many excavators yearly as sold in the US by all manufacturers; base excavator kits are shipped to Sany America's assembly facility in Peachtree City, Ga.

wikis.title: Ten years of the A400M in the Bundeswehr
wikis.summary: Airbus story (December 2024) listing ten facts on the A400M in German Air Force service since first delivery on 18 December 2014.
wikis.body:
- 18 December 2014: Airbus handed over the first A400M to the Bundeswehr; it landed next day at Wunstorf (LTG 62). As of December 2024, 48 of 53 ordered delivered; 47 at Wunstorf, one at Airbus Seville testing self-protection.
- Over 51,000 flight hours as of November 2024, 25,000 since January 2022.
- Four turboprops of almost 11,000 hp each (44,000 hp); top speed up to 750 km/h; range over 8,700 km; 3,300 km at full 37-tonne payload; can use unpaved runways; 116 paratroopers.
- MedEvac configuration (six units, two intensive care); tanker: 63,500 litres of fuel, refuels two Eurofighters or another A400M.
- Used for humanitarian missions (Kabul, Sudan, Turkey, Libya).
- Airbus is building a new A400M maintenance centre next to Wunstorf, scheduled to start operations in mid-2027; Manching does major checks every six years.
- Future: Global Support Services package, 'Block Upgrade 0', drone 'mothership' tests for FCAS, fire-fighting kit under development.

wikis.title: EMEC grid-connected wave test site at Billia Croo
wikis.summary: EMEC page describing its Orkney wave test site built in 2003, berths, cables and monitoring.
wikis.body:
- Constructed in 2003 at Billia Croo outside Stromness, western edge of Orkney mainland; average significant wave height 2-3 m, extremes up to 18 m (highest EMEC has recorded).
- Five cabled test berths in up to 70 m of water (four at 50 m, one deeper), about 2 km offshore and 0.5 km apart, plus a near-shore berth.
- Five 11 kV subsea cables feed the EMEC substation and the national grid.
- Three waverider buoys, a weather station, SCADA system and CCTV from the Black Craig former coastguard lookout.
- Listed clients include Aquamarine, Pelamis, Wello, Voith, Seatricity and others.

wikis.title: Tarmac Aerosave opens fourth A380-capable hangar in Teruel
wikis.summary: Aviation Week (9 October 2024) reports Tarmac Aerosave inaugurated a fourth A380-capable hangar at Teruel, Spain, on Oct. 8.
wikis.body:
- Unveiled at a ceremony on Oct. 8, 2024 at Teruel airport.
- Fits one A380 or four A320s; built in around nine months for EUR 15 million ($16 million); 95 m long, 85 m wide, about 34 m high; steel and aluminum frame, rock wool insulation, fully dismantlable and reusable.
- Original A380 hangar (room for two) is fully booked for the next two years.
- Teruel: presence since 2013, 230 staff (530 across Spain and France), 50 new roles planned; capacity for 140 aircraft and 20 engines. Third hangar built the prior year.
- Network: seven hangars, two at Tarbes, France, plus Toulouse storage for 40 aircraft.
- Tarmac Aerosave is a joint venture of Airbus, Safran and Suez. CEO Alexandre Brun.

wikis.title: Liebherr Customer Days 2012 at Ehingen: new cranes and four-crane lift
wikis.summary: Vertikal.net (19 June 2012) reports Liebherr's 2012 Customer Days at Ehingen, where it launched three cranes and lifted four cranes in a stack.
wikis.body:
- Fifth Customer Days at Ehingen (first in 1999), over 1,800 visitors on each of two days.
- New cranes: 750 tonne LTM 1750-9.1 all terrain, 220 tonne LTR 1220 telescopic crawler, and flagship 3,000 tonne LR 13000 crawler crane.
- Testing of the LR 13000 completed; first machine sold to Mammoet, being shipped to a refinery job in the USA.
- Demonstration 'four crane mobile': LR 13000 (108 m P boom) lifted an LR 11350, which lifted an LR 1350/1, which lifted an LTR 1100 (62 tonnes). LR 13000 combined load 1,430 tonnes at 30 m radius (capacity 1,521 tonnes, 94%). LR 13000 weighed 2,170 tonnes in this set-up; 5,000 tonnes on the crawlers.
- Specs: max load moment 65,000 tonnes, max under hook height 246 m, max radius 160 m.
- Plans: new 1,000 tonne-class crawler due at Bauma 2013; new five axle MK.
- Ehingen: 840,000 sq m site, 2,800 employees, 44% share of all-terrain market, revenues almost EUR 1.5 billion, about 1,450 cranes delivered in 2012, EUR 30 million investment planned for 2012.

wikis.title: Siemens at InnoTrans 2010: Vectron locomotive and other exhibits
wikis.summary: Article of 20 October 2010 on Siemens' InnoTrans 2010 stand featuring the Vectron locomotive, Inspiro metro, Desiro ML and Sistras storage systems.
wikis.body:
- Vectron, first shown to the industry in June, is for international and national freight and passenger traffic; standard maximum speed 160 km/h, upgradeable to 200 km/h without changing bogies; detachable front deformation zone.
- Inspiro metro: 3 to 8 car trains; wider doors; Syntegra drive reduces energy use by up to 30% and maintenance costs by up to 15%; optional driverless operation.
- Desiro ML for Belgian SNCB: almost 80 m, 280 seats, order for 305 three-car EMUs, delivered during 2010; new diesel-generator set saves up to 30%; over 600 orders confirmed or notified.
- Sistras energy storage: SES (stationary), MES (on board), HES (with traction battery), all using the Sistras ESM 125 core module with double-layer capacitors.

wikis.title: Giant autoclave shipped from Belgium to Russia (Amursk)
wikis.summary: Breakbulk.News (1 December 2020) describes transport of one of the gold mining industry's largest autoclaves from Antwerp to Amursk, Russia.
wikis.body:
- Autoclave for the second line of Polymetal's Amursk Hydrometallurgical Plant.
- Stage 1: from COEK Engineering plant in Geel by hold barge to Antwerp in mid-May 2020, loaded on SAL's heavy lift vessel mv Svenja.
- Sea leg from Antwerp via Suez Canal to De-Kastri took 30 days.
- Stage 2: reloaded onto a Ro-Ro barge selected by general contractor Key Point Logistics with Barrus Projects (no suitable barges exist locally), then via the Tatar Strait and Amur to a purpose-built Ro-Ro berth in Amursk, built for varying Amur water levels.

wikis.title: Mercedes-Benz LP 608 (RoadStars Legends)
wikis.summary: Mercedes-Benz Trucks feature on the LP 608 with short cubic cab, the first truck built at the Woerth plant on 14 July 1965.
wikis.body:
- An identical model rolled off the Woerth plant line on July 14, 1965 as its very first truck.
- Complemented the lower end of the range; permissible gross weight 6.5 tonnes, drivable with a car licence.
- First Mercedes-Benz truck with a four-cylinder direct-injection engine (OM 314): 80 hp at 2,800 rpm, torque 226 Nm, top speed 80 to 95 km/h.
- Only model in its series until the larger LP 808; in the first two years more than 10,000 built, 45 percent market share.

wikis.title: Musee des Egouts de Paris (Wikipedia, French)
wikis.summary: French Wikipedia article on the Paris sewer museum: history of sewer visits since 1867, the 2018-2021 renovation, and the current visit.
wikis.body:
- Located in the 7th arrondissement under esplanade Habib-Bourguiba, facing 93 quai d'Orsay at Pont de l'Alma; infobox gives opening 1867 and 80,000 visitors per year (2017).
- Guided sewer visits began at the 1867 Exposition universelle; Eugene Belgrand (director of water and sewers 1867-1878) had nine special wagonnets built.
- 1906-1939 educational, electric-wagon route; closed during WWII; from 1946 entrance at Concorde; from 1975 a proper museum, boat trip removed.
- Redeveloped 1989; about 95,000 visitors in 2007, 80,000 in 2017; closed summer 2018 for a EUR 2 million renovation (architects Frenak et Jullien) with accessibility and a new reception pavilion; reopened 23 October 2021.
- Since October 2021 open daily except Monday, 10h-17h (last entry 16h); closed when the Seine reaches the foot of the Zouave at Pont de l'Alma; visit 45-60 minutes over 500 m of working sewers, about 13 degrees.
- Galleries: Hugues Aubriot, Bruneseau, Alma vault, Bosquet collector, Belgrand.

wikis.title: Wicker Man wooden roller coaster at Alton Towers
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Wicker Man, a GBP 16 million wooden coaster that opened at Alton Towers on 20 March 2018.
wikis.body:
- Wooden coaster by Great Coasters International, layout by Skyline Design; opened 20 March 2018 after a three-day weather delay (ceremony moved from 17 to 24 March); cost GBP 16,000,000; replaced The Flume (closed October 2015).
- Codenamed 'Secret Weapon 8'; name confirmed 8 January 2018; first UK wooden coaster in 22 years and first to incorporate fire (per the article).
- Planning approved 25 August 2016; construction began 28 November 2016; first timber arrived 4 May 2017.
- Stats: 22 m tall (72 ft), drop 72.2 ft, length 2,608.3 ft (795.0 m), 43.6 mph (70.2 km/h), 0 inversions, duration 1:50, capacity 952 riders per hour, min height 120 cm, 3 trains of 12 cars (24 riders).
- John Wardley criticised the first drop; first two drops were redesigned.
- 26 July 2024: evacuated and closed after smoke from a foreign object on the track; reopened 17 August 2024.
- Ranked fifth for best new ride 2018 in Amusement Today Golden Ticket Awards.

wikis.title: Howrah railway station overview and infobox (part 1)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia intro and infobox for Howrah station in West Bengal, stating it is the largest and busiest railway complex in India.
wikis.body:
- Located in Howrah, West Bengal; also called Howrah Junction; code HWH; operated by Eastern and South Eastern Railway; owner Indian Railways.
- Stated as the largest and busiest railway complex in India and among the busiest and largest in the world; oldest surviving railway complex in India ([citation needed]).
- First public train 15 August 1854 (opened); rebuilt December 1, 1905; electrified December 14, 1957 (3 kV DC), converted to 25 kV AC in 1968; former operator East Indian Railway Company.
- 24 platforms (23 operational per text) and 25 tracks; platforms 650-700 m long; ten platforms suit trains of more than 24 coaches.
- Traffic: infobox 1.8 million passengers per day (2026); text says about 600 passenger trains, more than 1 million passengers a day; 252 Mail/Express and 500 suburban EMU trains daily.
- Connections: Howrah metro, bus depot, ferry ghat.

wikis.title: ITER receives poloidal field coil PF1 from Russia
wikis.summary: ITER newsline (13 Feb 2023): the Russian PF1 coil reached the ITER site on 10 February 2023, completing delivery of all six poloidal field coils.
wikis.body:
- PF1: 9 m diameter, about 160 tonnes; smallest of six ring-shaped magnets, only one not procured by Europe.
- Passed the ITER gates around 4:15 a.m. on Friday 10 February (2023).
- Left Sredne-Nevsky Shipyard, Saint Petersburg on 1 November 2022 after close to six years of fabrication; reached Marseille 9 January 2023; land journey began a month later.
- Convoy took four nights instead of three for the 105 km ITER itinerary (frame over 10 m wide); 288-wheel trailer; 70 Gendarmerie officers.
- Milestone: all seven Members have delivered at least one major component. It is one of 141 Highly Exceptional Loads since January 2015.
- With PF1 stored, all six coils are 'home': PF6 and PF5 installed, PF2 stored, PF3 and PF4 in final stages in Europe's on-site winding facility.
- DG Pietro Barabaschi said ITER would 'build the ITER tokamak'; Anatoli Krasilnikov spoke for Russia.

wikis.title: Rethe-Klappbrucke, Hamburg (German Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: German Wikipedia article on the combined rail and road bascule bridge over the Rethe in Hamburg port, opened for rail on 15 December 2017.
wikis.body:
- Combined rail and road double bascule bridge in the Port of Hamburg over the Rethe at the Reiherstieg, connecting Hohe Schaar and Neuhof; replaces the 1934 Rethe lift bridge (dismantled 2018).
- 104 m span, 64 m channel, unlimited height; road 14 m wide, rail 10 m wide; opens in about four minutes, closes in twice that.
- Built June 2011 to summer 2016; road opened 11 July 2016, rail 15 December 2017; owner Hamburg Port Authority; contractor Arge Rethebrucke (Hochtief, Bilfinger, Waagner Biro).
- Cost rose from EUR 95 million to just over EUR 173 million; called currently the largest railway bascule bridge in the world.
- 20 August 2020 bent hydraulic cylinder failed the road leaf; rail leaf closed from 21 September for at least two weeks; over 50 closures 2017-2020.
- Awards include Deutscher Brueckenbaupreis 2020 (March 2021).

wikis.title: Krupp 80 cm Schwerer Gustav (Dora) railway gun
wikis.summary: Old Machine Press article on the design, specifications and use of the Krupp 80 cm railway gun, including its 1942 firing at Sevastopol.
wikis.body:
- Origin: 1935 Wehrmacht request for ballistics reports; March 1936 Hitler asked Gustav Krupp about beating the Maginot Line; early 1937 design approved and three guns commissioned; first wanted by March 1940; construction started spring 1937.
- Specs: 80 cm (33.5 in) bore, barrel 32.48 m, length 47.30 m, complete gun 1,350,000 kg; 80 wheels; broken into 25 freight cars; about 250 men took 54 hours to assemble; 14 to 16 shots a day.
- Shells: AP 7,100 kg range 38 km; HE 4,800 kg range 47 km.
- 8 January 1942 Schwere Artillerie-Abteilung (E) 672 formed (1,420 men); crews called it 'Dora'.
- Sent to Crimea; first round at Sevastopol 5 June 1942 (14 shots that day); on 6 June hit an ammunition magazine buried 30 m under Severnaya Bay; 48 shells fired in total, only 10 landing within 60 m of target; Sevastopol fell 4 July 1942.
- A few weeks later Gustav Krupp gave it to Hitler as a personal gift.

wikis.title: DLR HY4 hydrogen fuel cell aircraft
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the four-seat hydrogen fuel cell HY4 demonstrator, first flown 29 September 2016 and later flown on liquid hydrogen in 2023.
wikis.body:
- Four-seat hydrogen fuel cell aircraft; technology demonstrator; Germany; built by DLR and Pipistrel; developed from Pipistrel Taurus G4; one built; status 'In development'.
- First flight 29 September 2016 from Stuttgart Airport, powered by gaseous hydrogen; designed by DLR Institute of Engineering Thermodynamics.
- Operated by DLR spinoff H2Fly, it completed the world's first piloted electric flights powered by liquid hydrogen in September 2023, one lasting over three hours.

wikis.title: Eli Electric Vehicles starts production of the Zero
wikis.summary: electrive report (Sept 21, 2021) that Eli Electric Vehicles has begun production of its Zero L6e light electric vehicle, with European sales starting in coming weeks at 11,999 US dollars.
wikis.body:
- Per a TechCrunch report, start-up Eli Electric Vehicles (Los Angeles) has begun production of the Eli Zero, an L6e-class electric light vehicle first shown as a concept at CES 2017. Production partner is to be in China.
- Sales begin "in the coming weeks", initially in small numbers in 13 European countries; starting price 11,999 US dollars (approx. 10,230 euros), before taxes in the US. Distribution via KSR Group, first in Austria, Germany and Switzerland.
- Specs: 2,250 mm long, 1,380 mm wide, 1,588 mm high, wheelbase 1,600 mm; two seats; 160 litres load volume; 4 kW rated motor, top speed 45 km/h. Batteries 5.8 kWh (up to 80 km range) and 8 kWh (up to 110 km); recharge at household socket in 2.5 or 3.5 hours.
- At CES 2017 the top speed was 40 km/h with range up to 100 km.
- Crowdfunding on StartEngine: just over 236,000 US dollars raised in the current campaign, about US$1.4 million earlier, and over US$6.5 million overall.
- CEO Marcus Li said geopolitical tensions and differing state laws on road licensing are reasons for focusing on Europe first; cites 30 km/h limits in Paris, Vienna and Amsterdam.

wikis.title: China rolls out a further 1 trillion yuan in stimulus
wikis.summary: MarketWatch teaser (updated Aug. 27, 2022) on China's surprise announcement of a 1 trillion yuan (about $146 billion) pro-growth stimulus package; the rest is paywalled.
wikis.body:
- Subhead: this latest $146 billion in assistance targets infrastructure, property and private business.
- Just a day after China's central bank reiterated it was sticking to limited stimulus, policy makers surprised observers on Wednesday by announcing 1 trillion yuan (about $146 billion) in pro-growth measures.
- The source says Beijing this year had only implemented occasional policies to kickstart recovery after strict COVID lockdowns and a long-running property crisis slowed growth to a crawl.
- By Tanner Brown; article is cut off by a subscription wall.

wikis.title: UC San Diego opens Pepper Canyon West transfer-student dorm
wikis.summary: EdSource brief (Sept 19, 2024) that UC San Diego opened Pepper Canyon West, a residence hall with 23- and 22-story towers housing 1,310 transfer students.
wikis.body:
- UC San Diego opened the residence hall Wednesday, per The San Diego Union-Tribune; two towers among the tallest such buildings in the U.S.
- Pepper Canyon West has one 23-story tower and one 22-story tower and will house 1,310 upper-division transfer students.
- UC Berkeley recently opened a dorm for transfer students as well.
- Chancellor Pradeep Khosla: "We are not only meeting a critical demand for housing, but also creating a unique opportunity for students to build lasting connections in a beautiful and inspiring place."

wikis.title: Ontario Line costs nearly double after latest contracts
wikis.summary: Toronto Star report (Nov. 23, 2022) that the Ontario Line's cost has risen to $17-19 billion from $10.9 billion after new contract awards.
wikis.body:
- Two contracts awarded in November by Infrastructure Ontario and Metrolinx, plus two more underway, put the cost of the 15-kilometre subway between $17 billion and $19 billion, versus the $10.9-billion price publicized in 2019. Per-kilometre cost is upwards of $1 billion.
- Nov. 17: Connect 6ix got the contract to operate and maintain trains and systems for $9 billion; May's update had put it at "greater than $2 billion".
- Ontario Transit Group won the south stations and tunnels design-build-finance contract for $6 billion, previously "greater than $4 billion". Two north-part contracts expected at $1 billion to $2 billion each.
- Construction began in March; completion not expected until 2031, four years later than planned. Line runs from Ontario Place to the Science Centre.
- Transit expert Steve Munro: "I have a suspicion they goofed." The province blamed rising inflation and supply chain shortages; NDP cited the P3 model and called for more oversight.

wikis.title: Total solar eclipse of July 22, 2028: path map (timeanddate)
wikis.summary: timeanddate page for the July 22, 2028 total solar eclipse path map; the captured text is mostly navigation with few facts on the eclipse itself.
wikis.body:
- Page title: "Total Solar Eclipse on Jul 22, 2028: Path Map & Times", an interactive path map (Leaflet/OpenStreetMap).
- Teaser: "Total Solar Eclipse 2028: The path of totality for this eclipse includes Sydney Harbour."
- Related teasers: the 2026 eclipse was the first totality in mainland Europe since 1999; the 2027 eclipse gives Luxor almost 6½ minutes of totality.
- Also lists upcoming eclipses: Aug 2, 2027 total solar; Feb 6, 2027 annular solar.
- Page shows "Published: Apr 1, 2024" on a related guide.

wikis.title: France conditionally confirmed as 2030 Winter Games host
wikis.summary: Reuters report (July 24, 2024) that the IOC conditionally picked the French Alps for the 2030 Winter Games, pending financial guarantees.
wikis.body:
- IOC session in Paris, July 24, 2024: the French Alps bid won 84 of 88 votes but is conditional on state and regional financial guarantees, which a caretaker government had been unable to deliver after elections.
- Guarantees must be signed by France's prime minister by Oct. 1 and ratified by parliament no later than March 1, 2025. The IOC will not countersign the host city contract (already signed by France) until then. Guarantees include the state's Olympic delivery guarantee and those of Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes and Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur regions.
- President Macron told the session he would ask the next prime minister to include the guarantee and an Olympic Law in priorities.
- French Olympic chief David Lappartient: "Never had an Olympic bid been so fast and then succeeded."
- France previously hosted Winter Games in Chamonix (1924), Grenoble (1968) and Albertville (1992). The project aims to unite the north and south French Alps. By Karolos Grohmann.

wikis.title: Brightline West high-speed rail now expected late 2029
wikis.summary: Planetizen item (Jan 18, 2026) that Brightline West's Las Vegas-Southern California line now has a late-2029 completion estimate, missing the 2028 Olympics.
wikis.body:
- Brightline West announced a new estimated completion date of late 2029, dashing hopes it would be ready for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
- The project started development in 2018 and was delayed by the Covid-19 pandemic.
- Per Newsweek (Sam Stevenson), construction is active at the future Las Vegas station off I-15 near the 215, but track-laying start is not announced.
- Route runs primarily along I-15 between Las Vegas and Rancho Cucamonga, with connection to Metrolink.
- Related items: cost jumped by $5.5 billion, and Brightline West asked USDOT for a $6 billion loan (Oct 6, 2025); groundbreaking April 23, 2024.

wikis.title: Audio-Technica ATH-AL5NC wireless open-back headphones
wikis.summary: Audio-Technica US product page for the ATH-AL5NC wireless open-back headphones, $279.00.
wikis.body:
- Price $279.00. Open-back wireless headphones with 53 mm drivers, weight 240 g, built-in microphone.
- Rechargeable battery up to 75 hours of continuous playback, up to 8 hours from a 15-minute charge.
- Audio-Technica CONNECT app: low latency mode, sound leakage reduction mode, EQ, soundscape function. Hi-res wireless audio.
- Earpads rest around the ears without clamping pressure.

wikis.title: Audio-Technica ATH-M20xSTS StreamSet streaming headset
wikis.summary: Audio-Technica US product page for the ATH-M20xSTS StreamSet streaming headset, $99.00.
wikis.body:
- Price $99.00. Lightweight (230 g / 8.1 oz) streaming headset with boom-arm cardioid condenser mic that mutes when the boom is flipped.
- Modeled after the ATH-M20x studio headphones; 40 mm drivers with enhanced bass; breathable mesh earpads.
- 2 m (6.6') detachable cable with 3.5 mm TRRS mini-plug; USB-C and USB-A adapters included.

wikis.title: Klipsch Reference Signature Series details at CEDIA Expo 2026
wikis.summary: CEPRO (Sept 2, 2026) on Klipsch revealing more of its upcoming Reference Signature Series at CEDIA Expo 2026, launching globally in winter.
wikis.body:
- Klipsch gave more details at CEDIA Expo 2026 after a preview at CES 2026, with invite-only First Listen demos; global launch "in the winter"; final pricing and complete specs to be announced at launch in Winter 2026.
- Six models: floorstanding RS-8301F and RS-6301F; monitors RS-8301M and RS-6301M; center RS-6301C; Dolby Atmos surround/height RS-6101SA.
- Phase-aligned horn design puts the midrange inside the tweeter horn. 8-inch models pair 8-inch woofers with a 6.5-inch midrange; 6-inch models pair 6.5-inch woofers with a 5.25-inch midrange. Titanium-diaphragm Linear Travel Suspension tweeter; spun-copper Cerametallic cones.
- One-piece BMC front baffle, curved cabinet edges, Ebony and Walnut finishes, leather top panel.
- Andy Spalla, Director of Product Management, mentions Klipsch's 80th year. By Nick Boever.

wikis.title: KEF Outdoor Collection and KASA amplifiers
wikis.summary: CEPRO (Sept 1, 2026) on KEF's new outdoor speakers, subwoofers and KASA network DSP amplifiers announced Sept. 1.
wikis.body:
- KEF Outdoor Collection, announced Sept. 1: first time KEF brings Uni-Q to a dedicated outdoor speaker. Models: SR4Q and SR6Q Landscape Satellites, BH6Q and BH8Q Bollard Speakers, BL8b and BL12b Bollard Subwoofers, BQ9 and BQ11 three-way bollards. Existing Ventura 5 and 6 round out the portfolio.
- IP66 or IPX5 ratings, UV-resistant; more than 500 hours salt-spray testing; operating -13°F to 158°F. Outdoor Collection in black; Ventura also white.
- Packaged systems: Landscape P4F (4-inch, 4.1) $2,000 MSRP; P4Q (4.5-inch Uni-Q with amplification) $5,000; P6Q (6.5-inch Uni-Q) $8,000.
- KASA network DSP amplifiers: Class D with GaN, AKM Velvet Sound converters, Music Integrity Engine DSP; browser-based setup; IP controlled. Four planned: KASA 2-250M $1,600; 4-250M $3,200; 8-150M $3,300; 8-250M $4,000 MSRP.
- By Zachary Comeau.

wikis.title: JBL Cove whole-home audio speakers
wikis.summary: JBL product page for the Cove M1, P1 and X1 Wi-Fi speakers and whole-home audio setup via the JBL One app.
wikis.body:
- Cove M1 compact Wi-Fi speaker: $229.95 each, 110W. Cove P1 portable: $399.95, 120W, up to 14 hours battery, IPX56, Dolby Atmos. Cove X1 3D room-filling: $449.95, 200W, Dolby Atmos.
- Multi-room, stereo and surround; pair two M1 or P1 with JBL Bar MK2 soundbars. Moment button, Spotify Tap, JBL One app 3-step setup, Auracast, hi-res over Wi-Fi.
- Tech: Constant Sound Field, AI Sound Boost, Dolby Atmos (P1 and X1).

wikis.title: Street Fighter (2026 film): cast, plot, release
wikis.summary: People article (Sept 6, 2026) on the 2026 Street Fighter movie, in theaters Oct. 16, 2026.
wikis.body:
- Release: theaters Oct. 16, 2026; filmed for IMAX. Set in 1993. Director Kitao Sakurai (previously four episodes of Twisted Metal).
- Trailers: first April 16, 2026; another Sept. 1. First preview at The Game Awards Dec. 11, 2025. Previous film 1994.
- Plot (per Deadline): Ryu and Ken Masters, "estranged Street Fighters", are recruited by Chun-Li for the next World Warrior Tournament and learn of a "deadly conspiracy".
- Cast: Noah Centineo (Ken), Andrew Koji (Ryu), Callina Liang (Chun-Li), Roman Reigns (Akuma), David Dastmalchian (M. Bison), Cody Rhodes (Guile), Andrew Schulz (Dan), Vidyut Jammwal (Dhalsim), Eric André (Don Sauvage), 50 Cent (Balrog), Jason Momoa (Blanka), Orville Peck (Vega), Olivier Richters (Zangief), Hirooki Goto (E. Honda), Rayna Vallandingham (Juli), Alexander Volkanovski (Joe), Kyle Mooney (Marvin), Mel Jarnson (Cammy).
- Produced by Paramount Pictures and Legendary Pictures.

wikis.title: Muraba Veil: one-apartment-wide Dubai skyscraper
wikis.summary: Time Out Dubai (Oct 23, 2024) on the planned Muraba Veil tower by RCR Arquitectes, 380 m tall and 22.5 m wide.
wikis.body:
- Developer Muraba; designer RCR Arquitectes. 73 storeys, 380 metres tall, 22.5 metres wide (the size of a single apartment). 131 units from two- to five-bedroom, each occupying the full width; prices from Dhs18 million.
- Amenities: wellness spa, restaurant, gallery, padel court, private cinema. Facade is a stainless steel mesh "Veil". Beside Sheikh Zayed Road with a view of the Burj Khalifa.
- Completion: "no date has been confirmed at this time".

wikis.title: Thessaloniki metro opens as archaeological window
wikis.summary: Reuters (Nov 30 / Dec 5, 2024) on the opening of Thessaloniki's metro with archaeological finds displayed in stations.
wikis.body:
- The Thessaloniki metro officially opened Saturday, Nov 30, 2024; first such system in Greece outside Athens. Construction began in 2006, took nearly 20 years, partly due to the 2009-2018 debt crisis.
- Workers found a Byzantine-era market and a Roman cemetery; artefacts displayed at stations such as Venizelou. Tunnels dug up to 31 metres (102 feet) deep to run below findings.
- PM Kyriakos Mitsotakis: "It is also a museum." Archaeologist Melina Paisidou criticised moving artifacts rather than leaving them in place.

wikis.title: Eiffel Tower rust and 60 million euro repaint ahead of the 2024 Olympics
wikis.summary: Reuters reports, citing French magazine Marianne, that the rusting Eiffel Tower needs full repairs but is getting a cosmetic 60 million euro paint job.
wikis.body:
- Reuters, PARIS, July 4 (published July 5, 2022): the Eiffel Tower is "riddled with rust and in need of full repairs", but is instead being given a cosmetic 60 million euro paint job ahead of the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, according to confidential reports cited by Marianne.
- The wrought-iron tower is 324 metres (1,063 ft) high, built by Gustave Eiffel in the late 19th century, and welcomes about six million visitors each year.
- Expert reports cited by Marianne suggest the monument is in a poor state. An unnamed manager said: "It is simple, if Gustave Eiffel visited the place he would have a heart attack."
- The repaint is the 20th time the tower has been repainted.
- About 30% of the tower was supposed to be stripped and given two new coats, but COVID-19 delays and lead in the old paint mean only 5% will be treated, Marianne said.
- Operator Societe d'Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel (SETE) could not be immediately reached for comment; it is reluctant to close the tower for long because of lost tourist revenue, Marianne said.

wikis.title: Groundbreaking for American Express headquarters at 2 World Trade Center
wikis.summary: New York governor's press release on the July 2026 groundbreaking of 2 World Trade Center, the future American Express global headquarters.
wikis.body:
- Dated July 9, 2026, Albany, NY: Governor Kathy Hochul celebrated the groundbreaking for 2 World Trade Center, the final commercial office tower on the World Trade Center campus.
- More than 2 million square feet over 55 floors; developed by Silverstein Properties on Port Authority land under a long-term ground lease; design architect Foster + Partners.
- American Express will be sole owner and occupant; completion is "expected to be completed in 2031".
- Located at 200 Greenwich Street; completion is the final milestone in the commercial buildout of the 16-acre campus.
- Headline claims: more than 2,000 union construction jobs and billions in economic impact.
- Quotes: Hochul called it "a major milestone"; Denise Pickett, American Express President of Enterprise Shared Services, said it reaffirms the company's belief in the city (founded 1850).

wikis.title: Multiplex tops out Sapphire by the Gardens towers, Melbourne
wikis.summary: Multiplex news release of 3 August 2022 saying both towers of S P Setia's Sapphire by the Gardens in Melbourne's CBD have topped out.
wikis.body:
- 03 August 2022, Melbourne: Multiplex reached the topping-out milestone on both high-rise towers of S P Setia's Sapphire by the Gardens mixed-use development.
- Location: corner of Exhibition and La Trobe Streets; designed by Fender Katsalidis with Cox Architecture.
- Towers are 232 m and 220 m above street level: a 62-level 5-star flagship Shangri-La Hotel (500 rooms) and a 60-level residential tower with 325 luxury apartments.
- The hotel and residential tower are joined by a Sky Lounge on Level 46 with a glass-floor oculus overlooking the Royal Exhibition Building and Carlton Gardens; the sky bridge is "46-storeys in the air".
- Hotel has champagne gold façade fins and the largest ballroom space in Melbourne's CBD (six-metre-high ceilings).
- S P Setia CEO Datuk Choong Kai Wai: completion will mark their fifth significant Melbourne development. Multiplex's Graham Cottam: constructing two towers simultaneously takes exceptional planning.

wikis.title: MTA begins environmental review of the Interborough Express
wikis.summary: Governor Hochul's 15 October 2025 announcement that the MTA is starting SEQRA environmental review of the Interborough Express in Brooklyn and Queens.
wikis.body:
- October 15, 2025: the MTA began the environmental review of the Interborough Express (IBX) under the New York State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA); the first major milestone after the project entered preliminary engineering and design in August.
- Three public meetings: Wed Oct. 29 at Brooklyn College; Thu Nov. 6 at Christ the King High School, Middle Village, Queens; virtual on Wed Nov. 12.
- Review runs concurrent with preliminary design; it will produce a Draft Scoping Document and ultimately a draft Environmental Impact Statement.
- Hochul: IBX will improve commutes of "over 160,000 daily riders". MTA's Janno Lieber: 900,000 New Yorkers live along the proposed route.
- IBX will connect nearly 900,000 New Yorkers in underserved parts of Brooklyn and Queens to subway, bus and Long Island Rail Road.

wikis.title: Shanghai Tower: height and sustainability facts (ICE)
wikis.summary: Institution of Civil Engineers project page on the 632 m Shanghai Tower, completed 2015, with cost, design and sustainability facts.
wikis.body:
- Shanghai Tower, Shanghai, China: 632 m (2,074 ft), 128 storeys, in the Lujiazui finance and trade zone. Page lists year 2015, duration 7 years, cost US$2.4bn.
- Completed in 2015 and officially opened to the public in 2016; can accommodate up to 16,000 people; owned by the Shanghai city government.
- Structure: nine cylindrical buildings stacked; inner glass facade and outer layer twisting 120 degrees, with nine indoor zones of public space (gardens, cafes, shops).
- Elevators go 73.8 km/h (described as the world's fastest); one of the highest observation decks; 258-room Four Seasons hotel with a pool on the 84th floor, 393 m (1,289 ft) up.
- Tallest of three mega-skyscrapers in the financial district with Jin Mao Tower and Shanghai World Financial Centre.
- Page says it covers 576,000 m2 (about 410,000 above ground, 166,000 below); 60,000 m3 of concrete poured over 63 hours using 450 mixer trucks and eight pumping stations; first high-rise with a cloud computing system serving up to 20,000 people. Goal: the most sustainable building.
- Gensler's Art Gensler at the August 2013 topping out: it "redefines the role of tall buildings in contemporary cities". (The page gives both 127/128 storeys and 125 floors in different places.)

wikis.title: One Vanderbilt, SL Green's supertall in Midtown Manhattan
wikis.summary: Urban Land magazine feature (8 July 2024) on the design, leasing, amenities and observation deck of One Vanderbilt.
wikis.body:
- Urban Land, by Sibley Fleming, July 8, 2024.
- One Vanderbilt opened in 2020 "in the midst of the pandemic"; SL Green's $3.3 billion office tower is the fourth tallest in New York City: 1,401 feet (427 m), 93 stories, 1.7 million sq ft rentable.
- Rents reached $300 per square foot, the highest in the city; 99 percent leased with a weighted average lease term of 15 years.
- Tenants named: TD Securities, Carlyle Group, KPS Capital Partners, Greenberg Traurig, McDermott Will & Emery, DZ Bank.
- SUMMIT One Vanderbilt observation deck spans floors 91-93 and generates north of $100 million annually.
- Architect: Kohn Pedersen Fox (Jamie von Klemperer). Base is cut away on East 42nd Street to preserve the view of Grand Central Terminal; a third-floor cafe with 75-foot glass curtain wall; 14,000 sq ft plaza by PWP Landscape.
- Entire third floor (Vandy Club) is tenant amenities, per developer Robert Schiffer of SL Green.

wikis.title: Salesforce Tower opens for business in San Francisco
wikis.summary: San Francisco Examiner report (13 Jan 2018) that the 1,070-foot Salesforce Tower at 415 Mission St. officially opened, with Salesforce moving in.
wikis.body:
- By Laura Waxmann, Jan 13, 2018: despite ongoing construction, the 1,070-foot-tall Salesforce Tower at 415 Mission St. officially opened on Monday; one tenant had begun moving in.
- Salesforce (anchor tenant) signed a lease in 2014 with Boston Properties and Hines for 714,000 sq ft (32 floors, incl. the 61st floor), since expanded to eventually 36 floors. Building formerly known as the Transbay Tower.
- 1.4 million sq ft of leasing space; 97 percent leased; "We have one floor left" (Helen Han, Boston Properties).
- Construction began in 2013. Salesforce employees occupied two of 61 floors by Friday; CEO Marc Benioff tweeted the "first occupants" as "very historic". Over 600 Salesforce employees to occupy by end of January.

wikis.title: 22 Bishopsgate reaches practical completion
wikis.summary: Multiplex news item of 4 December 2020 announcing practical completion of the 278 m 22 Bishopsgate tower in London.
wikis.body:
- 04 December 2020: Multiplex's team achieved practical completion of 22 Bishopsgate "earlier this week".
- Described as Europe's first vertical village and the tallest tower in the City of London; 278 metres tall; delivers 1,275m sq ft of workspace.
- Led by AXA IM - Real Assets for an international consortium of investors with Lipton Rogers Developments; started onsite January 2017.
- At peak more than 1,200 people worked onsite, over one third from local boroughs; Covid-19 caused disruption.
- Steel-framed tower with central concrete core; three-level basement on piled foundations; tallest building in the world to use the closed cavity facade (CCF) curtain wall system.
- Quote from Andrew Feighery, Project Director, credits Multiplex staff and hundreds of subcontractors.

wikis.title: ProSlide's Siam Park project, Tenerife
wikis.summary: ProSlide project page describing its rides at Siam Park water park on Tenerife.
wikis.body:
- Siam Park, Costa Adeje, Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain) opened in 2008; ranked the #1 water park by Trip Advisor every year since 2014 (page also says over 850,000 visitors annually; approximate attendance 849,900).
- ProSlide and Siam Park began working together in 2008 to develop 11 rides; since then 3 additional projects and 18 signature water rides over 12 years.
- General Manager Christoph Kiessling chose ProSlide for innovation and ability to customize ride paths to difficult hillside topography.
- Lists 17 attractions, including RocketBLAST/FlyingSAUCER 45, TORNADO 24/TornadoWAVE 60, BehemothBOWL 60, MAMMOTH, TORNADO 60, CannonBOWL 40 (x2), FreeFALL, PIPEline (x2), Turbo PIPEline (x2), ProRACER and KIDZ rides.
- Award listed: 2023 IAAPA Brass Ring Award, Best New Product Water Park Ride, Dueling RocketBLAST, Siam Park - Saifa.

wikis.title: Le Commandant Charcot reaches the North Pole
wikis.summary: Seatrade Cruise News report that Ponant's Le Commandant Charcot became the first French and first LNG-powered ship to reach the geographic North Pole.
wikis.body:
- Ponant's hybrid electric Le Commandant Charcot reached the geographic North Pole, 90° North, "this week" - a first for a French ship, and the first LNG-powered ship to do so.
- Reached at 10:38 a.m. Sept. 6 (year not stated in the text), with Capt. Etienne Garcia at the helm and Capt. Patrick Marchesseau at his side.
- Garcia: "I am hugely proud to have been at the helm of the very first French ship to reach the geographic North Pole... the ultimate achievement of a collective adventure started by Ponant many years ago."
- Article by Anne Kalosh, Seatrade Cruise News.

wikis.title: Meyer Werft delivers AIDAnova, first LNG-propelled cruise ship
wikis.summary: Seatrade Cruise News on the delivery of AIDAnova by Meyer Werft to AIDA Cruises after two delays.
wikis.body:
- AIDAnova, described as the world's first LNG-propelled cruise ship, was delivered to AIDA Cruises by Meyer Werft on a Wednesday morning, after two delays (originally set for mid-November; pushed back twice, aiming for before Christmas).
- Handover at Bremerhaven's Columbus Cruise Centre after moving from Eemshaven, Netherlands. Sails without passengers for Lisbon (Sunday) then the Canary Islands.
- First passengers scheduled to embark Dec. 19 at Tenerife, where Carnival Corp. & plc operates the new LNG-ready cruise terminal. Winter: seven-day itineraries between Gran Canaria, Tenerife, Lanzarote, Fuerteventura and Madeira; summer in the Mediterranean.
- Reasons for delay: the complex propulsion plant, plus a fire aboard during outfitting at Eemshaven, still under investigation ("arson cannot be ruled out").
- Felix Eichhorn, AIDA president: a milestone toward sustainable cruises; further LNG ships due in AIDA's fleet in 2021 and 2023.

wikis.title: The world's first Underground, London Transport Museum
wikis.summary: London Transport Museum gallery page on the Metropolitan Railway, opened in 1863 as the world's first underground railway.
wikis.body:
- Work began in 1860 on the Metropolitan Railway, designed to link three main line termini with the City, built mostly by cut-and-cover construction.
- First section opened from Paddington to Farringdon on 10 January 1863. The District line began operating five years later; the two companies fell out and did not complete the Inner Circle until 1884.
- Steam locomotives created a permanent fug in stations and tunnels. The only surviving 1860s steam engine, Metropolitan number 23 (A class 4-4-0T, 1866), is in the Museum.
- London's population was about 1.7 million when Queen Victoria was crowned in 1837; congestion reached crisis point. The Metropolitan line "is the oldest underground railway in the world"; construction took nearly two years and caused huge street disruption.

wikis.title: Intel unveils Xeon E5-2600 v3 'Grantley' server processors
wikis.summary: eWeek report on Intel's Sept. 8 (2014) launch of the Xeon E5-2600 v3 'Grantley' chips based on Haswell, with DDR4 and up to 18 cores.
wikis.body:
- Intel unveiled the Xeon E5-2600 v3 "Grantley" at a press event in San Francisco on Sept. 8, the day before its annual Intel Developer Forum (IDF) in the same city.
- 22-nanometer chips based on the "Haswell" architecture, with as many as 18 cores and DDR4 memory; the source says up to 36 percent improvement in power efficiency.
- Almost two dozen Grantley processors: 4 to 18 cores, frequencies topping out at 3.5GHz, thermal design power 55 to 145 watts for servers and 160 watts for workstations.
- Server vendors including Dell, Lenovo, Hewlett-Packard and Cisco Systems will use the chips. Intel said in August it was already selling the E5-2600 v3 to cloud and HPC customers.
- The E5 line accounts for more than three-quarters of the server chips Intel sells; Intel holds more than 90 percent of the server chip market.
- Features: Per-Core P-states (each core at its own frequency and voltage, versus the same P-states for all cores on "Romley"/Ivy Bridge), Energy Efficient Turbo Mode, Cache Allocation Monitoring, AVX 2.0 instructions, Integrated Voltage Regulator.
- DDR4 reduces power consumption by 20 to 40 percent with twice the bandwidth of DDR3, per Samsung's J.S. Choi.
- At IDF Intel will announce the Open Network Platform Server reference architecture (SDN/NFV) using the E5-2600 v3, "Fortville" Ethernet Controller XL 710 and QuickAssist Adapter 8950.
- Intel will continue custom processors for particular customers such as eBay (Eoin McConnell).
- Competition: AMD launched 12- and 16-core Opterons earlier in the year and looks to ARM-based Opteron 1100A "Seattle"; ARM SoCs from AMD, Applied Micro, Marvell and Cavium expected to gain momentum into 2015.
- Published Sep 8, 2014 by Jeff Burt; updated Feb 2, 2021.

wikis.title: Microsoft to sell standalone Xbox One Kinect for $150 in October
wikis.summary: GeekWire report that Microsoft will sell a standalone Kinect for Xbox One from Oct. 7, 2014 for $149.99, bundled with Dance Central Spotlight.
wikis.body:
- Microsoft announced (Aug 27, 2014) a standalone Kinect for Xbox One, available starting Oct. 7 for $149.99, which is $50 cheaper than the Kinect for Windows. It comes with the new Dance Central Spotlight game.
- Microsoft began selling the Xbox One without Kinect on June 9 at $399, a $100 cut from the original $499 Xbox One with Kinect; the source says sales doubled in one month. Microsoft also noted increased demand for Xbox One with Kinect.
- Kinect-less bundles starting at $350 will be available later in the year.
- The Xbox One originally cost $100 more than the PlayStation 4; the source says the PS4 has outsold the Xbox One in the U.S. for the past seven months.
- By Taylor Soper, GeekWire.

wikis.summary: GearJunkie sponsored post (March 31, 2016) introducing BioLite's SolarPanel 5+, a thin solar charger with built-in battery and kickstand, priced at $79.95.
wikis.body:
- Sponsored by BioLite. The SolarPanel 5+ is described as thinner and lighter than an iPad: 6.6mm thin, about 14 oz.
- Built-in 2200mAh Li-ion battery; the brand says it can take a phone from 5% to 85% in about 2.5 hours.
- Integrated corner latches attach it to a backpack; battery and charge-strength indicator on the top edge; Maximum Power Point Tracking adjusts to sun strength.
- Price: $79.95.
